Locating the Gender Payment Gap Among Recent Cardiothoracic Surgery Graduates: A Bottom-up Analysis of Medicare Payments
items.abstract: Background Women comprise an increasing proportion of cardiothoracic surgery trainees, yet gender differences in Medicare payments persist. Whether these differences reflect clinical volume or payment for the same service remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 2024 Medicare fee-for-service data for cardiothoracic surgeons graduating from integrated residency or independent fellowship programs between 2013 and 2023. Cardiac and thoracic surgeons were analyzed separately; mixed-practice surgeons were excluded. Mixed-effects models assessed associations between surgeon gender, clinical activity, and standardized payments. Results Among 898 surgeons, women comprised 19% (n=107) of cardiac surgeons and 25% (n=84) of thoracic surgeons. Women received lower mean annual standardized payments than men in cardiac surgery ($79,524 vs $103,940) and thoracic surgery ($52,180 vs $66,474; both p Conclusions Women treated fewer Medicare patients, performed fewer services, billed fewer unique service codes, and received lower annual payments than men. The payment difference was largely attenuated after accounting for clinical activity, while payment for the same service did not differ by gender. These findings locate the Medicare payment difference primarily in clinical volume and breadth of practice rather than service-level reimbursement.

items.title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation
items.abstract: Background Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population. Methods Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization. Results The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference Conclusions For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

items.title: Statewide Trends in Morbidity and Mortality in Octogenarians Undergoing Isolated Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting
items.abstract: Background We sought to determine whether advanced age modifies the association between established preoperative risk factors and 30-day outcomes following isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), compare temporal trends between octogenarians and younger patients, and characterize differences in perioperative outcomes between the two groups. Methods Using the Michigan Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons Quality Collaborative (The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database), we identified 105,445 patients undergoing isolated CABG from 2006-2024. Outcomes and case volumes were assessed across four eras. Operative mortality was evaluated using mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect. Secondary analyses used multiple imputation with hospital-clustered multivariable logistic regression to evaluate age-related effect modification for short-term mortality and morbidity. Results Octogenarians comprised 8.1% of cases (8,563/105,445). Operative mortality was higher in octogenarians (4.8%; n=413) than patients Conclusions In octogenarians, CABG remains associated with higher morbidity and mortality than in younger patients, with minimal changes in 30-day outcomes over the last 20 years. Most traditional risk factors demonstrated similar relative associations across age groups, with age-specific effects in select postoperative domains.

items.title: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Medicaid Expansion and its Effect on Stage at Diagnosis and Surgery Rates in NSCLC
items.abstract: Background Given the uncertain future and potential changes to Medicaid, we sought to evaluate the impact of the 2014 Affordable Care Act Medicaid Expansion on non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) stage at diagnosis and rates of surgery for patients diagnosed with clinical stage I disease. Methods The National Cancer Database was used to identify patients diagnosed with NSCLC between 2004 and 2022, stratified by diagnosis timing (pre- vs post Medicaid expansion) and state expansion status. Demographic, clinical, and treatment variables were compared across time periods and expansion status using chi-square tests (categorical) and t-tests (continuous). Results Among 1,585,967 patients diagnosed with NSCLC, during the study period, 37.9% (n=600,411) were diagnosed pre-expansion and 62.1% (n=982,556) post-expansion (Table 1). A notable shift toward earlier stage of diagnosis was identified in the post-expansion era: only 17.4% (n=85,351) of patients were with cIA NSCLC pre-expansion compared to 27.3% (n=243,434) post-expansion. This shift was additionally more pronounced in expansion states (28.1% [n=135,686] vs 26.2% [n=107,748], p Conclusions Medicaid expansion was associated with increased early-stage NSCLC diagnosis and surgical treatment with larger gains in expansion states, suggesting a direct effect on access and screening. As Medicaid policy evolves, continued advocacy is vital to ensure early detection and adequate care delivery for patients with NSCLC.

items.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Role of Esophagectomy in Stage 4 Esophageal Cancer
items.abstract: Background Nearly 40% of new cases of esophageal cancer are diagnosed at stage 4. Esophagectomy may offer a survival benefit in highly selected patients with stage 4 esophageal cancer. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Databases including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched. Studies reporting survival outcomes in patients with stage 4 esophageal cancer undergoing surgical resection were included. Random-effects models were used to pool 3-year overall survival (OS) and hazard ratios (HRs). Subgroup analyses were performed based on the timing of survival measurement (diagnosis vs. surgery). Results Eleven studies comprising 608 surgical patients were included. The pooled 3-year OS was 43% (95% confidence interval {CI}, 22%-67%) when measured from surgery and 61% (95% CI, 23%-89%) when measured from diagnosis or treatment initiation, with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 >80%). Pooled HR analysis of the 2 comparative studies without gastric cancer showed better survival with surgery, although the difference was not significant (HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.00-6.19]); a sensitivity analysis with the gastric cancer study yielded a similar estimate (HR, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.03-2.02]). Favorable prognostic factors included R0 resection, ypM0 status, lower nodal burden, response to systemic therapy, and oligometastatic disease. Conclusions In highly selected patients with stage IV esophageal cancer, particularly those with oligometastatic disease and favorable response to systemic therapy, esophagectomy may be considered within a multimodal treatment strategy. These findings support a biologically driven, response-adapted approach to conversion surgery. Prospective studies are required to define its role.

items.title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons 2026 Long-term Risk Models for Lung Cancer Resection
items.abstract: Background The Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) has designed and validated risk models to predict long-term survival in patients undergoing lung cancer resection. Methods Adult patients undergoing curative intent lung resection for primary lung cancer in the STS General Thoracic Surgery Database (2015-2023) were included. Vital status was ascertained through linkage to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services inpatient records. The primary endpoint was mortality, truncated at 7 years with >12% remaining at risk. 70% derivation and 30% validation subgroups were utilized. Individualized survival prediction risk scores were derived using separate stratified multivariable Cox proportional hazards models for patients with and without major postoperative complications. Model discrimination was quantified by bootstrap-adjusted Harrel's C-index. Calibration was assessed visually comparing predicted and observed survival curves. Results The study included 112,756 patients across 362 STS participant hospitals, of whom 7.0% experienced a postoperative complication. Median follow-up was 3.9 years (95% CI, 3.8-4.0), during which 28,903 deaths (25.6%) occurred. Adenocarcinoma (66.0%) and stage I disease were most prevalent (68.8%). The optimism-adjusted C-index for the risk models were good for patients with [0.71 (95% CI, 0.70-0.71)] and without major complications [0.72 (0.71-0.73)]. Calibration of the model was excellent overall and in prespecified subgroups in the 30% validation set. Conclusions The STS now offers thoracic surgeons short- and long-term models for self-evaluation, quality improvement, and research. Development of public facing risk calculators will operationalize this novel resource.

items.title: Pharmacological Prevention of Cardiac Surgery-Associated Acute Kidney Injury: Why Trials Failed and a Reimagined Endpoint Framework
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury affects approximately one in four adults and is independently associated with perioperative mortality and progression to chronic kidney disease. Despite more than two decades of randomized pharmacological trials, few have met their primary endpoint. METHODS: This invited narrative review examined 33 pivotal randomized trials of pharmacological prevention published from 2004 to 2026, grouped by mechanism, and related population, intervention timing, and endpoint selection to trial outcome. RESULTS: Trials using short-term creatinine-based kidney injury endpoints produced the positive signals, whereas trials using major adverse kidney events at 90 days as the primary endpoint were negative. This divergence reflects both the low power of that composite for detecting injury prevention and unresolved biology, since no agent has shown benefit on both types of endpoint. Positive trials shared a matched mechanism, a defined population, and an aligned endpoint. Recurrent failure modes were endpoint misalignment, mismatch between population and the timing of injury, confounding by postoperative cardiac recovery, and direct drug effects on creatinine or urine output that mimic or mask injury. CONCLUSIONS: We propose a trial framework with persistent stage 2 or 3 acute kidney disease at 30 days, by Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria, as the primary endpoint; preoperative albuminuria as an enrichment criterion; and attenuation of the postoperative rise in albuminuria at 30 and 90 days as a key secondary endpoint. Platform designs with biomarker-enriched enrollment could convert the next generation of trials into interpretable tests of kidney protection.

items.title: Survival Is Not Necessarily Success: The Fontan Paradox
The Importance of Mentorship in Cardiothoracic Surgery
Who Owns Aortic Follow-Up, and Who Decides When It Ends?
Questioning the necessity of the artificial pancreas
Evolution of Trans-carotid access from an unconventional solution to broad adoption
Beyond Operative Survival: The Critical First Year After Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair
The Effect of implant surface properties on tissue reaction and bar rotation in pectus excavatum surgery
Association of Adult and Pediatric Cardiac Surgery Volumes with Outcomes of the Ross Procedure in Adults
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is growing interest in application of the Ross procedure for treatment of aortic valve disease; however, utilization is restricted to specialized centers. The present study evaluated the differential association of adult aortic valve surgery and pediatric cardiac surgery volumes on outcomes of adults undergoing the Ross operation. METHODS: The 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database was queried to identify all adults undergoing the Ross procedure. Hospitals were categorized as pediatric high-volume centers (pHVC, ≥75th percentile pediatric cardiac surgery volume), adult high-volume centers (aHVC, ≥75th percentile aortic valve replacement/repair volume among non-pHVC), and low-volume centers (LVC). Major adverse events (MAE) were defined as a composite of mortality, stroke, prolonged ventilation, acute renal failure, pulmonary embolism, cardiac arrest, and reoperation. RESULTS: Among 1,212 adults undergoing the Ross operation, 37.7% were treated at pHVC, 56.7% at aHVC, and 5.6% at LVC. National utilization increased from 63 cases in 2016 to 385 in 2022, with the number of performing centers rising from 14 to 37. Patients at LVC experienced the highest rates of MAE (42.1% vs aHVC 8.8% vs pHVC 3.8%, p<0.001). After risk adjustment, care at LVC was associated with a 7.7-fold increase in odds of MAE compared to pHVC (95% CI 3.0-19.7, p<0.001). Outcomes at aHVC and pHVC were comparable, although aHVC had higher rates of reoperation (4.5% vs 0.6%, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Adults undergoing the Ross operation at LVC face worse outcomes compared to aHVC and pHVC. These findings support selective referral strategies and regionalization of care.

items.title: Safety and Feasibility of Single-Port Robotic Lung Cancer Resection: Initial United States Experience of 145 Consecutive Cases
items.abstract: PURPOSE: The da Vinci single-port (SP) robotic system was approved for thoracic surgery in the United States in July 2024. Reports of its application in lung cancer remain limited. We present the initial experience with 145 consecutive SP resections for primary lung cancer at a single institution, with an emphasis on safety and oncologic quality. DESCRIPTION: The SP robotic platform enables lung resection through a single subcostal incision, avoiding intercostal nerve injury. EVALUATION: Three surgeons performed 34 SP lobectomies, 23 segmentectomies, and 88 wedge resections (95% stage I, 5% post-induction) between 6/2025-7/2026. Perioperative outcomes, oncologic quality, and learning curve were analyzed. Median operative time was 113 minutes, estimated blood loss 10mL, and length of stay 2 days. There were 3 conversions. R0 resection occurred in 99.3% of cases. Median lymph node yield was 5 nodes. There were zero mortalities and 4.8% major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥III). Cumulative-sum analysis identified a learning curve plateau after 23 cases. CONCLUSIONS: Subcostal SP robotic lung resection is feasible and safe with acceptable perioperative and oncologic outcomes. Comparative studies are warranted.

items.title: Surgical Timing and Physiology-Specific Outcomes in Congenital Heart Disease
items.abstract: Background In low- and middle-income countries, most children with congenital heart disease reach the operating room after the guideline-recommended window has closed. Existing analyses grade delay by chronological age or a binary early/late split and report outcomes in aggregate, not by physiology. Methods All 12,190 consecutive pediatric congenital heart operations at a single Indian tertiary center (2020-2025) were graded against national guidelines using a lesion-normalized Guideline Deviation Score, from G0 (timely) to G4 (critically delayed). Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines assessed operative mortality, morbidity, and resource utilization overall and within seven pre-specified physiological subgroups. Results Of 10,187 gradable operations, 73.7% were delayed and 34.8% critically delayed. Operative mortality was 2.1% (adjusted OR per grade, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.81-0.96]; P = .004). Fontan-stage palliation was the only subgroup with progressive morbidity increase (64% at guideline age, 85% at grade 3; P = .002), inflecting near age 12 years. Left-to-right shunt lesions showed forward morbidity accumulation (adjusted OR, 1.05 [1.01-1.09]; P = .03). Resource utilization rose with delay overall (adjusted OR, 1.04 [1.01-1.07]; P = .01) and in left-to-right shunt and transposition physiology, but fell in cyanotic and Fontan-stage groups. Conclusions Three in four children missed their guideline window. Operative mortality did not rise with delay, which reflects case-mix confounding rather than evidence that delay is safe, since the youngest and sickest children are operated first. Morbidity rose with delay in Fontan-stage and left-to-right shunt physiology. Physiology-specific grading supports surgical decision-making when a child presents late.

items.title: Impact of Mental Health Disorders on Pulmonary Resection: A Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Medicare Linked Study
items.abstract: Background To determine the prevalence of comorbid mental health disorders (MHDs) and association with stage of diagnosis, extent of resection, and post-operative morbidity/mortality in patients undergoing operative intervention for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods Adults undergoing elective resection of stage I-III NSCLC were identified from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (July 2018-June 2024) and linked to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to determine long-term survival. Primary outcomes were stage at diagnosis, extent of resection, perioperative morbidity, and 5-year survival. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regressions estimated associations between MHDs on each outcome. Risk-adjusted survival was derived using multivariable frailty Cox proportional hazards regression. Results Among 103,263 patients, 24.4% (n=25,163) had ≥1 MHD. Prevalence of MHDs increased from 16.8% in 2018 to 28.0% in 2024 (p Conclusions The prevalence of MHDs among patients undergoing NSCLC resection nearly doubled over 6 years and was associated with an ∼20% increase in morbidity and a reduction in adjusted 5-year survival. These findings underscore the need for targeted perioperative pathways and longitudinal support to mitigate adverse outcomes in this growing population.

items.title: Beyond PaO2: From Donor Assessment to Donor Management in Lung Transplantation
Trends in Outcomes and Regional Rates of Pulmonary Thromboendarterectomy: A National Analysis
items.abstract: Background Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy (PTE) is the guideline-recommended treatment for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). Here, we report modern-era national-level outcomes and identify regions that lack access to PTE. Methods The STS Adult Cardiac Surgery Database was queried from 2012 to 2024 for patients in the USA who underwent PTE with circulatory arrest for chronic disease. Patient characteristics, region, travel distance, area deprivation index (ADI), temporal trends (2012-2018 vs 2019-2024), and center volume (≤15/year vs >15/year) were described and evaluated for association with 30-day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs). Results Over the study period, 4,101 PTEs were performed; 1,238 in 2012-2018 and 2,863 in 2019-2024. Between the two periods, 25 centers closed and 35 centers opened. Higher volume centers (>15 PTE/ year) had significantly lower 30-day post-operative mortality rates compared to lower-volume centers (2.6% vs. 5.5%, p Conclusions The volume-outcome relationship for 30-day mortality after PTE persists over time and there is regional variation in rates of PTE. Development of regional centers of excellence is imperative to ensure access to high-quality CTEPH treatment.

items.title: Two Decades of Single Ventricle Palliation: Survival Improvement and the Persistent Burden of Fontan Morbidity
items.abstract: Background Population-level data on long-term outcomes after single ventricle staged palliation in East Asian cohorts are lacking. We examined era-specific trends in survival, Fontan completion, and morbidity in a Korean nationwide cohort. Methods This retrospective cohort study used Korean National Health Insurance Service claims data (2002-2023). Patients undergoing Stage I palliation were stratified into four calendar-period eras and followed through December 2023. Survival and morbidity were assessed by Cox regression; Fontan completion was analyzed by Fine-Gray competing risk methods and at fixed post-palliation horizons. Results Among 1,732 patients (median follow-up 20.0-199.9 months), adjusted mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.54 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.69) and 0.35 (95% CI, 0.26-0.48) in eras 3 and 4 versus era 1 (both P Conclusions Over two decades, survival after single ventricle palliation improved substantially in Korea, most strikingly in hypoplastic left heart syndrome, whereas Fontan attainment did not improve at a common horizon. The rise in heart failure and thromboembolism, together with higher mortality below the highest socioeconomic stratum, identifies a growing population requiring lifelong surveillance and targeted support.

items.title: Two-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement in Severe Mitral Annular Calcification
items.abstract: Background The SUMMIT-MAC trial is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the Tendyne Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement (TMVR) system in patients with severe mitral annular calcification (MAC). Primary outcomes demonstrated significant improvements in mitral regurgitation severity, heart failure symptoms, and quality-of-life; leading to FDA approval of Tendyne. Intermediate term TMVR outcomes have not been reported. Methods The SUMMIT-MAC cohort (NCT03433274) enrolled high surgical-risk patients with severe MAC (average volume 5,679 ± 5,670; range 741 to 37,437 mm 3 ) and significant mitral valve dysfunction. Independent assessments of mitral disease were performed at an echocardiography core laboratory and adverse events were adjudicated by a clinical events committee. Two-year follow-up visits were achieved in 95% of available patients, with an average follow-up of 18.7 months. Results The cohort included 103 patients from 37 sites. Mean age was 78.0±6.5 years, 55% were women, 74% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mitral regurgitation was present in nearly all patients at baseline (97% grade >2+). At 2 years all-cause mortality was 32.3% (32 patients) and cardiovascular mortality was 23.6% (23 patients). 97% (56/58) of patients with available echocardiograms at 2 years had ≤1+ mitral regurgitation. Additionally, at 2 years, 84% of patients were in NYHA functional class I/II and quality-of-life improved significantly (KCCQ-OS, Δ24.2±19.6 points; p Conclusions In a high-risk cohort of patients with mitral valve disease and severe MAC, Tendyne TMVR had acceptable sustained clinical outcomes and quality-of-life over 2 years. The reduction of mitral regurgitation severity was sustained through 2-years post TMVR.

items.title: Impaired Left Atrial Contractile Strain and Late Pacemaker Implantation After the Cox–Maze Procedure Despite Maintained Sinus Rhythm
items.abstract: Background Late bradyarrhythmia requiring permanent pacemaker implantation remains a challenge after the Cox-Maze procedure. We evaluated whether left atrial contractile strain at 1 year predicts late pacemaker implantation in patients with normal sinus rhythm. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 259 patients who underwent the Maze procedure between 2012 and 2024 and maintained normal sinus rhythm at 1 year. Left atrial contractile strain was assessed using two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. Results Of 329 patients screened, 50 were excluded for atrial fibrillation recurrence at 1 year (1-year freedom from atrial fibrillation, 83.8%). During follow-up (median 58 months), 22 patients required pacemaker implantation. The optimal strain cutoff was -1.8% (area under the curve 0.658), and patients with impaired left atrial function (strain ≥ -1.8%) had a higher incidence of pacemaker implantation (log-rank P Conclusions Impaired left atrial contractile strain 1 year after the Cox-Maze procedure independently predicts late pacemaker implantation despite stable normal sinus rhythm, particularly within the first 5 years, highlighting a dissociation between electrical and functional recovery. It may serve as a surrogate for atrial fibrosis and latent conduction disturbance, warranting intensified surveillance in high-risk patients during this period.

items.title: Multi-arterial Grafting: From Highly Selective to Routine Use in Females and the Elderly - A Statewide Quality Improvement Analysis
items.abstract: Background This study evaluated the impact of the Michigan Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgeons Quality Collaborative initiative to increase multiarterial bypass grafting, focusing on elderly and female patients. Methods Adults undergoing isolated, coronary artery bypass grafting with a left internal thoracic artery and >1 additional graft were included in the analysis (2014-2025). Patients were classified as single-arterial or multiarterial grafting (>2 arterial coronary anastomoses) including bilateral internal thoracic artery or internal thoracic artery with radial artery. Primary outcomes included multiarterial grafting utilization overall and within elderly (≥70 years) and female patients. Secondary outcomes included STS risk-adjusted, recalibrated observed-to-expected ratios for 30-day or operative mortality and major morbidity/mortality. Results Of 51,739 patients, 11,705 (22.6%) underwent multi-arterial grafting of whom 2836 (24.2%) were elderly and 1896 (16.2%) were female. Multiarterial grafting increased over-time (2014:7.5%; 2024: 42.8%, p Conclusions This statewide quality improvement initiative was associated with a safe increase in multiarterial grafting overall, and among the elderly and women; however, disparities persisted in these groups. These findings highlight the need for targeted initiatives to further expand the adoption of multiarterial grafting.

items.title: The Bridge from Surgery to Survival
Analysis of State-Level Disparities in the Supply and Adequacy of Thoracic Surgeons Across the United States
items.abstract: Background Previous studies have highlighted deficiencies in the number of thoracic surgeons practicing in the United States (US). This study analyzed geographic disparities in the supply, demand, and adequacy of thoracic surgeons. Methods This was a microsimulation of thoracic surgeons in the US using the Health Workforce Simulation Model from 2026 to 2038. Supply and demand were defined as the number of full-time equivalent (FTE) thoracic surgeons working and needed, respectively. Adequacy was defined as the ratio of supply over demand. Trends were analyzed with linear regression and comparisons were made with Chi-squared tests. Results From 2026 to 2038, the supply of thoracic surgeons was projected to decrease (4,930 to 4,610 FTEs, 6.5% decrease, P Conclusions Projected shortages exist in thoracic surgery with notable geographic disparities across the US. Future work is needed to develop strategies that increase thoracic surgeon supply in areas with identified deficiencies.

items.title: Mitral Valve Repair Failure: Mechanisms, Re-repair Feasibility, and Outcomes of Reintervention. A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Background Mitral valve repair is the preferred treatment for degenerative mitral regurgitation whenever feasible and durable. Amid the increasing volume of mitral repairs, mitral valve repair failure has emerged as an increasingly recognized clinical entity in contemporary mitral surgery. Methods A systematic literature search was conducted to identify studies reporting intraoperative or interval/postoperatively detected mitral valve repair failure. Evidence synthesis included a systematic summary and analysis of incidence, failure modes, factors favoring re-repair, re-repair techniques and intervention-specific outcomes. Results Intraoperative mitral valve repair failure was reported across nine unique studies totaling 18,429 patients undergoing initial mitral valve repair, of whom 580 (3.1%) experienced intraoperative failure requiring re-cross-clamping. Re-repair was the primary management strategy in intraoperative failure, with a pooled re-repair rate of 82%. Interval mitral valve repair failure was analyzed from 12 studies including 1,363 patients, occurring at a mean of 6 years following the index repair. Disease progression was the most frequent mechanism of interval failure (44%), followed by technical failure (35%) and new disease (17%). In interval failure, valve replacement remained the most employed strategy, while re-repair was performed in 35% of patients. Re-repair was associated with significantly superior long-term survival (78.3% vs. 58.3%; HR 2.44, 95% CI [1.79-3.33], p Conclusions Mitral valve re-repair is a safe and feasible option in selected patients with degenerative mitral valve repair failure and is associated with improved long-term survival. Early technical failures and localized, non-calcified defects with preserved leaflet tissue are most likely to benefit from re-repair.

items.title: Durability of Mitral Repair for Bileaflet Prolapse in Asymptomatic Patients: Par, or Birdie?
Using an Artificial Intelligence ECG-Derived Biological Age for Risk Stratification of Patients Undergoing Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence using a convolutional neural network can estimate patients' age from ECG data. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of AI ECG-derived age in predicting outcomes following surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). Methods Preoperative ECGs obtained within 30 days before surgery were used to calculate AI ECG-derived age in 5,503 patients undergoing SAVR. Age gap was defined as AI ECG-derived age minus chronological age. Associations between age gap and postoperative outcomes were evaluated. A threshold of age gap >5 years was used to define advanced ECG age. Results Median chronological age was 73.2(65.3-79.5) years, and AI ECG-derived age was 70.4(64.6-74.8) years. Median age gap was -3.0(-8.4 to 2.5) years. In 35.7% of patients, AI ECG-derived age exceeded chronological age, and in 16.7% it was >5 years. Patients with advanced ECG age were younger but had higher rates of diabetes, renal failure, and current smoking and had higher BMI. Postoperatively, advanced ECG age was associated with increased risk of 30-day mortality (OR 1.69, p=0.043), blood transfusion (OR 1.44, p Conclusions AI ECG-derived age identifies a subgroup of SAVR patients with advanced physiological aging. An elevated age gap is independently associated with worse early postoperative outcomes and reduced long-term survival following SAVR.

items.title: Successful Implementation of Standardized Longitudinal Follow-up after Surgery for Congenital Heart Disease
items.abstract: Background To understand and improve long-term congenital heart surgery outcomes, longitudinal data are essential but challenging to capture. We evaluated a novel program to facilitate routine longitudinal data collection. Methods Patients undergoing Society of Thoracic Surgeons Benchmark Operations at two centers (2007-2019) were included. Annual follow-up data (vital status and age-specific burden of disease questionnaires) were collected using an automated email system along with medical record and local registry data queries, with coordinator follow-up if needed. Completeness of follow-up and associated factors were analyzed in multivariable logistic regression. Results Of 4,075 subjects, vital status was captured for 98% (median follow-up 6.0 years; IQR 3.1-9.2). Vital status at one year was known for 95%; overall follow-up completeness (observed-to-potential follow-up time) was 81%. At least one follow-up questionnaire was completed by 85%, with 58% utilizing the automated email system. Those with genetic/non-cardiac abnormalities (OR 2.28, 95%CI 1.28-4.28), single ventricle palliation (Norwood OR 11.2, 95%CI 3.01-72.7; Glenn/hemi-Fontan OR 7.79, 95%CI 2.21-49.5), and tetralogy of Fallot repair (OR 2.43, 95%CI 1.11-5.59) had higher odds of known vital status. Follow-up questionnaire completion had higher odds for non-Hispanic white patients (OR 1.54, 95%CI: 1.27-1.86) and higher median income households (OR 1.05/$10,000, 95%CI: 1.01-1.09). Conclusions This program captured vital status and burden of disease, with one-year survival determined for nearly all patients. Automation reduced human resource needs by more than half. Future efforts will focus on expanding to other centers and improving follow-up for disadvantaged groups.

items.title: Large Graft or Large Aorta? Height-Indexed Stent-Graft Diameter After Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair
Fight or Flight: A Multidisciplinary Approach to Diagnosis and Management of Mediastinal Paragangliomas
items.abstract: Background Mediastinal paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors, leading to potentially invasive clinical investigation and inadequate staging. Functional secretory activity, high germline mutation rates, multifocal disease burden, and proximity to the great vessels demand a multidisciplinary approach. We describe our longitudinal multidisciplinary experience building a center of excellence model. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of 19 patients with mediastinal paraganglioma managed at a quaternary referral center, capturing demographics, imaging, preoperative testing, operative details, and perioperative outcomes. Results There were 14 (73.7%) females with a median age of 46.3 years (IQR 38.5-57.6 years). Sixteen (84%) of 19 patients were referred from outside centers; 9 (47.3%) underwent biopsy before referral, with three (15.8%) experiencing catecholamine crisis, pneumothorax, or hemorrhage. Nine (47.4%) tumors were adjacent to the aorta, and seven (42.1%) adjacent to the pulmonary artery, with vascular involvement in 17(89.5%) of the 19 patients. Thirteen (68%) were functional and five (26.3%) had multifocal disease. Succinate dehydrogenase mutations were found in 63.6% of patients tested. Cardiopulmonary bypass was required in 63.2%, with zero 30-day mortality. Postoperative complications occurred in 47.4%, predominantly atrial arrhythmia. Median hospital stay was four days. Four patients developed local recurrence at a median recurrence-free survival of 16.9 months, all with positive margins or multifocal disease. Conclusions Mediastinal paragangliomas can be safely resected within a multidisciplinary center of excellence. Early recognition, avoidance of uninformed biopsy, functional staging, preoperative alpha blockade, and tumor profiling and genetic evaluation with genetic counseling are essential components.

items.title: Structure Preservation Should Guide the Surgical Choice in Double Small Annuli
Standardization, Practicality, and Concomitant Ablation During CABG
The more you look, the more you find: Intraoperative lymph node evaluation in NSCLC
Not Yet a Nail in the Coffin for Ex Vivo Heart Perfusion
Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-Mutation Testing in Patients with Resected Stage IB-IIIB Lung Adenocarcinoma: Are Guidelines Followed?
items.abstract: Background Testing for Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR)-mutations in resected stage IB-IIIB non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer is now standard for all patients, regardless of demographics. Current hospital- and patient-level testing rates and trends are unknown. In this context, we analyze hospital- and patient-level variation in EGFR testing nationally. Methods We used the national cancer database (NCDB) to identify patients with stage IB-IIIB lung adenocarcinoma between 2021-2023 undergoing resection. We used a hierarchical multivariable logistic regression model to create risk- and reliability-adjusted EGFR testing rates across hospitals and compare those across quintiles. We also used a logistic regression model to compare the likelihood of testing based on patient demographics and socioeconomic factors. Results Of 25,124 stage IB-IIIB patients with lung adenocarcinoma undergoing surgery, 14,061 (56.0%) patients at 906 hospitals were tested for EGFR mutations. There was significant variation in testing rates between hospitals (20.8% lowest quintile vs 89.7% highest, p Conclusions Only 1 in 2 patients with stage IB-IIIB lung adenocarcinoma treated surgically are tested for EGFR mutations, with wide variation in care between hospitals and patients. Further quality initiatives are needed to target hospitals and providers and raise awareness to ensure guideline-concordant care.

items.title: Sex, Smoking Status, and Long-Term Outcomes After Lung Cancer Resection: An STS General Thoracic Surgery Database Analysis
items.abstract: Background The incidence of lung cancer in women is increasing, yet the effect of smoking history on survival remains uncertain. Methods Adults who underwent resection for non-small cell lung cancer (2015-2024), from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons database, were grouped by sex and smoking status. Outcomes were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox models. Results In total, 145,103 patients were identified (current or former smoker women: 65,650 [45.2%]; current or former smoker men: 55,912 [38.5%]; never-smoker women: 16,902 [11.7%]; never-smoker men: 6,639 [4.6%]. Median age was 69 years. Never-smoker women were more likely to be Asian, have clinical stage I disease, and have adenocarcinoma; they also had the lowest rates of 30-day mortality and major morbidity. Current or former smoker men had the highest complications rates. These findings persisted after risk adjustment. Longitudinal mortality data were available for 59,756 patients (57%). Five-year survival was 79% for never-smoker women, 70% for never-smoker men, 71% for current or former smoker women, and 58% for current or former smoker men. Risk-adjusted survival was longer in women versus men and in never-smokers versus current or former smokers for both sexes. Compared with never-smoker women, all-cause mortality risk was higher in current or former smoker women (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]=1.18 [95% confidence interval {CI},1.11-1.26]), never-smoker men (aHR=1.44[95% CI,1.30-1.60]), and current or former smoker men (aHR=1.71 [95% CI,1.59-1.84]). Conclusions Never-smoker women had the lowest perioperative risk and superior long-term survival, highlighting sex and smoking status as independent determinants of outcomes after lung cancer resection.

items.title: Post-Transplant Risk Signal Among Left Ventricular Assist Device-Bridged Recipients in the Contemporary Allocation Era
Relationship Between Timing of Surgery and Procedure-Specific Outcomes in Neonates and Infants for Congenital Heart Surgery.
items.abstract: Background Determining the right timing for neonatal heart surgery remains difficult. In a large multicenter cohort, we studied the relationship between birthweight, timing of surgery, and outcomes to identify optimal surgical timing. Methods Using the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Congenital Heart Surgery Database from 2010-2022, we retrospectively reviewed infants who underwent surgery within 90 days of birth. Procedures analyzed included coarctation of aorta (CoA), ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair, atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) repair, tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) repair, Norwood procedure, and arterial switch operation (ASO). Birthweight, prematurity, and genetic syndromes were analyzed as predictors of operative mortality using categorical and continuous models, including nonlinear spline analysis. Patients were divided into five birthweight categories for risk comparison. Results The cohort included 35,315 patients: 26,367(74.7%) neonates and 8,948(25.3%) infants. Low birthweight ( Conclusions Except for Norwood and ASO procedures, weight and timing had limited impact on mortality, supporting individualized surgical decision-making rather than reliance on historical weight thresholds.

items.title: Survival and Aortic Reintervention Following Hemiarch vs. Extended Arch for Acute Type A Dissection in Patients Over Age 65
items.abstract: Background Although ascending hemiarch replacement is considered standard, some have advocated extended arch reconstruction as the preferred strategy in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined. Methods Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-elective hemiarch or extended arch for ATAAD in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services linkage (July 2017-2023,N=3,562;2,442[68.6%] hemiarch;1,120[31.4%] extended arch) were compared. Primary endpoints were long-term mortality and aortic reintervention beyond 30 days and were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence functions, followed by multivariable regressions. Results Hemiarch patients tended to be slightly older (73.8±6.1vs.73.1±5.9 years), female (46.6%vs.39.6%), and hyperacute ATAAD (80.1%vs74.7%). Malperfusion was more frequent in extended arch (27.8% vs 20.6%). Extended arch patients had: i) longer cardiopulmonary bypass, cross-clamp, and circulatory arrest times and ii) more frequent antegrade and/or retrograde cerebral perfusion. Short-term outcomes and rates of concomitant procedures were similar between groups. Risk-adjusted analysis showed no treatment effects for survival, aortic reintervention, operative mortality, and stroke. Conclusions Extended arch for treatment of ATAAD in patients aged ≥65 years was not associated with improved mortality or aortic reintervention compared to hemiarch at intermediate followup. Absent patient-specific indications, hemiarch may be sufficient in patients aged ≥65 years with ATAAD.

items.title: International Expert Consensus Statement on Contemporary Prevention and Management of Postoperative Delirium in Cardiac Surgery
Corrigendum to: Building the Future: A Proposed Framework for Training Residents in Minimally Invasive Cardiac Surgery
Three Decades of Paediatric Heart Transplantation: Long-term Outcomes and the Evolving Role of Mechanical Circulatory Support
items.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the definitive therapy for children with end-stage heart failure, while donor scarcity exposes candidates to deterioration during waiting. Mechanical circulatory support (MCS), particularly ventricular assist devices (VADs), has therefore become an increasingly important bridge to transplantation.1–5 We report the long-term experience of a single high-volume congenital heart centre over more than 3 decades, focusing on temporal changes in paediatric HTx and the evolving role of pretransplant MCS. We retrospectively reviewed 267 patients transplanted at our institution between 1988 and 2024. The cohort was defined by transplantation within the paediatric/congenital programme. Clinical, operative and follow-up data were extracted from institutional records. Overall survival was assessed by Kaplan–Meier analysis. Mechanical circulatory support before HTx was retained as a clinical variable rather than used to define the primary study groups. Mechanical circulatory support included extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and VAD support. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Justus Liebig University Giessen (AZ 94/23; July 27, 2023).

items.title: What Are the Survival Outcomes of Patients Requiring Postcardiotomy Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support?
items.abstract: Postcardiotomy low cardiac output syndrome (PC-LCOS) remains a poorly characterized complication of cardiac surgery, often necessitating temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) with resource utilization and variable outcomes. Evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, derived from retrospective, single-centre studies. Consequently, the prognosis of patients requiring postcardiotomy tMCS remains uncertain, representing a critical concern for clinicians initiating support. In-hospital survival after postcardiotomy tMCS remains ∼40% (range 15%-55%), with varying results based on clinical severity, extent and aetiology of ventricular dysfunction, type and timing of tMCS.1,2 On-support mortality accounts for ∼60% of in-hospital deaths, predominantly occurring within the first 3 days of support and associated with greater preoperative instability, severe postoperative haemometabolic compromise, cardiac arrest, bleeding, and delayed tMCS initiation.1,3 Conversely, post-weaning mortality accounts for ∼40% of deaths and is closely related to complications including re-thoracotomy, bowel ischaemia, acute kidney injury, and septic shock.1,2 Survival according to tMCS duration follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, with the highest values (49%) among patients supported for 4-7 days. Approximately 30% of patients requiring postcardiotomy tMCS remain on support for >7 days, with in-hospital survival falling to 33% and 27% beyond 7 and 10 days, respectively.4 Survival decreases in specific populations, including patients ≥70 years of age (24%-31%), those undergoing aortic surgery (26%-33%), receiving extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (overall: 33%-35%; with favourable neurological outcome: 23%-29%),5 postoperative tMCS (36%), or central cannulation (28%-32%), although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given potential selection bias.1,4 Prophylactic, preoperatively planned tMCS initiation before cardiopulmonary bypass weaning in patients at high risk of PC-LCOS has yielded promising survival rates of up to 96%.3 Despite high early mortality, survivors to discharge have a favourable long-term prognosis, with an estimated 66% 10-year survival.1

items.title: The Standstill in Cardioplegia: Have We Reached the Peak of Myocardial Protection?
David Paul Taggart (1958-2026): In MemoriamSurgeon-scientist, patient advocate, and friend
items.abstract: The death of David Paul Taggart on August 8, 2026, at the age of 68, has deprived cardiovascular surgery of one of its most original, courageous and impactful voices. It has also deprived us both of a longstanding academic partner and friend. David was an outstanding surgeon and clinical investigator, and a relentless advocate for scientific truth who put the interests of the patient above all other considerations. David Taggart was born in Glasgow on July 1, 1958 and grew up in Scotland, with his seven siblings in a close-knit family. He studied medicine at the University of Glasgow, qualifying in 1981. His postgraduate training took him through Glasgow, Paris, Newcastle and London, including the Royal Brompton Hospital, where he trained under Sir Magdi Yacoub and Mr Christopher Lincoln; he often spoke fondly of their mentorship. He received an MD with Honours in 1989 and completed a PhD at the University of Strathclyde in 2000. In 1995 he was appointed Consultant Cardiothoracic Surgeon at Oxford’s John Radcliffe Hospital; in 2004 he became Professor of Cardiovascular Surgery at the University of Oxford. During his long and happy Oxford career, Professor Taggart—often simply called “Prof” by his many students, mentees and colleagues—conducted or participated in more than 20 original studies and clinical trials and authored more than 350 peer-reviewed publications. He served as President of the Society for Cardiothoracic Surgery in Great Britain and Ireland (SCTS) from 2010 to 2012. Although he is best known as a global expert on surgical coronary revascularization, Taggart’s early research revealed a broad intellectual curiosity in numerous areas of cardiac surgical physiology and pathophysiology. He examined hypothermia and the metabolic, endocrine and acute-phase responses to cardiopulmonary bypass and investigated postoperative respiratory dysfunction, attempting to distinguish the contributions of cardiopulmonary bypass from those of bilateral internal thoracic artery harvesting. His PhD thesis explored whether antagonism of platelet-activating factor could ameliorate the myocardial, pulmonary and cerebral consequences of cardiac surgery. Later studies led by Taggart included biochemical assessment of myocardial injury, a randomized investigation of postoperative lung injury and a randomized neuroprotection trial. Even when interventions were not consistently beneficial, Taggart published those negative findings, demonstrating his firm belief in the importance of randomized trials to provide evidence for cardiac surgical procedures. In the middle of his career, Taggart began to focus on advancing the state of the art in coronary bypass surgery. His 2001 systematic review of largely observational data found a substantial survival advantage associated with bilateral rather than single internal mammary artery grafting.1 This prompted him to build a multidisciplinary collaborative team to undertake the difficult task of testing the hypothesis prospectively. The result was the Arterial Revascularisation Trial (ART), which he conceived with the late Douglas Altman, to compare mortality rates between coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) using standard single internal thoracic artery grafts versus bilateral internal thoracic artery grafts in a randomized controlled trial. The grant application for ART to the UK Medical Research Council and British Heart Foundation was successful, and £3.4 million (about 5 million US dollars at the time) was awarded to Taggart, the University of Oxford and the Clinical Trials and Evaluation Unit at Royal Brompton Hospital, London. Between 2004 and 2007, 3102 patients were randomized at 28 cardiac surgery sites in 7 countries to single or bilateral internal thoracic artery CABG surgery with vein grafts. Enrolment into the trial was consistently ahead of schedule which was a tribute to Taggart’s leadership and ability to convene a group of enthusiastic cardiac surgeons to participate in the trial. Clinical follow-up and data analysis have continued through 15 years, during which David partnered closely with Oxford cardiologist Marcus Flather to lead the analytic team. An interim 5-year report,2 the primary outcome report at 10 years3 and the most recent 15-year follow-up report4 were consistent and showed that for the intention-to-treat analysis there was no difference in mortality rates between the two strategies. For the secondary composite outcome of death, myocardial infarction and stroke there was a slight numerical advantage for the bilateral approach, but this was not statistically significant. Interpretation was complicated by important treatment crossovers: approximately 14% of patients assigned to bilateral grafting received only one internal thoracic artery, while approximately 22% assigned to single grafting received a radial artery as a second arterial conduit. David presented the 15-year ART results at the American Association for Thoracic Surgery meeting in May 2026. The intention-to-treat comparison remained neutral, whereas the as-treated analysis again associated actual receipt of multiple arterial grafts with significantly lower mortality. ART is an important trial because observational studies have consistently shown that bilateral internal thoracic artery grafts are associated with lower mortality compared to standard single internal thoracic artery grafts, but these studies are often confounded by unbalanced covariates like age and gender which may introduce bias in spite of statistical adjustments. Taggart was one of the pioneers of multiple arterial graft CABG and many of his operations included bilateral internal thoracic artery grafts carried out using off-pump techniques. He personally enrolled more than 400 patients in ART and his own results demonstrated about 15% proportional mortality reduction with the bilateral approach—an observation that he was proud of even if it did not change the trial’s overall conclusion. Taggart’s body of work included several studies of off-pump CABG. He was an investigator and co-author in the international CORONARY trial,5 the largest randomized comparison of on-pump and off-pump CABG. His subsequent ART sub-analyses clearly demonstrated that off-pump surgery can achieve excellent outcomes, but its success is highly dependent upon operator experience. In ART, low-volume off-pump surgeons performed fewer grafts, converted to cardiopulmonary bypass more frequently and had worse patient outcomes.6 He also investigated methods of improving the performance of saphenous-vein grafts. The VEST programme evaluated whether external stenting could reduce adverse remodelling, lumen irregularity and diffuse intimal hyperplasia. The first randomized study showed reduced intimal hyperplasia area at 1 year, and subsequent multicentre work demonstrated improved FitzGibbon patency classification and reduced intimal thickening at 2 years, although a definitive clinical benefit remained unproven.7 Taggart also brought his evidence-based approach to intraoperative assessment of graft quality, with the prospective, multicentre REQUEST registry, in which protocol-based transit-time flow measurement and high-frequency epicardial and epi-aortic ultrasonography were used in 1016 patients undergoing CABG. Intraoperative assessment prompted a change in the planned operative strategy in 25.2% of patients, including graft revision in 7.8% of patients. This project reflected Taggart’s belief that the technical quality of coronary bypass surgery should be objectively measured and verified rather than presumed at the conclusion of every CABG operation.8 The rise of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in the 1990s and early 2000s saw a corresponding decline in CABG numbers globally. Taggart was very concerned about this, not because he was worried about becoming an “extinct” cardiac surgeon but because he felt that patients were being sold short with incorrect treatment decisions in favour of PCI when treating symptomatic coronary artery disease (CAD). He expressed concerns that cardiac surgeons were being left out of the decision-making process, where the interventional cardiologist would often assess the patient and advise PCI treatment without wider consultation. His efforts, and the efforts of others, led to the concept of the “heart team” approach, whereby patients with advanced or complex CAD would be discussed in a multidisciplinary team meeting with cardiologists, cardiac surgeons and other experts to provide the best treatment strategy. Reports that pooled individual patient data from the randomized trials of PCI vs CABG for symptomatic CAD consistently showed survival advantages for CABG in patients with complex CAD, including diabetes. These results shaped the revascularisation guidelines from the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the European Association of Cardiac and Thoracic Surgeons (EACTS) and undoubtedly allowed patients more appropriate access to CABG. Taggart was a popular speaker on this topic at international meetings, and his command of the relevant data and his fearless ability to push back against the tide of popular opinion was legendary. Taggart’s invited Ferguson Lecture at the Society of Thoracic Surgeons meeting in 2006 bore a title that broadcast his deeply held conviction: “Coronary artery bypass grafting is still the best treatment for multivessel and left main disease, but patients need to know.”9 Taggart was also well known, even notorious in some circles, for his fallout with the EXCEL study group, which conducted a large randomized controlled trial comparing PCI versus CABG in patients with left main CAD. When the 5-year results were being analysed, Taggart pointed out that mortality rates were higher in the PCI group and felt that the manuscript should emphasize the mortality outcome, but was voted down. Taggart also felt that the Universal Definition for perioperative MI should be reported in a sensitivity analysis as prespecified, and that the difference in definition of perioperative MI had effectively tilted the composite primary endpoint in favour of PCI; this was later shown to be mathematically true.10 He ultimately resigned from the EXCEL Steering Committee and took his name off the author list. This became a widely reported issue, with the New England Journal of Medicine requesting clarifications and the BBC launching an independent investigation of the data.11 This episode underscored Taggart’s trademark determination to seek the truth for patients and ensure that information is shared transparently with the scientific and clinical community. The eventual ESC/EACTS reassessment concluded that, among low-surgical-risk patients with left-main anatomy suitable for either treatment, both CABG and PCI were clinically reasonable, while proposing Class I, Level A support for CABG and Class IIa, Level A support for PCI. This controversy did nothing to diminish Taggart’s advocacy for the multidisciplinary Heart Team approach to coronary care. His commitment to ethical partnership between cardiac surgeons and cardiologists was recognized by the leadership of Transcatheter Therapeutics Asia-Pacific (TCTAP) in granting David Taggart the Master of Masters award in 2026, the first time a surgeon has ever received this prestigious award. In 2015, Taggart and Puskas co-founded the International Coronary Congress (ICC), and subsequently the International Society for Coronary Artery Surgery (https://internationalcoronarycongress.com). Now in its 12th year, ICC is the only annual international scientific meeting entirely devoted to advancing the state of the art in surgical coronary revascularization and has been attended by more than 10 000 cumulative delegates from more than 50 countries. From the inaugural meeting in 2015, Taggart delivered numerous lectures at each ICC meeting, engaged in many collegial debates and panel discussions and earned legions of admirers and friends from among his international coronary surgical colleagues. He was especially proud of having co-founded the International Coronary Congress; Taggart was an academic globalist who viewed world-class coronary surgery as something that should be available around the world. Moreover, he was convinced that coronary surgeons in all parts of the world could best advance the state of the art in coronary surgery by working and learning together. Taggart and Puskas created and personally funded the ICC Founders’ Fellowship to help defray the costs of attendance at each annual ICC meeting for young coronary surgical trainees and junior faculty; it has now been renamed the David Taggart Memorial Founders’ Fellowship. Taggart was immediately recognizable at the ICC or any other scientific meeting in his customary Oxford shirt and denim jeans, without a jacket or tie (Figure 1). David Taggart and John Puskas at the Inaugural Meeting of the International Coronary Congress, New York City, 2015. David Taggart was a tireless educator in coronary surgery globally and travelled the world delivering hundreds of invited lectures. He was a generous mentor to dozens of trainees and hundreds of colleagues worldwide. Also with Puskas, Taggart conceived and co-edited the 2021 Oxford University Press textbook entitled “State-of-the-Art Surgical Coronary Revascularization,” the first and only major textbook devoted solely to every nuance of surgical coronary revascularization.12 Taggart had many interests outside of cardiac surgery. He had an encyclopaedic knowledge of contemporary art. He loved sailing in the Mediterranean, snowboarding in the Alps, appreciated a good pub anywhere and possessed a mischievous sense of humour. In June 2026, only weeks before his death, he married Kathleen Hargreaves, his life partner, in an elegant ceremony in the Cotswolds, England. After a Mediterranean honeymoon, Taggart lectured in Asia in July 2026. Typical of David’s self-determination, he continued to live and to work as he saw fit, without breaking stride, despite his terminal illness. David Taggart’s greatest professional legacy is not an operation, conduit, clinical trial or controversy. It is an attitude towards our profession: surgeons must generate evidence rather than merely invoke experience; difficult improvements should not be dismissed because they require advanced training; important negative results deserve publication; and allegiance to institutions, specialties and even professional colleagues must remain subordinate to allegiance to our patients. He was a genuinely honest and honourable professional colleague. He was a tremendously productive academic partner for more than 20 years for each of us and a close friend to us both. We will miss him dearly. Godspeed, David Taggart. None declared. None declared. AI was used to confirm the accuracy of references and dates.

items.title: Coronary Dominance and Variations in Right Ventricular Failure After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
Congenital syphilis requiring VA-ECMO: A case report
items.abstract: Congenital syphilis (CS) is a severe infection with a rising global incidence and potentially life-threatening neonatal outcomes. We present a late preterm infant exhibiting respiratory distress, hepatosplenomegaly, and systemic inflammation. Diagnosed with congenital syphilis at 12 hours of life, targeted antimicrobial was promptly initiated. Despite maximal medical management, her clinical course rapidly deteriorated into refractory shock, severe pulmonary hypertension, and multiple organ dysfunction. This necessitated venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). The infant underwent 7 days of VA-ECMO, 19 days of renal replacement therapy and 23 days of mechanical ventilation before successfully discharging with multidisciplinary follow-up. This case underscores the devastating potential of re-emerging congenital syphilis. It also highlights VA-ECMO as a viable rescue therapy for refractory neonatal shock, emphasizing the critical need for early referral to specialized centers.

items.title: Hemodynamic effects of a novel counter-pulsatile system for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
items.abstract: Background and aims Mortality from heart failure is still high despite all the recent advances. Continuous-flow (CF) Veno-arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) can temporarily maintain systemic and pulmonary hemodynamics, at the cost of overloading the left ventricle (LV). A new Pulsatile Ventricular Assist Platform (pVAP) could offer a more physiological hemodynamic support. Methods 6 large porcine models of acute ischemic left ventricular (LV) failure received the pVAP in a VA-ECMO configuration. Invasive systemic and intraventricular hemodynamic measurements were taken with synchronized counter-pulsatile flow (SCPF) and CF support at the same flow rate. The measurements were compared with no support (ON vs OFF) in both modalities. Results The pVAP successfully delivered VA-ECMO in acute ischemic heart failure. The device maintained stable hemodynamics and increased the forward cardiac output (CO F ) without overloading the LV and with no change in the LV pressure-volume area (PVA). SCPF, but not CF, was associated with improved LV afterload and ventricular-arterial coupling compared to no support. Conclusion The findings suggest that the pVAP is feasible also in a VA-ECMO configuration, supporting hemodynamics with more physiological effect on effect on the LV dynamics.

items.title: Circulatory failure requiring extracorporeal life support in ARDS: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Introduction Venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation is established support for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome with refractory respiratory failure, but some patients also have circulatory failure and receive cardiac or cardiorespiratory extracorporeal life support. Mortality in this group is poorly defined. Methods We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of observed hospital and intensive care unit mortality according to the initial extracorporeal life support configuration, with certainty of evidence assessed using GRADE. Odds ratios are expressed for respiratory support relative to cardiac or cardiorespiratory support, so that a value below 1 indicates lower mortality with respiratory support alone. Results Twelve observational studies contributed data from 5,875 patients. Hospital mortality was lower with respiratory support (9 studies; odds ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval 0.37–0.92; I 2 = 62.5%; 95% prediction interval 0.21–1.60; low-certainty evidence), as was intensive care unit mortality (5 studies; odds ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.23–0.69; very-low-certainty evidence). The cohorts were clinically heterogeneous and rarely adjusted for shock severity, vasoactive support, lactate, cardiac function or general severity scores. Conclusions Because the configuration was selected in response to haemodynamic compromise and may also reflect centre practice, these pooled estimates describe an association and not the effect of an extracorporeal support strategy. Higher observed mortality in patients receiving cardiac or cardiorespiratory support is likely to be explained in large part by greater baseline illness severity and residual confounding.

items.title: Goodbye to randomized controlled trials on mechanical circulatory support
Perioperative outcomes after total coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT): A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background Total coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT) is a sternum-sparing approach to multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Published evidence is predominantly observational. This review summarizes reported perioperative outcomes after TCRAT; its principal quantitative synthesis is single-arm and does not establish comparative effectiveness against conventional CABG. Methods This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidance and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437661). PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to May 1, 2026. Studies reporting perioperative or clinical outcomes in adults undergoing TCRAT were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and the JBI checklist for case series. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions used the Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation; continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Results Seven cohorts comprising a reported total of 1869 patients were included. The pooled in-hospital/short-term mortality estimate was 0.92% (95% CI, 0.28–1.83%; I 2 = 48.8%), and the pooled stroke estimate was 0.76% (95% CI, 0.10–1.82%; I 2 = 61.6%). Pooled incidences of postoperative atrial fibrillation and re-exploration were 11.53% and 3.44%, respectively; deep wound infection was uncommon (0.15%). Pooled mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 146.17 and 78.05 minutes. Estimates for operative times and length of stay were highly heterogeneous. The exploratory diabetes-stratified analysis did not detect a statistically significant mortality difference ( p = 0.8443). Conclusion The available cohorts describe the perioperative outcomes reported after TCRAT in selected patients and centers. These single-arm pooled estimates should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence, superiority, or non-inferiority compared with conventional CABG. Larger, well-adjusted comparative studies with standardized outcomes and long-term follow-up are needed.

items.title: Apparent membrane lung dysfunction during veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation following methylene blue administration: Case report
items.abstract: We report the case of a 72-year-old man who underwent cardiac surgery for Group B Streptococcus infective endocarditis with embolic hepatic abscesses. Severe postoperative vasoplegia was treated with repeated methylene blue boluses and infusions while on central veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-A ECMO) for refractory cardiogenic and vasoplegic shock. Following multiple methylene blue administrations, the ECMO return tubing appeared dark, raising concern for membrane lung dysfunction (MLD). However, post-membrane lung blood gases confirmed adequate oxygen exchange and visual inspection on the post-membrane lung side of the circuit revealed bright red blood within the membrane lung (ML) and all rigid connectors. The discoloration was determined to have resulted from methylene blue staining of the flexible PVC tubing which mimicked the appearance of the post-ML flexible PVC tubing in a failed membrane lung despite the oxygenator functioning appropriately. Awareness of this artifact is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions; evaluation of post-ML blood gases and visual comparison with unstained ECMO circuit components can distinguish this benign finding from true MLD.

items.title: Impact of dynamic pump speed adjustment versus constant speed in left ventricle assist device patients on exercise performance: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background Adjusting pump speed in patients with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) during exercise may improve hemodynamics and enhance functional capacity in advanced heart failure, but its clinical benefit over fixed-speed operation remains uncertain. We evaluated whether dynamic, exercise-driven LVAD speed modulation improves physical performance compared to fixed-speed settings. Methods and results PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing dynamic adjustment versus fixed pump speed control during exercise in patients with LVADs. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mean differences (MD), and binary outcomes using risk ratios (RR), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical analysis was performed using R (version 4.3.1). Eight studies were included, with study sample sizes totaling 124 participants; seven used crossover designs and one used a non-randomized repeated-measures design. Potential overlap between two reports from Jung et al. precluded interpretation of this total as the number of unique participants. Dynamic pump-speed modulation was associated with higher peak oxygen uptake (VO 2 ) (MD 1.07 mL/kg/min; 95% CI 0.73 to 1.41; p < 0.001; I 2 = 42%) and LVAD pump flow at peak/end of exercise (MD 1.24 L/min; 95% CI 0.68 to 1.79; p < 0.001; I 2 = 89%). No differences were observed in peak cardiac output (MD 0.12 L/min; 95% CI −0.74 to 0.98; p = 0.786; I 2 = 67%) or ventilatory efficiency, assessed by the VE/VCO 2 slope (MD −1.58; 95% CI −3.25 to 0.09; p = 0.063; I 2 = 76%). Conclusion Dynamic LVAD speed adjustment may improve exercise capacity, as suggested by higher peak VO 2 , although peak cardiac output and ventilatory efficiency showed no clear improvement. Given the small studies, heterogeneous protocols and possible participant overlap, it remains uncertain whether this apparent benefit is sustained or clinically meaningful to patients.

items.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation (AR) at high surgical risk, guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is often the only available option. Transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for aortic stenosis and has also been evaluated in patients with pure AR. However, no adequately powered randomized trial has compared TAVR with GDMT alone in this population. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, open-label trial in China. Patients with severe pure AR for whom surgery was considered difficult or unacceptable by the local heart team or who persistently declined surgery were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow system plus GDMT or GDMT alone. The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year. RESULTS: We assigned 210 patients with severe pure AR to the TAVR group (n=109) or GDMT group (n=101) at 18 centers. At 1-year follow-up, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the primary end point was significantly lower in the TAVR group than in the GDMT group (8.3% vs 24.8%; hazard ration [HR], 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14–0.66]; P =0.001), driven primarily by a reduction in heart failure rehospitalization (3.7% vs 21.3%; HR, 0.16 [95% CI, 0.06–0.47]; P < 0.001). TAVR was associated with higher rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation, most of which occurred within 30 days after the procedure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe pure AR, TAVR plus GDMT significantly reduced the rate of all-cause death, disabling stroke, or heart failure rehospitalization at 1 year compared with GDMT alone despite higher 30-day rates of major or life-threatening bleeding and new permanent pacemaker implantation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT04864145

items.title: Validation of the PREVENT-HF Risk Prediction Equation in US Veterans
items.abstract: One in four adults in the United States will receive a diagnosis of heart failure (HF) in their lifetime (1), highlighting an urgent need for expanded prevention.Accurate prediction of HF risk is critical to prioritize high-risk individuals for targeted intervention.The American Heart Association's PREVENT-HF equation is a novel HF risk prediction tool (2).However, it is unclear how well this model generalizes outside of its development cohort.This is important for populations with disproportionately high risk of HF, such as US Veterans (3).Prior validation in this population has focused on other endpoints (e.g., atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease [ASCVD]) and limited outcome ascertainment to Veterans Health Administration (VHA) data, which didn't capture diagnoses from Medicare or VHA-paid community care claims (4).To address this gap, we validated PREVENT-HF in US Veterans.

items.title: Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples
items.abstract: Background: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment. Methods: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF. Results: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040). Conclusions: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

items.abstract: coronary heart disease ◼ ezetimibe ◼ hypolipidemic agents ◼ low-density lipoprotein ◼ statins W hile the breadth of Dr Eugene Braunwald's contributions to cardiology is staggering, few lines of inquiry rival the relentless perseverance with which he pushed forward the field of lipid lowering in what he termed "the race to the bottom." 1 Dr Braunwald described his first exposure to the lipid hypothesis of atherogenesis in the 1950s while at the National Heart Institute (now the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute), through interactions with a biochemist and future Nobel Laureate, Christian B. Anfinsen. 1 Dr Braunwald noted that while the lipid hypothesis had not yet gained widespread acceptance, these interactions left him convinced of the validity of the hypothesis and, consequently, the role for treatment of hyperlipidemia in patients with atherosclerosis.At the time, Dr Braunwald's research efforts continued to focus on reducing myocardial infarct size, but he resolved to revisit treatment of hyperlipidemia in the future when better therapies became available.

Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months.
