items.title: Iliohypogastric and Ilioinguinal Nerve Block for Awake ECPella Cannulation in Pediatric Patients With Nonpostcardiotomy Cardiogenic Shock
items.abstract: In pediatric cardiogenic shock, endotracheal intubation may carry a high risk of cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction. This single-center retrospective case series (2020–2025) evaluated the feasibility, safety, and outcomes of ultrasound (US)-guided ilioinguinal–iliohypogastric (IhIG) nerve blocks (0.05–0.1 ml/kg of 0.25% ropivacaine) under light sedation to facilitate awake venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella (ECPella) surgical cannulation. Five adolescents (median age: 13 years, range: 7–17; median weight: 45 kg, range: 21–58) with nonpostcardiotomy cardiogenic shock underwent successful IhIG block placement in the pediatric intensive care unit by anesthesia-trained intensivists, followed by surgical cannulation in the catheterization laboratory. Intubation and mechanical ventilation were avoided during initial cannulation and throughout ECPella duration. Three patients required a modified chimney Y-graft for cannula placement, and two experienced local surgical bleeding. All five patients survived to hospital discharge, with three achieving direct biventricular recovery. Based on these preliminary data, US-guided IhIG nerve block seems a feasible and safe strategy for awake ECPella cannulation in selected pediatric patients, successfully avoiding high-risk invasive ventilation and general anesthesia.

items.title: Impact of Showering Methods on Driveline Exit Site Microbiology and Driveline Infection in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices
items.abstract: Driveline infection (DLI) remains a major complication in patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). This study evaluated the impact of different showering methods on bacterial colonization at the driveline exit site (DLES) and the incidence of DLI. Patients who underwent LVAD implantation at our institute from 2008 to 2021 were included and classified into two groups: the open group, in which the DLES was exposed and washed with running water, and the covered group, in which the DLES was sealed with a waterproof dressing during showering. The primary outcome was the incidence of DLI within 3 years following hospital discharge. A total of 103 patients were included (the open group, n = 47; the covered group, n = 56). The DLI-free rate was significantly higher in the covered group than the open group (77% vs. 49%; p = 0.003). Pseudomonas aeruginosa was detected less frequently at the DLES, and DLI caused by P. aeruginosa was significantly reduced in the covered group. Multivariate analysis suggested that the open showering method was an independent risk factor for DLI (hazard ratio, 2.816; 95% confidence interval, 1.325–5.984; p = 0.007). The covered showering method was associated with a significantly lower incidence of DLI, particularly infections caused by P. aeruginosa .

items.title: Outcomes and Complications of Axillary Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support: A Single-Center Experience
items.abstract: Axillary intra-aortic balloon pump (axi-IABP) support has emerged as an alternative to femoral access for patients with advanced heart failure, offering improved mobility and potential benefits in pretransplant conditioning; however, data on associated complications remain limited. We conducted a retrospective study of 55 patients who underwent axi-IABP placement between January 2019 and July 2025 at our institution. The cohort had a median age of 59 (interquartile range [IQR], 52–65) years and presented with cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS). Axi-IABP successfully bridged 87.3% of patients to advanced therapies. A total of 83 complications were identified in 60.0% of patients, most commonly malposition in 23.6% of patients, gas leak alarms in 16.4% of patients, and kinking in 16.4% of patients. Serious vascular complications were infrequent. The median time to first complication was 10.5 (IQR, 2.75–25.5) days. Female sex was associated with a higher hazard of first complication when controlled for height (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 2.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.04–7.27; p = 0.041). In conclusion, axi-IABP is an effective bridging strategy that enhances patient mobility but is associated with a high rate of device-related complications, predominantly mechanical in nature, underscoring the importance of careful patient selection and monitoring.

items.title: Levosimendan and Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Weaning: Still an Open Question?
Beyond VA-ECMO Cannulation: Socioeconomic Disparities and Pathways to Definitive Therapy
Response to the Letter to the Editor: Beyond VA-ECMO Cannulation: Socioeconomic Disparities and Pathways to Definitive Therapy
Renal Decline Before Heart Transplantation in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Recipients: United Network for Organ Sharing Analysis
items.abstract: Although baseline renal impairment and post-heart transplantation (HT) dialysis are established clinical predictors, the prognostic impact of pre-HT renal decline in patients bridged with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) remains unclear. We retrospectively analyzed patients from the United Network for Organ Sharing registry who underwent HT following LVAD support between 2009 and 2024. Renal decline was defined as a greater than or equal to 40% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from listing to HT. Among 10,454 patients, 624 (6.0%) experienced pre-HT renal decline. Patients with renal decline had longer waitlist durations (median 297 vs. 197 days; p < 0.001), lower eGFR at HT (42.0 vs. 70.6 ml/min/1.73 m 2 ; p < 0.001), and higher rates of post-HT dialysis (23.7 vs. 12.8%; p < 0.001). Independent predictors of renal decline included longer waitlist time and perioperative blood transfusions, whereas HeartMate 3 LVAD use was protective. Renal decline was independently associated with an increased risk of post-HT dialysis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.64) and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 1.16), with post-HT dialysis strongly predicting mortality (aHR: 3.48). Renal deterioration is a significant predictor of post-HT dialysis and mortality in LVAD-bridged patients. Incorporating renal trajectory into risk stratification may enhance candidate selection and promote perioperative renal protection strategies.

items.title: Cardiac Output From Right Ventricular Pressure: Not the Solution for Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
items.abstract: Cardiac output (CO) monitoring is challenging during venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV ECMO), as thermodilution techniques are unreliable. Cardiac output from right ventricular pressure (RVP) waveforms has recently been considered. We evaluated whether RVP-derived CO (CO RV ) accurately reflects cardiac output measured by echocardiography (CO US ) during VV ECMO. Ten anesthetized pigs underwent femoro-jugular VV ECMO implantation. A Swan-Ganz IQ catheter provided continuous CO RV monitoring throughout the experiment. Cardiac output was modulated using either dobutamine (5–20 µg/kg/min) or landiolol (10–40 µg/kg/min) infusions. Agreement between CO RV and CO US was assessed using Pearson correlation and Bland–Altman analysis. Overall, 596 paired CO measurements were performed in seven animals. Cardiac output ranged from 1.05 to 9.46 L/min. Correlation between CO RV and CO US was poor ( R = 0.24; R 2 = 0.057; p < 0.05). Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of +1.94 L/min with wide limits of agreement (−1.44 to +5.32 L/min). Correlations between individual right ventricular pressure waveform components and CO US were heterogeneous and weak to moderate (diastolic RVP, R = 0.36; right ventricle +d P /d t [delta pressure/delta time] R = 0.40; systolic RVP R = 0.60). CO RV is not reliable during VV ECMO in our experiment. Further studies are needed to assess CO RV performances.

items.title: Current Global Trends and Challenges of Pediatric Ventricular Assist Device Programs: An ACTION Collaborative Survey
items.abstract: Ventricular assist devices (VADs) have become an established therapy for children with end-stage heart failure, yet multinational data describing pediatric VAD programs remain limited. We conducted a 12 question survey through the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) involving 74 international healthcare professionals from pediatric VAD programs outside North America. The survey assessed device and resource availability, multidisciplinary team composition, program challenges, and future priorities. Fifteen responses representing 15 centers from 14 countries were received, including 13 centers with established pediatric VAD programs. Most centers (91%, 10/11) managed 1–5 pediatric VAD patients annually. Berlin Heart EXCOR and HeartMate 3 were available in 85% (11/13) of centers, while only 46.7% (7/15) had a dedicated VAD coordinator. Major barriers included inadequate education for intensive care unit (ICU) and nursing staff and patients (69%, 9/13), financial constraints (54%, 7/13), limited device availability (46%, 6/13), and lack of outpatient VAD experience, with 31% (4/13) of centers reporting no experience discharging patients on VAD support. Substantial variation in device availability, multidisciplinary resources, and program experience exists across regions. These findings highlight important gaps in pediatric VAD care and support international collaboration to improve education, infrastructure, and access to advanced heart failure therapies.

items.title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device–Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight
items.abstract: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24–48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in LVAD recipients may enable prompt recognition and timely intervention.

items.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Patients With Pulmonary Hemorrhage
items.abstract: Severe pulmonary hemorrhage may lead to refractory hypoxemia and/or hemodynamic collapse and cause high mortality. However, the use of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in this patient population is rare. The aim of this study is to better define and understand this patient population by exploring the baseline characteristics, complications, and outcomes of patients who receive ECMO support due to pulmonary hemorrhage, based on data extracted from the extracorporeal life support organization (ELSO) registry. Between 2003 and 2023, 96 patients received ECMO due to pulmonary hemorrhage. Complications occurred in 54% of the patients, mainly acute kidney injury (AKI) with need for renal replacement therapy (RRT; 28%) and bleeding (pulmonary, gastrointestinal) (15%). Respiratory infections occurred in 37.1% of the patients. The most common diagnostic/therapeutic procedures were computed tomography scans in 9%, bronchoscopy in 41%, surgery in 8%, and apheresis in 6% of the patients. Interventional radiology procedures were performed in only 2% of the patients. Interpretation of these data should be performed cautiously, as underreporting is a known limitation of the ELSO Registry. Forty-seven patients (49%) were weaned from ECMO, and 46 (48%) survived until discharge. Survival and complication rates are comparable to the overall ECMO cohort in the ELSO Registry, which makes ECMO a feasible strategy in this patient population.

items.title: Learning to Live With a Ventricular Assist Device: Patient, Caregiver, and Clinician Concerns Following Implantation and Hospital Discharge
items.abstract: Patients undergoing ventricular assist device (VAD) implantation and their caregivers must attain knowledge and skills to perform VAD self-care safely. Little is known about the similarities and differences among patients, caregivers, and VAD clinicians related to VAD self-care training and management. This study explored the perspectives of 15 VAD patients, 12 VAD caregivers, and 18 VAD clinicians through individual semi-structured interviews focused on understanding barriers related to VAD self-care training and concerns about VAD self-care post-discharge. We identified four major themes (training related, care transitions, fear and uncertainty, clinical consequences). All participant groups discussed concerns related to daily VAD self-care and the transition home after implantation. Caregivers and clinicians discussed the steep VAD self-care learning curve. Caregivers and patients discussed fears in general ( eg , constant fear) and specific terms ( eg , VAD malfunction), whereas clinicians who discussed fear/uncertainty identified strategies for dealing with emergent situations. Concerns regarding adverse events and non-adherence arose primarily from clinicians. Although some alignment was found, concerns varied among stakeholders. A common understanding of these nuanced concerns may improve VAD self-care training and the preparation of patients and caregivers.

items.title: External Validation of a Risk Score Assessment for Pediatric Ventricular Assist Device Mortality
items.abstract: The ACTION score was internally validated to predict mortality after pediatric ventricular assist device (VAD) placement. This study aims to externally validate the ACTION score and compare its performance to the INTERMACS profile for prediction of mortality in pediatric VAD candidates. The publicly available Pedimacs dataset (531 patients) was used for external validation. The Pedimacs dataset as well as a contemporary ACTION dataset (1,304 patients) were used to compare the performance of the ACTION score and INTERMACS profile. A statistically significant linear trend in the proportion of death across increasing ACTION scores ( p < 0.0001) was observed in the Pedimacs dataset, with a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve demonstrating an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71. Both the ACTION score and the INTERMACS profile demonstrated a significant linear trend in the proportion of death across scores in the ACTION dataset. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.71 and 0.58 for the ACTION score and INTERMACS profile, respectively. The ACTION score is externally validated with the Pedimacs dataset and is a fair predictor of mortality. The ACTION score performed better than the INTERMACS profile in predicting mortality using both historical Pedimacs data and contemporary ACTION data.

items.title: Serologic Guidance for Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Selection and Survival Using the Cosmos Dataset
items.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a life-support therapy for patients with severe cardiac or respiratory failure. Despite its growing use, evidence-based guidelines for ECMO candidacy remain limited due to small, single-center studies and heterogeneous designs. This study leveraged Epic Cosmos, an electronic health record dataset encompassing over 300 million patient records, to analyze outcomes among 42,210 adults treated with ECMO between January 1, 2019, and February 15, 2026, involving 23,116 (54.8%) venoarterial (VA), 14,632 (34.7%) venovenous (VV), and 4,462 (10.6%) hybrid (VA and VV) cases. Hospital mortality varied from 37% (VV) to 50% (VA). Poisson models by ECMO type for in-hospital mortality adjusted for key demographic and clinical variables showed the admitting diagnosis group had the strongest association with subsequent mortality. Several blood chemistry markers measured within the 24 hours before ECMO initiation were also associated with increased mortality, including elevated lactate, elevated creatinine, and lower pH, though strength of association varied by ECMO type. Our findings support the use of large electronic health record (EHR) datasets for ECMO outcomes research and identify exploratory associations between preinitiation biomarkers and in-hospital mortality that require further validation.

items.title: Left Ventricular Unloading With Self-Expanding Pump During Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Acute Myocardial Infarction
items.abstract: Increased left ventricular (LV) afterload and distension during venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support may impede myocardial perfusion in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Active LV unloading has been associated with improved outcomes. We report the first clinical use of a self-expanding percutaneous ventricular assist device (NyokAssist; magAssist, Suzhou, China) for LV unloading during VA-ECMO in a 56 year old man with AMI-related cardiogenic shock (CS). Successful coronary angiography and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of the culprit left circumflex (LCx) lesion were performed with NyokAssist + VA-ECMO support. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO on post-procedure day 5 and remained on NyokAssist support alone for an additional 7 days before being transferred on VA-ECMO to a heart transplant center for consideration of advanced heart failure therapies due to limited myocardial recovery. No device-related complications were observed. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of early implementation of a combined VA-ECMO and NyokAssist support strategy, enabling LV unloading, temporary hemodynamic stabilization, end-organ improvement, and VA-ECMO decannulation in a patient with AMI-related CS. As this report describes a single-patient experience, further clinical studies are warranted to define the safety, efficacy, and potential role of the use of NyokAssist in combination with VA-ECMO in the management of AMI-related CS.

items.title: Preoperative Six-Minute Walk Distance Predicts Mortality After Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
items.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification remains a challenge in advanced heart failure before durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. We assessed whether preoperative six-minute walk distance (6MWD) was associated with all-cause mortality and compared its discrimination with peak oxygen uptake (pVO 2 ). In this retrospective single-center cohort (January 2016–May 2025), 136 of 206 implanted patients had an eligible preoperative 6MWD. Deaths through May 29, 2026, were ascertained from recorded death dates. During follow-up, 85 patients died; median observed follow-up was 871.5 days. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.712 for 6MWD (n = 136) and 0.639 for pVO 2 (n = 127); paired comparison in 127 patients showed no significant difference (DeLong p = 0.212). Each 50 m increase in 6MWD was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.88, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79–0.98). Patients walking less than 350 m had worse survival (log-rank p = 0.002; HR: 1.98, 95% CI: 1.27–3.11). The association persisted after adjustment for age, INTERMACS profile, and device type (HR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.27–3.54). Preoperative 6MWD may contribute to risk stratification before durable LVAD implantation; the threshold requires external validation.

items.title: Ventricular Assist Devices Effectively Bridge Pediatric Patients to Heart Retransplantation: An ACTION Registry Study
items.abstract: The use of ventricular assist devices (VAD) in pediatric patients as a bridge to heart transplantation has increased over the past two decades. However, the use of VAD to bridge pediatric transplant recipients to retransplantation is rare and under-studied. We performed a retrospective study using the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) registry to evaluate patient characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients bridged to retransplant with VAD. A total of 24 patients were identified and supported for a median duration of 64 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 15.0–101.25). Of these, 54% (n = 13) were implanted as a bridge to retransplant candidacy (BTC) and 46% (n = 11) as a bridge to retransplant (BTT). We found a high prevalence of major adverse events, including infection in 75% (n = 18), bleeding in 42% (n = 10), renal dysfunction requiring dialysis in 33% (n = 8), and stroke in 8% (n = 2). Despite this, 71% (n = 17) survived to retransplant, with an 88% 1 year survival following retransplant. Device mortality was higher in BTC compared to BTT (46% vs . 9%; p = 0.046). Our study is the first multicenter study evaluating the use of VAD as a BTT. We exhibit a high prevalence of adverse events on VAD, but a favorable waitlist and post-retransplant survival.

items.title: ASAIO 2026 Annual Conference Summary
Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
items.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children’s hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The primary outcome was pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) mortality. Among 73 patients (non-ECPR, n = 58; ECPR, n = 15), ECPR was associated with increased mortality in unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR], 5.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.47–18.53; p = 0.010). After adjustment for pre-ECMO physiologic variables, the association between ECPR and mortality was no longer significant (adjusted OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 0.37–8.08; p = 0.483). Lower pre-ECMO arterial pH remained associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR, 1.87 per 0.1 decrease; 95% CI, 1.20–2.92; p = 0.006). In a sensitivity analysis, underlying cardiac disease was associated with lower mortality than noncardiac disease (adjusted OR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.07–0.79; p = 0.020). These findings highlight the associations of pre-ECMO physiologic status and underlying disease category with PICU mortality.

items.title: Precannulation Risk Factors Associated With Hemorrhagic Events During Respiratory Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Children: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
items.abstract: Hemorrhagic complications are frequent and clinically significant during pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet associated precannulation factors remain poorly defined. We evaluated these factors in a multicenter retrospective cohort of children receiving respiratory ECMO at four Colombian centers during 2018–2022. A total of 106 children were included; 53 (50.0%) developed at least one hemorrhagic complication during ECMO support, and 83% of events occurred within the first 7 days after cannulation. Cannulation-site bleeding was most frequent (41.5%), followed by intracranial hemorrhage (22.6%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (17.0%). In bias-reduced adjusted analyses, higher precannulation lactate concentrations, lower bicarbonate levels, previous severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, adenovirus infection at admission, and longer mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support before ECMO remained associated with bleeding. Patients who developed hemorrhagic complications had higher 28 day mortality than those without bleeding (39.6% vs . 13.2%; p = 0.002). When bleeding was modeled as a time-dependent exposure, hemorrhagic events were associated with a higher subsequent hazard of 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 4.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.09–11.64). Hemorrhagic complications affected half of children receiving respiratory ECMO, occurred predominantly during the first week, and were associated with increased mortality. Several precannulation characteristics remained associated with bleeding in bias-reduced adjusted analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

items.title: Interpreting Hemodynamic Superiority of Direct Cardiac Compression: The Importance of Experimental Independence and Biventricular Balance
Development and Validation of a Reproducible Cross-Species Liver Machine Perfusion Platform in Rats and Mice
items.abstract: Ex vivo liver machine perfusion is increasingly used for graft assessment and reconditioning, but reproducible small-animal platforms remain limited. We developed a modular rat-mouse liver machine perfusion platform built around a shared extracorporeal circuit backbone with interchangeable cannulation interfaces, continuous inflow pressure monitoring, and a compact dry thermal-bead bath supporting benchtop subnormothermic and normothermic studies as well as cold-room hypothermic deployment. Performance was assessed by methylene blue perfusion mapping with pixel-based quantification and by blinded Suzuki histologic injury scoring. In mice, the portal cannulation site within the superior mesenteric vein-portal segment determined the completeness of whole-organ perfusion; positioning the cannula distal to the gastric/splenic/pancreatic tributary and proximal to the inferior pancreaticoduodenal vein ensured homogeneous lobar perfusion. In rats, single portal inflow left peripheral lobar regions relatively underperfused, whereas dual portal venous plus hepatic arterial inflow produced the most uniform perfusion (perfused surface area 58–75% vs. 100%). Histology showed preserved architecture on liver biopsies, with total Suzuki scores of 0–1 of 12 across procurement baseline, immediate perfusion, and cold storage plus reperfusion groups. Reproducible whole-organ perfusion demonstrated depends on species-specific vascular access. The current platform was validated for perfusion adequacy and short-term structural preservation; metabolically sustained support and functional viability remain to be demonstrated.

items.title: Automated Blood Conditioning for Artificial Lung Evaluation: A Feasibility Study
items.abstract: Artificial organs and Extracorporeal Life Support (ECLS) systems require extensive in vitro evaluation before in vivo preclinical and human trials are conducted. Current methodologies require large volumes of blood, extensive manual labor, and lengthy conditioning periods. To remedy these shortcomings, an “Automated Blood Conditioning (ABC) platform” was developed. Automated blood conditioning is a closed-loop perfusion circuit, control algorithm, and protocol that rapidly conditions and continuously maintains blood conditions for artificial lung and ECLS system evaluation, permitting efficient testing of ECLS devices with minimal blood volume, and showing potential for long-term use. The platform includes a hemoconcentrator, Terumo CDI 500 blood parameter monitor (CDI 500), custom gas mixer, and computer-based controller. A proportional-integral-derivative (PID) algorithm automatically adjusts sweep gas concentrations to maintain target inlet blood conditions despite disturbances from the test device. From arterial conditions, oxygen saturation (sO 2 %) settles at the venous target of 65% in approximately 5 minutes, and partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO 2 ) at 45 mm Hg in approximately 6 minutes. In this feasibility study, four independent runs on separate blood batches (48.5 hours) held sO 2 % within ±5% of target for 99.2% of steady-state samples (error 1.2%); the primary evaluation run maintained physiologic conditions for its first 10 closed-loop hours, and device flows up to 0.6 L/min using 1.1 L of blood.

items.title: Reply to Letter to the Editor: Interpreting Hemodynamic Superiority of Direct Cardiac Compression
Exercise Right Atrial Stiffness From Pressure-Volume Loops and Prognosis in Pulmonary Hypertension
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In pulmonary hypertension (PH), risk assessment focuses on right ventricular function and may overlook exercise-related right atrial (RA) functional limitation. We investigated whether RA stiffness during exercise reflects impaired right-heart filling reserve and is associated with prognosis beyond conventional measures. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 68 participants in this observational study, including 42 with precapillary PH. Participants who had PH ruled out and patients with postcapillary PH formed reference groups. Participants underwent 3-dimensional echocardiography, right heart catheterization, and invasive RA pressure-volume loop analysis at rest and during standardized semisupine exercise. RA filling stiffness was derived from the reservoir phase. Patients with precapillary PH were stratified by median exercise RA filling stiffness. RESULTS: At rest, high- and low-stiffness groups had comparable right ventricular function, afterload, and cardiac index, but the high-stiffness group exhibited impaired phasic RA strain and venous congestion (median [interquartile range] liver stiffness, 7.1 [6.0–8.8] versus 5.2 [4.8–5.8] kPa; P =0.021). During exercise, mean RA pressure increased similarly, but the high-stiffness group had impaired peak cardiac index (3.3±1.0 versus 4.1±0.9 L/min per m 2 ; P =0.015) and RA strain. Unlike resting RA stiffness, high exercise RA stiffness was independently associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 4.37 [95% CI, 1.20–15.96]). A model including RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve discriminated high RA stiffness (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.90). CONCLUSIONS: RA stiffness during exercise integrates resting congestion with limited cardiac reserve and unmasks mortality risk missed by resting metrics. RA conduit strain and right ventricular functional reserve noninvasively identify the high-stiffness subgroup.

items.title: Antecedent Kidney Function and Cardiovascular Mortality in Over 300 000 Patients With Incident Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease is a frequent comorbidity in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and has been proposed as a contributor to its development. However, the spectrum of antecedent kidney function before incident HFpEF and its association with subsequent cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter cohort study across 170 US Veterans Affairs hospitals, including patients with incident HFpEF diagnosed between January 1, 2000, and June 30, 2025. HFpEF was ascertained using natural language processing-derived left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% closest to the incident HF date and a validated HFpEF algorithm incorporating loop diuretic use, elevated natriuretic peptide levels, and an HFpEF–age, body mass index, and atrial fibrillation score >0.5. Antecedent kidney function was classified using 2 estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) measurements obtained ≥90 days apart before incident HFpEF and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. We characterized antecedent kidney function, including albuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g), and examined its associations with 5-year cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Competing-risk analysis was performed accounting for noncardiovascular death as a competing event for cardiovascular death. RESULTS: Of 304 712 patients meeting HFpEF ascertainment criteria, 236 910 comprised the final cohort; 51% had antecedent eGFR ≥60 mL/min per 1.73m 2 . Overall, 15% had an eGFR ≥90 mL/min per 1.73m 2 . Patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m 2 were older and had more diabetes and hypertension. 51% of the patients with eGFR <60 mL/min per 1.73m 2 had body mass index <30 kg/m 2 , including 20% with body mass index <25 kg/m 2 . Progressively lower antecedent kidney function was associated with graded increases in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization. Among decedents, the proportion of deaths attributed to cardiovascular causes increased from 25% in the preserved eGFR (≥90 mL/min per 1.73m 2 ) without documented albuminuria to 32% with albuminuria and 38% with advanced kidney dysfunction ( P <0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide study of patients with incident HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction was common but not uniformly present before HFpEF onset. Furthermore, among patients who developed HFpEF, antecedent kidney dysfunction identified a higher-risk phenotype, with progressively greater cardiovascular mortality and heart failure hospitalization with declining kidney function.

items.title: Heart Failure Presenting With Concurrent Chylothorax and Chylous Ascites Resolved by Revascularization in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: A Case Report and Review
Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF. METHODS: Male ZSF1 Obese rats (HFpEF, n=8) and Wistar Kyoto lean normotensive controls (Control, n=8) were studied at 26 weeks of age. The gastrocnemius was analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics. Differential expression across all omics layers was determined using standard statistical modeling with thresholds of absolute fold‑change >1.5 and FDR <0.05, unless otherwise specified. Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle metabolomics and lipidomics were performed in HFpEF and control rats, including analyses of the soleus and the extensor digitorum longus, to validate features associated with predominantly oxidative and glycolytic muscle, respectively. RESULTS: Pathway-level analysis for RNA sequencing and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (natural enrichment score (NES), −2.1; P <0.005), electron transport chain (NES, −2.0; P <0.005), and tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle (−1.8; P <0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES, 2.2; P <0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES, 1.8; P <0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES, 1.8; P <0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of tricarboxylic acid cycle cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-phosphatidylcholine species. Phosphatidylethanolamines species (16:0/16:1–18:0/18:2) were increased. CONCLUSIONS: HFpEF skeletal muscle shows signatures of profound mitochondrial and peroxisomal dysfunction with lipid overload, impaired branched chain amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, and a shift in membrane phospholipid composition, supporting an acquired metabolic myopathy in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

items.title: Recognition Requires Nomination: The People Who Make Excellence Visible
A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial of a Digital Health Intervention for Medication Optimization in Heart Failure: The ENGAGE-HF Trial Outcomes
items.abstract: Background: Despite clear evidence that guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) significantly reduces mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced and mildly reduced ejection fraction, real-world implementation remains suboptimal. Digital health interventions may promote GDMT titration after hospital discharge. Methods: The ENGAGE-HF trial was a multicenter, two-arm, open-label, randomized controlled trial across three academic centers, funded by the AHA Strategically Focused Research Network (SFRN) for Health Technology and Innovation. Patients recently hospitalized with HF, with or without a primary hospital diagnosis of HF, and LVEF <50% receiving suboptimal GDMT were randomized 1:1 to either the ENGAGE-HF app or usual care for 90 days. The ENGAGE-HF intervention consisted of a patient-facing mobile app and a clinician dashboard overseen by study coordinators. The primary outcome was the Medication Optimization Score (MOS, scale 0-100%) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes were individual GDMT therapies and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 90 days. Results: A total of 134 participants were randomized. At 90 days, the adjusted MOS was significantly higher in the ENGAGE-HF group compared to the control group (83.7% vs. 74.0%, p = 0.010). Results remained consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses. Overall prescribing prevalence increased more in the ENGAGE-HF group for MRAs (+15.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points) and SGLT2 inhibitors (+10.9 vs. +2.5 percentage points). Furthermore, the ENGAGE-HF group demonstrated greater increases in achieving target doses for ARNI (+18.8% vs. +6.3%) and beta-blockers (+8.5% vs. +0.6%). KCCQ-23 CSS at 90 days was 75.2 (SE 2.6) in the intervention group versus 72.2 (SE 2.6) in the control group (between-group p = 0.40). Conclusions: ENGAGE-HF, a digital health intervention that integrates remote monitoring, patient engagement, and clinical decision support, significantly improved GDMT optimization at 90 days compared with usual care among patients with HF. Registration: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT06750549

items.title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association
items.abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

items.title: Evaluation of an Echocardiography-Based Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Early HFpEF Detection
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is difficult to identify because of nonspecific symptoms and subtle echocardiographic abnormalities. EchoGo HF, an FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) model, estimates HFpEF probability from a single apical 4-chamber echocardiographic clip, but has been validated only in patients with clinically adjudicated HFpEF. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether AI-HFpEF can detect early HFpEF in community-dwelling adults without a clinical heart failure (HF) diagnosis and predict incident clinical HFpEF in patients within a health system. METHODS: The authors included 2 community cohorts (the MESA [Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis] Early HF study and the DHMS [Dallas Hearts and Minds Study]). Early HFpEF was defined by impaired exercise capacity or health-related quality of life with objective evidence of elevated cardiac filling pressures in patients without clinically diagnosed HF. The AI-HFpEF model was applied to resting echocardiograms, and the diagnostic performance was assessed. Multivariable models examined associations between AI-HFpEF output and early HFpEF phenotype. Separately, we included adults in the UTSW (University of Texas Southwestern) Health System with structurally normal echocardiograms and no prior HF (2018-2024) and assessed the association of AI-HFpEF output with incident HFpEF (adjudicated using a validated registry) using Cox regression. RESULTS: FPEF (AUROC: 0.83 vs 0.77), and diagnostic positivity was associated with early HFpEF (OR: 6.76; P < 0.001), shorter exercise duration, and lower peak oxygen uptake. In the UTSW cohort (N = 6,876; median follow-up = 33 months; incident HFpEF = 3.4%), an AI-HFpEF diagnostic positive result was associated with >2-fold higher incident HFpEF risk (aHR: 2.08; P < 0.001). This association persisted across all conventional diastolic dysfunction grades. CONCLUSIONS: AI-HFpEF identified the early HFpEF phenotype in community-dwelling adults and independently predicted incident clinical HFpEF among patients in a health system.

items.title: Echocardiography After Preeclampsia
Sex Differences in Health Status in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction
Identifying High-Risk Patients
Full issue PDF
Editorial Board
From Proband to Relative
Leadless Cardiac Resynchronization Results in Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling
Implications of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1RAs, and Nonsteroidal MRAs on the Anticipated Burden of Heart Failure
items.abstract: Background Several treatments that reduce the risk of heart failure (HF) have been introduced recently. Their impact on the future burden of HF in the U.S. has not been well characterized. Objectives This study aims to estimate the potential impact of recently approved cardiometabolic medications on the future burden of HF in the United States. Methods Using a nationally representative sample of persons in the United States 30-79 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline, we used the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events) equation to estimate the 10- and 30-year burden of HF and the projected impact of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on these estimates. The authors estimated the total number of HF cases that could be averted with risk-based treatment and calculated the number needed to treat to prevent HF. Results An estimated 5.5 million (95% CI: 5.1-5.8 million) U.S. adults 30-79 years of age without established cardiovascular disease will develop HF over 10 years. It is estimated to decrease to 5.1 million (95% CI: 4.7-5.4 million) with indicated treatment with a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, 5.2 million (95% CI: 4.8-5.6 million) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, 5.4 million (95% CI: 5.0-5.7 million) with nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and 4.8 million (95% CI: 4.4-5.2 million) with the use of combination therapy. The use of combination therapy in eligible persons with an estimated 10-year HF risk of ≥10% would result in 6.8 million (95% CI: 6.1-7.5 million) eligible participants, and 498,000 (95% CI: -663,000 to -319,000) fewer cases of HF, with a number needed to treat of 14 (95% CI: 10-22) to prevent 1 incident case. Conclusions The projected burden of HF in the U.S. is substantial. A risk-based approach to preventive treatment may help reduce this considerably. The feasibility of such an approach deserves further investigation.

items.title: Reinitiation of Optimal Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy After Coronary Bypass Grafting in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction
Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide in Obesity-Related HFpEF: Rationale and Design of CAMEO-SEMA
Remote Voice Analysis for Monitoring Ambulatory Heart Failure Patients: Results of the DETECT-HF Study
items.abstract: Background The Cordio HearO System is a software medical device that analyzes daily voice recordings to identify changes associated with worsening HF. Objective The objective of the DETECT-HF study was to evaluate the ability of the HearO System to detect impending HF events (HFEs) using a voice-based monitoring algorithm. Methods DETECT-HF was a prospective, international, multicenter, single-arm, blinded, noninterventional study in HF patients who performed daily voice recordings on their smartphones. Co-primary endpoints were sensitivity for detecting adjudicated first HFEs (HF hospitalization or outpatient HFE requiring intravenous therapy) and the unexplained priority notification rate (UPNR). Performance was assessed against predefined criteria of a lower 95% confidence interval (CI) ≥60% for sensitivity and <3 notifications/person-year for UPNR. Analyses were also performed using all HFEs (first and recurrent events). Secondary endpoints included safety and usability assessments, including patient adherence to daily voice recordings. Results Between March 2021 and July 2025, 563 patients were enrolled. Mean age was 67.6±11.5 years, and 70.9% were male. The HearO System detected 52 of 76 first HFEs, yielding a sensitivity of 68.4% (95% CI: 58.0%-78.9%; p=0.0573), which was below the pre-specified performance target. For all HFEs (n=112), sensitivity was 70.5% (95% CI: 60.8%-78.7%). On average, HFEs were detected 24.1 days before clinical presentation. UPNR was 2.65 notifications/patient-year (95% CI: 2.53-2.76; P<0.001) for first HFEs, meeting the pre-specified performance criterion, and 2.59 notifications/patient-year (95% CI: 2.48-2.70) for all HFEs. Sensitivity and UPNR estimates were consistent across prespecified subgroups. A questionnaire demonstrated excellent usability (mean scores ranging from 4.7 to 4.9 on a 5-point scale across usability questions). Mean adherence to daily recordings was 85%, and no device-related adverse events occurred. Conclusions Voice-based monitoring with the HearO System detected impending HFEs weeks before clinical presentation with reasonable sensitivity, low alert burden, high adherence, and an excellent safety profile.

items.title: A Multi-Center Cluster-Assigned Trial of Electronic Alerts to Improve Prescribing of Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Therapy for Heart Failure
Ultraprocessed Food Consumption and Incident Heart Failure
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with adverse cardiometabolic outcomes and increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. However, the relationship between UPF intake and incident heart failure (HF) remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aims of this study were to examine the relationship between UPF consumption and incident HF and to evaluate potential biological mediators. METHODS: A sample of 6,531 U.S. adults 45-84 years of age without cardiovascular disease at baseline from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) was analyzed. UPF intake was classified according to the Nova system. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between UPF intake and incident HF. Phenotypes were classified as heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (ejection fraction <50%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (ejection fraction ≥50%). Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the potential mediating role of waist-to-height ratio as a surrogate measure for central adiposity. RESULTS: Higher UPF intake was significantly associated with increased risk of incident HF across sequentially adjusted models. In the primary model (model 2), each additional daily serving of UPF was associated with a 5% higher risk of incident HF (HR: 1.052; 95% CI: 1.002-1.103). When stratified by phenotype, UPF intake remained significantly associated with HFpEF (HR: 1.096; 95% CI: 1.016-1.183) but not HFrEF. Participants in the upper 80% of UPF intake had a >2-fold higher risk for HFpEF than those in the lowest 20% (HR: 2.234; 95% CI: 1.289-3.874). In mediation analyses, waist-to-height ratio statistically accounted for ∼51% of the association between UPF intake and total HF and 49% of the association between UPF intake and HFpEF. CONCLUSIONS: Higher UPF consumption was significantly associated with an increased risk for incident HF, with associations driven primarily by the HFpEF phenotype. Central adiposity, measured by waist-to-height ratio, demonstrated a potential mediating role, suggesting that obesity-related cardiometabolic pathways may represent an important pathway linking UPF consumption to HF risk.

items.title: Rethinking Authorship in Large Multicenter Clinical Trials
Safety and Efficacy of Omecamtiv Mecarbil by QRS Duration and Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy in GALACTIC-HF
items.abstract: Background Prolonged QRS duration portends worse outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). In GALACTIC-HF, omecamtiv mecarbil (OM) reduced the primary composite endpoint of first heart failure (HF) event or cardiovascular death. Objectives The objectives of this study were to evaluate whether QRS duration and the presence of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) modify the treatment effect of OM. Methods GALACTIC-HF enrolled patients with symptomatic HF, HFrEF (≤35%), and elevated natriuretic peptides. Baseline QRS duration was available in 8,089 of 8,232 participants (98.0%), who were classified into 3 groups: QRS duration <120 ms without CRT (n = 3,724), QRS duration ≥120 ms without CRT (n = 3,225), and CRT regardless of QRS duration (n = 1,140). The authors assessed whether the effect of OM on the primary composite endpoint, first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, and all-cause death differed across these groups. Results Patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT and those with CRT were older, had lower EF, worse health status, and higher N-terminal pro–B-type natriuretic peptide levels than those with QRS <120 ms without CRT. When modeled as a continuous variable, baseline QRS duration was associated with clinical outcomes among patients without CRT but not among those with CRT. Among patients with QRS ≥120 ms without CRT, OM appeared to confer less benefit for the primary composite endpoint ( P interaction = 0.072), for cardiovascular death ( P interaction = 0.003), and for all-cause death ( P interaction = 0.009). In contrast, among patients treated with CRT, OM was beneficial regardless of QRS duration. Conclusions In GALACTIC-HF, OM appeared less effective in patients with prolonged QRS duration who did not have CRT, whereas it remained beneficial in CRT-treated patients. (Global Approach to Lowering Adverse Cardiac Outcomes Through Improving Contractility in Heart Failure [GALACTIC-HF]; NCT02929329 )

items.title: Systemic Microvascular Endothelial Dysfunction in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder featuring microvascular dysfunction and metabolic comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the extent to which systemic microvascular abnormalities reflect HFpEF or coexisting T2D remains incompletely understood. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to characterize systemic microvascular dysfunction in patients with HFpEF and to evaluate the contribution of comorbid T2D. METHODS: Systemic microvascular function, defined as flow responses expressed as cutaneous vascular conductance, was assessed using laser speckle contrast analysis with iontophoresis of acetylcholine, insulin, and sodium nitroprusside. Analysis adjusted for age and sex were performed across healthy controls (n = 23), T2D (n = 138), HFpEF without T2D (n = 63), and HFpEF with T2D (n = 27). RESULTS: Insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion was reduced in participants with T2D (-0.30 arbitrary perfusion units [APU]/mm Hg; P < 0.001) and in HFpEF with T2D (-0.32 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.004) compared with controls, whereas responses in HFpEF without T2D were not different from controls. Perfusion responses to sodium nitroprusside were reduced in T2D and HFpEF with T2D, while responses to acetylcholine were preserved. No statistically detectable interaction between HFpEF and T2D was observed. Sex did not modify the relationship between HFpEF and microvascular dysfunction, but exploratory sex-stratified analyses showed reduced insulin-mediated microvascular perfusion in T2D (mean difference: -0.30 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.020) and HFpEF + T2D (mean difference: -0.51 APU/mm Hg; P = 0.002) compared with controls. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic microvascular dysfunction, particularly impaired insulin-mediated vasodilation, was observed in HFpEF. The observed abnormalities were predominantly present in participants with comorbid type 2 diabetes.
