items.title: Effect of Wrist Extension Angle on Radial and Ulnar Artery Sonoanatomy in Children: A Prospective Ultrasound Study
items.abstract: Background Ultrasound‐guided radial artery cannulation is common in pediatrics but technically challenging. While the ulnar artery is a potential alternative, its sonoanatomy relative to the radial artery is not well defined. Aims This study aimed to compare the sonoanatomic characteristics of the radial and ulnar arteries in children, evaluating how age, weight, and wrist position (0°, 30°, and 45°) influence arterial dimensions and depth to identify the most favorable profile for cannulation. Methods Ultrasound evaluation of the radial and ulnar arteries was performed at 0°, 30°, and 45° wrist extension in 180 anesthetized children aged 0–120 months using custom‐made wooden blocks. Arterial dimensions and skin‐to‐artery distance were evaluated overall and across age (≤ 24 vs. > 24 months) and weight (≤ 12 vs. > 12 kg) subgroups to identify optimal access conditions. Results Wrist extension angle did not significantly affect anteroposterior diameter (1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.078), but significantly influenced transverse arterial diameter (1.5–1.6 mm, p = 0.003) and skin‐to‐artery distance (2.4–2.8 mm at 30°, p < 0.001). The radial artery was widest at 0° (1.6 ± 1.0 mm), while the ulnar artery peaked at 30° (1.6 ± 0.4 mm). Skin‐to‐artery distance was minimized at 30° for both vessels. In children ≤ 12 kg, radial transverse diameter decreased paradoxically from 0° to 45° (1.6 ± 0.4 to 1.4 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.013), while the ulnar artery was widest at 30° (1.5 ± 0.3 mm, p = 0.007). In infants ≤ 24 months, wrist angle did not significantly influence radial artery depth ( p = 0.631, mean overall depth between 2.5–2.6 mm). Conclusion A 30° wrist extension angle provides the most favorable sonoanatomic profile for both arteries. Although a larger vessel caliber may potentially facilitate cannulation, its clinical benefit remains uncertain as cannulation outcomes were not assessed. These findings support individualized ultrasound‐guided assessment rather than a fixed positioning strategy.

items.title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate a health system–wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum. METHODS: We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021–May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024–August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed. RESULTS: We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% ( P =.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% ( P <.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% ( P =.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P =.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally. CONCLUSION: The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

items.title: Association Between Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes and Postpartum Contraceptive Method Selection and Use
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adverse pregnancy outcomes are associated with self-reported postpartum contraceptive use and method selection. METHODS: We performed a secondary data analysis of data from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (phase 8 cohort, 2016–2022). The exposures of interest were adverse pregnancy outcomes, including maternal hypertension, diabetes, preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, and infant death. Contraceptive methods were grouped into four categories: permanent contraception, long-acting reversible contraception, prescription-start methods (patch, ring, pill, or injectable), and patient-start methods (condoms, natural family planning, withdrawal, or abstinence) based on the level of clinical engagement required. We employed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association between adverse pregnancy outcomes and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, we used multinomial logistic regression to analyze whether adverse pregnancy outcomes influenced method selection. RESULTS: In this analysis of 222,412 individuals, 32.7% of the study sample experienced at least one adverse pregnancy outcome and 77.4% of the sample reported using contraception. In weighted models, experiencing three or more adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraception usage (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.82–0.97). Patients who experienced infant death had lower odds of using any postpartum contraception than those who did not (aOR 0.39; 95% CI, 0.33–0.46). We observed no association between experiencing preterm birth, prolonged infant hospitalization, gestational diabetes, or hypertension and postpartum contraceptive use. Among postpartum contraceptive users, experiencing at least one adverse pregnancy outcome was associated with a higher likelihood of using permanent contraception relative to patient-start methods. CONCLUSION: Experiencing an increasing number of adverse pregnancy outcomes was associated with lower odds of postpartum contraceptive use. Adverse pregnancy outcomes were associated with permanent contraception use. Patient-centered contraceptive counseling and shared decision making to support patients in identifying and actualizing their postpartum reproductive goals are necessary in the wake of adverse pregnancy outcomes.

items.title: Patient Report of Subsequent Uterine-Sparing Leiomyomata Procedures up to 10 Years
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine risk of subsequent treatment after uterine-sparing procedures for uterine leiomyomata. METHODS: Study participants from two uterine leiomyomata procedure studies were recontacted. The baseline procedures studied included myomectomy, endometrial ablation, laparoscopic ultrasound–guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA), and uterine artery embolization (UAE). Participants reported all uterine leiomyomata procedures after their baseline uterine-sparing leiomyomata procedure. The subsequent treatment options analyzed included the baseline uterine leiomyomata procedures plus hysterectomy and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–guided focused ultrasonography. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate differences in retreatment risk according to baseline procedure by means of hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95% CIs. Fisher exact tests were used to examine the association between baseline procedure and retreatment procedure. RESULTS: The total number of participants in the study is 817. Median age at baseline procedure was 39.7 years; participant median age at recontact was 46.8 years. Follow-up after baseline procedure was 4.0–10.5 years. Baseline procedure types included myomectomy (n=469, 66.0%), endometrial ablation (n=90, 12.7%), RFA (n=96, 13.5%), and UAE (n=56, 7.9%). Of the 204 participants (28.7%) who had retreatment for uterine leiomyomata, the most common subsequent procedure was hysterectomy (n=94, 46.1%), followed by myomectomy (n=57, 27.9%), UAE (n=26, 12.7%), endometrial ablation (n=12, 5.9%), MRI-guided focused ultrasonography (n=9, 4.4%), and RFA (n=6, 2.9%). Within 5 years after the baseline procedure, 79.1% (95% CI, 76.2–82.1%) had no additional uterine procedures; 64.1% (95% CI, 57.7–71.2%) had none within 10 years. When endometrial ablation, RFA, and UAE were compared with myomectomy, RFA was found to have a higher retreatment rate (HR 1.61, 95% CI, 1.08–2.40). Those who had undergone myomectomy at baseline were the least likely (10.9%) and those who had undergone endometrial ablation were most likely (22.2%) to have a subsequent hysterectomy. CONCLUSION: The majority of women who have uterine-sparing uterine leiomyomata procedures can remain treatment free for 5–10 years. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06430320.

items.title: Improving Mental Health Support for Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Mothers Through a Universal Screening Quality-Improvement Initiative
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To improve early perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening for neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) mothers and facilitate timely referral to mental health services through the integration of a dedicated mental health clinician at our level 3 NICU. METHODS: A multidisciplinary team convened to address barriers to universal maternal mental health screening in our NICU. Key drivers were identified, focusing on appropriate screening tools, availability of a mental health clinician, and a robust referral process should a mother screen positive. The primary outcome measure was percentage of referrals made for mothers who screened positive for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders. The process measure was percentage of mothers screened. Clinical characteristics were compared between mothers who screened positive and those who screened negative to ensure that any disparities identified were addressed in real time. RESULTS: Since implementation of our universal screening program, 95.0% of mothers in our NICU have been screened for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (an increase from 29.5%). Of those, 59.9% required referral for additional psychosocial support (an increase from 25.3%). Mothers who screened positive were more likely to be Black non-Hispanic ( P <.001), and mothers who screened negative were more likely to be White non-Hispanic ( P =.021). No differences were identified in delivery mode or breastfeeding at discharge. CONCLUSION: A dedicated NICU mental health clinician, with multidisciplinary buy-in, may allow the successful implementation and maintenance of a universal perinatal mood and anxiety disorder screening and referral program.

items.title: Hospital-Level Variation in Antenatal Corticosteroid Use for Late Preterm Births
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether and to what extent hospitals across the United States vary in their use of late preterm steroids. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of singleton births with known gestational ages identified in the Premier Healthcare Database from 2015 to 2022. The primary variable of interest was hospital-level adoption of antenatal corticosteroid use for late preterm singleton deliveries, calculated as the proportion of late preterm singleton births (34–36 completed weeks of gestation) with any betamethasone exposure during the same late preterm period. Hospital adoption was defined as the weighted average rate of steroid administration among late preterm births across the entire postperiod. Hospitals were ranked by their late preterm steroid adoption rates and categorized by quartile based on the empirical distribution. Temporal trends were assessed using annual hospital-level adoption rates and visualized using time series plots and distributional plots. A logistic regression model was constructed to identify hospital characteristics associated with being a highest-quartile adopter. RESULTS: The analysis cohort included 726 hospitals and 5,109,270 births, of which 309,837 (6.1%) were singleton late preterm births. Hospital steroid exposure rates ranged from 0% to 92% and were categorized into quartiles based on overall exposure rate, with cutoffs at 22.4%, 33.9%, and 45.1%. Median exposure rates increased progressively across quartiles, from 15.4% (IQR 10.0–18.9%) in the lowest-adopting hospitals (quartile 1) to 54.3% (IQR 49.1–61.0%) in the highest-adopting hospitals (quartile 4), with substantial within-quartile variation. In the multivariable model, urban location was a strong predictor of high adoption after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.03; 95% CI, 1.04–4.02, P =.04). Compared with Midwestern hospitals, Southern hospitals had significantly lower odds of being high adopters (aOR 0.32; 95% CI, 0.17–0.61, P <.001). Among clinical case mix variables, a higher proportion of late preterm births at 34 weeks of gestation was strongly associated with high adoption (aOR 2.39; 95% CI, 1.73–3.36, P <.001). CONCLUSION: After the publication of the ALPS (Antenatal Late Preterm Steroids) trial, the adoption of late preterm steroid use was heterogeneous among U.S. hospitals. These findings highlight the need for a more in-depth exploration of local factors that drive the adoption of evidence-based practices outside of observable hospital characteristics.

The Rising Tide of Cardiovascular Risk in Younger Women
items.abstract: Menopause management is in the midst of a paradigm shift as enthusiasm, fueled by the lay press and online influencers, increases amongst women, yielding an escalating interest in hormone therapy (HT) that has not been experienced since the turn of the last century. Updates to regulatory labeling of menopausal HT products include the removal of boxed warnings and language that recommended using the lowest dose for the shortest time while focusing on risks and benefits to those seeking menopause symptom relief—women younger than 60 or within 10 years of menopause. This renewed desire for menopausal HT must be tempered with the understanding that risks for cardiovascular disease (CVD) are also rising in premenopausal women as are hospitalizations for acute coronary syndromes. Factors that contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk include adverse pregnancy outcomes, which are occurring with increasing frequency. The metabolic changes that accompany the menopause transition further complicate a woman's cardiovascular risk profile. Many women today will arrive at menopause with more advanced CVD risk than what was encountered in the past. If women are considering HT for menopausal symptom relief or bone preservation, careful consideration is required to identify and treat modifiable CVD risks—dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, hypertension, and, increasingly, obesity—to targets established by guidelines before initiating HT. Risk assessment with validated risk calculators can help stratify CVD risk, a factor that determines lipid lowering therapy, and the advisability and choice of menopausal HT. The rising tide of cardiovascular risk does not have to make waves at menopause.

items.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease in Pregnancy
items.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) presents unique clinical considerations related to fertility, medical therapy, and delivery planning. The strongest predictor of adverse pregnancy outcomes is active disease, making maintenance of remission a central management priority. Prepregnancy counseling for patients with IBD should address reproductive goals, nutritional status, and the potential effect of prior pelvic surgery on fertility. Most established IBD therapies, including aminosalicylates, thiopurines, and biologic agents, can be continued to maintain remission, whereas methotrexate is contraindicated, and Janus kinase inhibitors and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulators are generally avoided. Delivery planning should be individualized, with cesarean delivery generally favored for active perianal Crohn disease or rectovaginal fistula and shared decision making emphasized for patients with an ileal pouch–anal anastomosis. Optimal outcomes depend on coordinated multidisciplinary care that prioritizes disease control, treatment continuation, and individualized reproductive and delivery planning.

items.title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy and Black–White Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the proportion of the Black–White racial disparity in severe maternal morbidity (SMM) that could be eliminated by preventing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,242,574 Black and White birthing people 12–55 years of age with deliveries in Massachusetts from 1998 to 2021 using PELL (Pregnancy to Early Life Longitudinal data system). Maternal race was used as a proxy for exposure to racism. The primary outcome was SMM excluding blood transfusion–only events (SMM-20); we also considered SMM including blood transfusion–only events (SMM-21) and cardiac complications. We conducted causal mediation analyses with HDP as the mediator and used G-estimation to estimate the Black–White racial disparity in SMM that would remain if HDP were prevented. We calculated the proportion of the disparity that could be eliminated by preventing HDP and severe HDP separately. RESULTS: Compared with White birthing people, Black birthing people experienced 63.8 excess SMM-20 events per 10,000 in-hospital deliveries (95% CI, 58.1–69.6). If HDP were prevented, the disparity would be reduced to 38.6 excess SMM-20 events (95% CI, 32.9–44.2), suggesting that 39.6% of the absolute Black–White racial disparity in SMM-20 could be eliminated. The estimated proportions eliminated were 33.1% for SMM-21 and 57.6% for cardiac complications. The proportion of the Black–White racial disparity eliminated by preventing severe HDP alone was 27.9% for SMM-20, 20.7% for SMM-21, and 31.3% for cardiac complications. CONCLUSION: Preventing HDP could substantially reduce Black–White racial disparities in SMM.

A Randomized Trial of Fractionated CO2 Laser With Topical Clobetasol Compared With Fractionated CO2 Laser With Placebo for Treatment of Vulvar Lichen Sclerosus
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare skin-related outcomes in women with vulvar lichen sclerosus treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser with concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% with women treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser plus placebo ointment. METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial was conducted at nine U.S. sites from March 2022 to April 2025. English- or Spanish-speaking adult women with lichen sclerosus electing vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment were eligible. Women were excluded if they had prior vaginal mesh prolapse repair, previous radiation therapy, prior laser, immunomodulators or systemic therapy for lichen sclerosus, active genital infection, suspicious vulvar lesion or malignancy, active treatment for malignancy, or poor wound healing or if they were currently pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy. All participants underwent three vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatments 4–6 weeks apart and were randomized 1:1 to concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% or petrolatum-based ointment (placebo) 0.25–0.5 g nightly for 4 weeks starting at first laser treatment and then twice weekly until end of study. The primary outcome was proportion of women with improvement of 16 or more points on the Skindex-29, a validated questionnaire measuring a patient's skin-related symptoms and functioning, assessed at 4–5 weeks after completion of fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment. Additional outcomes included Skindex-29 domain scores, patient impression of improvement (PGI-I [Patient Global Impression of Improvement] score), treatment satisfaction, and adverse events. RESULTS: Two hundred one participants were randomized, and 180 (89 clobetasol vs 91 placebo) had complete data. Most women indicated symptom onset 1 year or more before lichen sclerosus diagnosis, and approximately 90% had previously used topical corticosteroids. Nearly a third of all participants achieved the primary outcome (30.3% clobetasol vs 27.5% placebo, P =.67). Participants in the clobetasol arm demonstrated a greater improvement in Skindex-29 symptom score (mean change −19.0±18.5 clobetasol vs −10.1±19.8 placebo, P <.01) and total score (mean change −13.0±15.9 clobetasol vs −8.1±15.5 placebo, P =.04). More participants were “satisfied” or “very satisfied” with treatment after clobetasol (85.4% clobetasol vs 69.2% placebo, P =.01). Fifteen adverse events occurred in 12 participants (6 per cohort). CONCLUSION: There was no difference in the proportion of patients improving at least 16 points on the Skindex-29 after combined vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser and clobetasol compared with placebo. The clobetasol group reported greater improvement in lichen sclerosus–specific symptoms and higher treatment satisfaction. The rates of adverse events were low regardless of concomitant therapy. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04951206.

items.title: Urgency urinary incontinence, one condition, or many? Cluster analysis of physiological variables in the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II cohort.
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Our understanding of the pathophysiology of urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) remains incomplete, limiting treatment selection. Although UUI is considered to be multifactorial, evidence for which factors contribute is limited and there has tended to be a focus on bladder dysfunction, rather than taking a more multi-dimensional view. Objective To identify physiologically distinct phenotypes of UUI by cluster analysis of bladder and urethral motor and sensory function tests. Methods Secondary analysis of data from the Symptoms of Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction Research Network (LURN) II Organ project which included 56 women with UUI and 31 asymptomatic controls was performed. Participants underwent urethral motor and sensory assessments, and rapid-fill cystometry before and after intravesical lidocaine instillation. Thirty-two physiological variables were analyzed using a validated, resampling-based consensus clustering pipeline. Cluster differences were assessed using ANOVA with false discovery rate correction ("P adj ") and logistic regression. Results Three distinct phenotypes were identified. Cluster A (n=15) showed detrusor overactivity during both saline and post-lidocaine fills, and reduced bladder sensation volumes (39-55% of controls) with normal urethral function. Cluster B (n=18) demonstrated significant lidocaine-related capacity increase of 138 mL (72%) (P adj ≤ 0.003 and P adj ≤ 0.0001, respectively) and a 30% decrease in maximum urethral closure pressure (P adj = 0.0076). Cluster C (n=23) exhibited minimal change in volumes post-lidocaine and a general lack of detrusor overactivity. Demographics and symptoms were similar across clusters. In regression analysis adjusting for age, BMI, and vaginal parity, primary predictors for A were detrusor overactivity (AUC = 0.95); for B, lidocaine-related capacity change (AUC = 0.92); and for C, low first desire to void (post-lidocaine) normalized by the functional (bladder diary) bladder capacity (AUC = 0.83). Conclusions In this exploratory analysis, clustering of physiological data identified three potential UUI phenotypes with differing bladder and urethral characteristics. If validated in larger cohorts, these phenotypes could guide trials testing whether phenotype-directed treatment improves outcomes.

items.title: Baclofen Vaginal Suppositories in Chronic Pelvic Pain: a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled Trial
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Background Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction is a common contributor to chronic pelvic pain (CPP), yet targeted treatment options remain limited. Objective To determine whether baclofen vaginal suppositories in CPP is safe and effective when compared with placebo. Methods This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial compared 20mg baclofen vaginal suppositories to placebo suppositories nightly in women with CPP. Women older than18 years without allergy to baclofen or the suppository base were included if they had ≥40/100 mm pain on a visual analogue scale (VAS) with palpation of the obturator internus or levator ani on standardized pelvic exam. Improvement in this standardized pelvic exam 100mm VAS pain score represented the primary outcome. Participants completed Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) pain interference, PROMIS global health, PROMIS sexual function at baseline, 4, and 8 weeks, with repeat pelvic examination at 8 weeks. The study was powered to detect the minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 20mm on a 100mm VAS pain scale on a standardized pelvic floor muscle examination with a total sample size of 34, 17 in each group. Adverse events, pill count, and other treatments for CPP during the study period were collected. Differences between treatment groups were assessed using the Mann-Whitney test, and multiple imputation was used to account for missing data. Results A total of 39 women were enrolled in the study with 37 randomized.19 patients received baclofen vaginal suppositories and 18 received placebo suppositories. Demographic data was similar between groups, with similar mean age (42.5 ± 12.5 baclofen vs 46.3 ± 12.2 placebo) and body mass index (29.4 ± 6.7 vs 29.8 ± 7.6). There was a statistically and clinically significant improvement in the primary outcome of change in the 100mm VAS pain score on pelvic floor muscle examination at 8 weeks relative to baseline in the baclofen group as compared to placebo (median improvement of 33.5 mm [IQR: 30 to 46.230.0] baclofen vs 7.2 mm [0.0 to 10.0] placebo, p= Conclusions In this appropriately powered, randomized trial, patients experienced statistically and clinically significantly less pain with 8 weeks of nightly baclofen vaginal suppositories when compared to placebo. Baclofen suppositories were shown to be well tolerated with no adverse events.

items.title: Hofbauer Cells and Placental Villous Inflammation in Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Spatial and Functional Analyses
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preterm birth is a major cause of neonatal morbidity/mortality strongly associated with pathological placental inflammation, but cellular mechanisms leading to this inflammation are poorly understood. OBJECTIVE(S): Our objectives were to ascertain which immune cells are in the placental villi, understand cell-specific profiles through technologies maintaining cell localization within the tissue, and determine the role of Hofbauer cells in the dysregulated placental inflammation during preterm versus term birth with a focus on spontaneous preterm birth. STUDY DESIGN: We first evaluated what cells (immune) are in the placental villi and which could be contributing to placental inflammation. We included 228 patients with preterm or term deliveries, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, and obtained placentas for histological analysis and performed imaging mass cytometry and spatial transcriptomics on a subset of tissue (n=24). Fresh placentas were also obtained to determine the inflammatory mediator profile and cell-specific protein production by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay and flow cytometry (n=8-11). RESULTS: Imaging mass cytometry revealed that placental macrophages (Hofbauer cells) were the main immune cell in the placental villi. Furthermore, we observed that preterm placentas, both spontaneous and non-spontaneous, had significantly increased CD163+ and CD68+ cells compared to term. Placental villi macrophages in spontaneous preterm versus spontaneous term analyses revealed a predominance of inflammatory genes and pathways with an involvement from trophoblast cells supporting inflammation, whereas stromal cells were primarily involved in extracellular matrix remodeling. Spontaneous vs non-spontaneous comparisons supported that even though both preterm birth groups are inflammatory, key inflammatory pathways such as TNF⍺ are enriched in spontaneous PTB, while in the term comparisons the pathways were either not related to inflammation or vastly different, with IL-2 being the top signaling pathway. In an ex vivo model of inflammation using placental explants, we found increases in pro-inflammatory mediators that coincided with our bioinformatic analyses. Primary cell experiments, using isolated cytotrophoblasts and Hofbauer cells, further supported that Hofbauer cells were a key contributor to pro-inflammatory mediator production. CONCLUSIONS: This work showcases the cell-specific profile of placental macrophages and the inflammatory profile observed in preterm placentas and provides novel insights into the pro-inflammatory role of Hofbauer cells in the placental villi.

items.title: Ultrasound-guided suction with balloon tamponade for cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy: a combined treatment strategy
items.containerTitle: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
items.abstract: Cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy (CSEP) is a severe iatrogenic complication of cesarean delivery (CD). However, there is no consensus yet on how to treat CSEP. This report describes a minimally invasive approach combining ultrasound-guided suction evacuation of the ectopic sac followed by immediate balloon tamponade insertion at the site of the prior CD. Continuous visualisation of the uterine-bladder interface helps prevent accidental uterine or bladder injuries, while mechanical balloon may help in providing adequate haemostasis. In our experience, this method may be a reasonable and potentially effective minimally invasive approach to treating CSEP, though it requires confirmation in adequately powered randomised controlled trials.

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccination in Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment at 18 to 30 Months
items.abstract: Importance Little is known about neurodevelopmental outcomes of children exposed to SARS-CoV-2 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine during pregnancy. Evidence on long-term offspring outcomes after in utero exposure to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination is needed to inform vaccine recommendations in pregnancy. Objective To evaluate whether there is an association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or shortly before pregnancy and offspring neurodevelopmental measures. Design, Setting, and Participants This multicenter, prospective, cohort study of 18- to 30-month-old children was conducted at 14 centers of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network from 2024 through 2025. Women who received a SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine during or within 30 days prior to pregnancy (exposed) were matched with women who did not (unexposed) by delivery site, delivery date, insurance status, and race and ethnicity. These data were analyzed from June 2025 to May 2026. Exposures Maternal receipt of at least 1 dose of an mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccine during, or within 30 days prior to, the index pregnancy vs no SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during pregnancy or within 30 days prior. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was Ages and Stages Questionnaire version 3 (ASQ-3) total score, which was deemed to be equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups if the 90% CI of the median difference was between −10 and 10. Secondary outcomes included domain-specific ASQ-3 scores, the Child Behavior Checklist, Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, and Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire scores. Results Of 3956 screened, 271 exposed and 240 unexposed children were enrolled. Matching on all characteristics was possible in 217 pairs. Of the 434 children enrolled, 258 (59.4%) were Non-Hispanic White, 96 (22.1%) Non-Hispanic Black, 52 (12.0%) Hispanic, and 28 (6.5%) were not represented by any of the above racial or ethnic groups. Median age at assessment was 25.8 [24.6 to 28.3] months, 221 were female (50.9%), and 213 were male (49.1%). Exposed mothers were more likely to be nulliparous; their children were slightly younger at assessment and more likely to have been vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. The primary outcome of ASQ-3 score was equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups (255 vs 260, adjusted median difference, −3.4; 90% CI, −9.8 to 3.0). There were no significant differences in secondary outcomes. Conclusions and Relevance In this multicenter cohort study, ASQ-3 scores were equivalent between 18- to 30-month-old children whose mothers did or did not receive mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or immediately prior to pregnancy. These findings support continued recommendations for SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy.

items.title: Youth Exposure to Food and Beverage Marketing on Digital Media Platforms
items.abstract: Importance Youth are heavy users of digital devices, and digital media increasingly represents a source for unhealthy food marketing, which the World Health Organization highlights as a risk for poor diet and health. Objective To examine the extent and nature of youth exposure to food marketing on digital media across multiple platforms. Design, Setting, and Participants This cross-sectional study conducted from November 2024 to October 2025 used real-time screen capture data and surveyed screen use to estimate youth exposure to food marketing on digital media, including differences by sociodemographic characteristics. Content and nutritional analyses assessed marketed food categories, companies, and product healthfulness based on the Pan American Health Organization’s nutrient profile model (PAHO-NPM), as well as characteristics of marketing exposure. Participants included youth in the US aged 8 to 17 years. Exposure Food marketing on digital media. Main Outcomes and Measures Hours of smartphone and/or tablet device use per day and estimated median food marketing exposures per year among youth. Distribution of marketed food items by food category and company were analyzed, as was the percent exceeding the PAHO-NPM standard. Marketing exposures were reviewed by platform, source, and type. Results Participants included 1011 youth (median [IQR] age, 12 [10-15] years; 519 female [51.3%]; 511 aged 8-12 years; 500 aged 13-17 years). Participants reported spending a mean (SD) of 3.7 (1.9) hours per day using smartphones or tablets outside of school or homework activities. Estimated median number of food marketing exposures among youths was 3883 (IQR, 0-16 697) per year. Exposure was higher for adolescents vs children (10 107 [IQR, 0-26 205] per year vs 1427 [IQR, 0-7795] per year; P &lt; .001), female vs male youths (8017 [IQR, 0-25 999] per year vs 2139 [0-9027] per year; P &lt; .001), and youth with non–college-educated vs college-educated parents or guardians (5380 [IQR, 0-22 422] per year vs 3431 [IQR, 0-15 128] per year; P = .04). Exposure was higher but not significant for non-Hispanic Black vs White youth (6358 [IQR, 0-24 053] vs 3697 [IQR, 0-16 287]; P = .06). The largest food marketed categories were fast food (1983 of 6896 [28.8%]), sweets (1407 [20.4%]), and beverages (1384 [20.1%]). A total of 2437 of 2660 nonrestaurant food marketed items (91.6%) did not meet PAHO-NPM standards. A total of 4256 of 5154 food marketing exposures (82.6%) to youth were viewed on social media platforms (TikTok, 1565 of 5154 [30.4%] and YouTube, 1162 of 5154 [22.6%]). The majority of marketing exposures were paid (2703 of 5154 [52.4%]), 2261 (43.9%) were earned, and 190 (3.7%) were owned. Almost half (3231 of 6896 [46.9%]) of marketed food items were from Children’s Food and Beverage Advertising Initiative (CFBAI)–member companies. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this cross-sectional study suggest that youth exposure to unhealthy food marketing on digital media is high and differences exist across sociodemographic groups. Results that a substantial portion of exposure comes from nonpaid earned media and CFBAI-member companies highlights the complexities of and need for regulation.

Satisfaction, Regret, and Harm After Hormone Therapy in Youth From a Multidisciplinary Gender Clinic
items.abstract: Importance Concerns about regret and harm have led to restrictions on transgender and gender-diverse youths’ access to testosterone or estrogen therapy (ie, hormone therapy [HT]), while empirical data on decisional regret among those initiating HT as youth remain limited. Objectives To examine satisfaction, regret, and perceived harm among individuals who initiated HT as youth and to identify demographic and clinical characteristics associated with regret or harm and current HT status (receiving vs not). Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study evaluates self-report surveys collected from October 2023 to October 2025 among former patients who initiated HT as youth at a single multidisciplinary gender clinic in the US. Data analysis was conducted from December 2025 to August 2026. Exposure Initiation of estrogen or testosterone. Main Outcomes and Measures Decision Regret Scale (DRS) total score (range, 0-100; higher scores indicate greater regret); item-level satisfaction, regret, and perceived harm; and current HT status. Associations with demographic and clinical characteristics were examined using nonparametric, Welch t , Fisher exact, or Pearson χ 2 tests as appropriate, with parametric sensitivity analyses for the DRS total score. Results Of the 376 participants who initiated HT as youth (112 [29.8%] initiating estrogen and 264 [70.2%] initiating testosterone; current age, 14-28 years; mean [SD] age, 20.9 [2.9] years; time since HT initiation: range, 1.2 months to 10.7 years; mean [SD], 4.9 [2.5] years), 4 were missing DRS scores, all of whom were currently receiving HT. Among the 372 respondents with DRS scores, overall decisional regret was very low (mean [SD] DRS score, 4.3 [14.7]; median [IQR], 0 [0-0]); 360 participants (96.8%) endorsed that receiving HT was the right decision, 10 (2.7%) reported regret, and 7 (1.9%) reported perceived harm. DRS scores were higher among participants not currently receiving HT vs currently receiving HT and among those identifying on the nonbinary vs binary spectrum; parametric sensitivity analyses estimated mean differences of 15.95 points (95% CI, 8.50-23.39) and 6.07 points (95% CI, 2.15-9.99), respectively. Participants not currently receiving HT (65 participants [17.3%]) were more likely than those currently receiving HT (311 [82.7%]) to have received testosterone (odds ratio, 3.58; 95% CI, 1.65-7.78; P = .001) and identify on the nonbinary spectrum (odds ratio, 8.88; 95% CI, 4.76-16.58; P &lt; .001), were older (mean difference, 1.04 years; 95% CI, 0.45-1.64 years; P = .001), and had longer time since initiating HT (mean difference, 1.00 year; 95% CI, 0.48-1.53 years; P &lt; .001). Neither regret or harm nor current HT status was associated with age at HT initiation or prepubertal gender diversity. Conclusions and Relevance The findings of this cohort study complement the literature documenting mental health benefits of HT, providing further support for existing standards of care for transgender and gender-diverse youth.
items.limitations: This study has several limitations. While the study assessed satisfaction with the decision to initiate HT, it did not examine satisfaction with the specific effects of HT. Although characteristics of participants no longer receiving HT were examined, reasons for discontinuation were not. Further, several participants reported ambivalent feelings toward HT (ie, neither agreeing nor disagreeing). Research has started to examine these treatment experiences and trajectories in greater depth among TGD adults; however, additional research specific to TGD youth is needed to support clinicians in providing developmentally informed and individualized care.

items.title: Air Pollution and Atopic Dermatitis in Children
items.abstract: Importance Atopic dermatitis is a common inflammatory skin condition that is heavily influenced by environmental factors, and while ambient air pollution has been linked to atopic dermatitis outcomes in adults, its effects in children remain more uncertain. Objective To synthesize the evidence examining the associations between ambient air pollutants and atopic dermatitis prevalence in children. Data Sources MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception to February 10, 2026. Study Selection Observational studies of children under 18 years of age that examined the association between at least 1 atopic dermatitis outcome of interest and a pollutant exposure were included. Data Extraction and Synthesis The PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines were used; methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and risk of bias was evaluated using the risk of bias in nonrandomized studies of exposure effects (ROBINS-E) tool. Data were synthesized using random-effects models, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were health care utilization and prevalence, incidence, or severity of atopic dermatitis in relation to predefined ambient air pollutant exposures, including nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ), particulate matter with a diameter of 10 µm or less (PM 10 ), particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 µm or less (PM 2.5 ), ozone (O 3 ), carbon monoxide (CO), and traffic-related pollution. Results Of 2528 citations, 52 observational studies met the inclusion criteria and were included. It was found that every 10-µg/m 3 increase in NO 2 (odds ratio [OR], 3.46; 95% CI, 1.06-11.31; moderate certainty) and SO 2 (OR, 3.96; 95% CI, 1.00-15.65; moderate certainty) was probably associated with increased atopic dermatitis outpatient visits. It was also found that every 10-µg/m 3 increase in PM 2.5 (OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 1.00-1.08; moderate certainty) and PM 10 (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.06-1.35; moderate certainty) was probably associated with higher atopic dermatitis prevalence. Findings were mixed or did not support associations between air pollutions exposure and incidence or severity of atopic dermatitis. Conclusions and Relevance This systematic review and meta-analysis found that increased levels of certain ambient air pollutants were probably associated with some increased population burden of atopic dermatitis in children.

items.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Accommodations, Behavior Therapy, and Stimulant Medication
items.abstract: Importance Although widely deployed, little is known about the efficacy of academic accommodations for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), alone or in combination of behavior therapy and stimulant medication. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of academic accommodations alone and in combination with behavioral interventions and stimulant medication. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a crossover randomized clinical trial with participants introduced to all conditions. Children with ADHD were enrolled in kindergarten through sixth grade. Academic accommodations were changed daily in a randomized order. Stimulant medication and placebo alternated weekly. The general classroom and enhanced behavior classroom intervention alternated every 2 weeks. The study was conducted in summer treatment program classrooms. For the present study, behavior was evaluated in (1) a classroom period where participants completed independent assignments and (2) a classroom period where participants were taught a lesson, completed small group cooperative tasks related to the lesson, and then took a quiz. Study data were analyzed from March to July 2026. Interventions The single and combined effects of academic accommodations, behavior therapy, and stimulant medication (methylphenidate, 0.3 mg/kg) were evaluated. Academic accommodations were extended time on tasks, frequent breaks during tasks, a low-distraction workspace, and the ability to stand at the desk, compared with a condition without an accommodation. A general classroom setting was compared with a classroom setting with enhanced behavior intervention. Main Outcomes and Measures Main outcomes were classroom rule violations during each of the two, 1-hour class periods, the number of seatwork items completed correctly (ie, academic productivity), and the quiz score. Results Of 306 children screened, 280 were enrolled in the study. A total of 255 children (mean [SD] age, 8.8 [1.6] months; 201 male [79%]) started the intervention, and 235 (84%) completed the study. Compared with placebo, stimulant medication increased effects related to seatwork productivity by 22% (ie, the rate ratio [RR] for this condition indicated that receiving medication compared with placebo multiplied the expected count of problems completed per minute by 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25), and quiz scores were significantly improved by 3.9 points (95% CI, 3.10-4.70 points). Medication and behavioral therapy significantly reduced classroom rule-breaking behavior by 37% (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.60-0.67) and 61% (RR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.37-0.42), respectively. There was no evidence that any of the academic accommodations significantly improved behavior or academic outcomes. No interactions were significant. Conclusions and Relevance Results of this crossover randomized clinical trial question whether school-based academic accommodations for children with ADHD should continue to be emphasized as accommodations were ineffective when used alone or in combination with other ADHD treatments. Results support the continued use of behavioral and pharmacological treatment for ADHD. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05469386

items.title: Cannabidiol for Severe Behavioral Problems in Youths With Intellectual Disability
items.abstract: Importance There is a high level of interest in cannabidiol (CBD) as treatment for severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disabilities. Given the lack of evidence, clinical trials are needed to inform practice. Objective To investigate the efficacy of CBD to reduce severe behavioral problems in children and adolescents with intellectual disability. Design, Setting, and Participants This parallel design, double-blind placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted between May 11, 2021, and May 8, 2025. Participants were children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years with an intellectual disability and severe behavioral problems from 3 children’s hospitals in Australia: The Royal Children’s Hospital in Melbourne, Monash Children’s Hospital in Melbourne, and The Children’s Hospital Westmead in Sydney. Intervention Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive CBD isolate in oil (10 mg/kg/d) or placebo orally for 8 weeks, with a 4-week follow-up period. Main Outcome and Measure The primary outcome was parent-reported score on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist, Irritability (ABC-I) subscale assessed at the end of the 8-week maintenance phase. Results Of 131 participants randomized after exclusion of 1 participant randomized in error, 65 were in the CBD group and 66 were in the placebo group. Overall, mean (SD) age was 11.2 (3.1) years, and 98 participants (74.8%) were male. A total of 110 participants (84.0%) had comorbid autism. Primary outcome data were available for 61 participants in the CBD group and 63 in the placebo group. Mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at baseline were 32.2 (7.3) and 30.0 (6.3) in the CBD and placebo groups, respectively. Intention-to-treat analysis showed similar mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at the end of treatment: 21.7 (11.0) in the CBD group and 19.2 (10.7) in the placebo group (mean difference, 2.4; 95% CI, −1.5 to 6.3). A similar proportion of participants experienced at least 1 adverse event in the CBD group (41 [63.1%]) and the placebo group (40 [60.6%]). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial, CBD was not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in youths with intellectual disability. The results suggest that CBD should not be used to treat severe behavioral problems in this population. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04821856

items.title: Cannabidiol for Disruptive Behavior—The Verdict Is In
Reduced Social Media Use and Change in Internalizing Symptoms Among High-Risk Young Adults
items.abstract: Importance National cohort analyses of the association between reduced social media use and subsequent improvement in internalizing problems among high-risk young adults—ie, those most likely to benefit from intervention—remain limited. Objective To assess whether reduced social media use is associated with improvements in internalizing problems among US young adults with frequent social media use and elevated internalizing problems. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study used data from the Population Assessment of Tobacco and Health Study (2013-2021). Repeated observations were organized into 4 consecutive, overlapping 3-wave intervals, each comprising 3 sequential survey waves ( t , t + 1, and t + 2); for example, interval 1 included waves 1-3, and interval 4 included waves 4-6. Young adults aged 18 to 24 years with elevated internalizing problems (all 4 symptoms) and frequent social media use (several times a day) at wave t were included. Data were analyzed from February to August 2026. Exposures Self-reported social media use frequency at wave t + 1 (nonfrequent [≤once daily] vs frequent [several times daily]). Main Outcomes and Measures Past-year internalizing problems (nonelevated [≤3 symptoms] vs elevated [4 symptoms]) at wave t + 2 via the Global Appraisal of Individual Needs–Short Screener (depression, anxiety, psychological distress, sleep difficulties). Results A total of 3788 person-interval observations (2561 [64.7%] female; aged 18-24 years at baseline) were included. Approximately 14% (n = 540) transitioned to nonfrequent use at t + 1. Reduced use was associated with greater likelihood of nonelevated internalizing symptoms at t + 2 (0.57 vs 0.49; prevalence difference, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.02-0.13; prevalence ratio, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27). Findings were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses, including alternative exposure definitions (weekly or less vs several times daily social media use: prevalence ratio, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.04-1.33), alternative missing-data handling approaches (prevalence ratio, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.04-1.25), design-based analyses (prevalence ratio, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06-1.28), concurrent models (prevalence ratio, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.01-1.26), and alternative outcome definitions using internalizing symptom counts, with non-frequent use associated with fewer symptoms (adjusted incidence rate ratio, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.85-0.96). Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, reduced social media use was associated with subsequent improvement in internalizing symptoms among US young adults with elevated symptoms and frequent use. These findings identify reduced social media use as a potentially modifiable target for prevention and early intervention in this high-risk population.

items.title: School-Based Health Centers and Student Health Care Use, Need, and Health Outcomes
items.abstract: Importance School-based health centers (SBHCs) are health clinics located in schools that provide comprehensive primary medical care at low or no cost to students. SBHCs are well positioned to improve health outcomes and health care use by eliminating transportation and cost barriers and to reduce disparities by primarily serving communities with low household incomes and high health care needs. Objective To determine the association of SBHC access with health, unmet health care need, and health care receipt for high school students in Oregon. Design, Setting, and Participants This cross-sectional study used 10 years of student survey data during 2006 to 2023 linked to information on SBHC access in high schools in Oregon. Participants were students in 11th grade statewide who took the health survey. Using entropy-balanced staggered difference-in-differences regressions, we estimated the association of having an SBHC at a student’s school with their outcomes. Data analysis was performed from July to September 2026. Exposure School-level measure of whether an SBHC was present in a high school in Oregon. Main Outcomes and Measures Three measures of mental health and suicidality, 2 measures of physical health, 2 measures of unmet health care need, and 1 measure of medical care received. Results Among 87 871 students at 180 schools, 43 397 (49.7%) were female, 42 824 (49.0%) were male, and 1157 (1.3%) were another gender. A total of 14 933 students attended a school with an SBHC during the study period. SBHC access was associated with statistically significant improvements in student mental health, with decreases in suicidal thoughts (−2.7 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI, −4.5 to −0.7 pp) and suicide attempts (−1.4 pp; 95% CI, −2.3 to −0.5 pp) and decreases in reports of unmet emotional health care needs (−2.1 pp; 95% CI, −3.8 to −0.6 pp). No other statistically significant associations with SBHC access were observed. Heterogeneous treatment effects by gender, sexual orientation, race and ethnicity, and rurality were observed. Conclusions and Relevance This study found that SBHC access was associated with improved mental health among high school students. There are nearly 4000 SBHCs in the United States, and they are primarily in schools with a high share of students from low-income families. Expanding access to SBHCs may help reduce mental health disparities.

items.title: Literacy Promotion and Child Health: The Role of Reach Out and Read
items.abstract: This Special Article draws on a State of the Art Plenary, Literacy Promotion and Child Health: Reach Out and Read at 37, presented at the 2026 Pediatric Academic Societies meeting, which reviewed the evolution of Reach Out and Read (ROR) as a clinical intervention, a subject of research, and an increasingly incorporated component of pediatric primary care. The ROR model, supported by a national organization, now reaches 4.8 million children and families throughout the United States. Much of this growth has been driven by clinicians seeking to support family relationships, child development, and educational trajectories through primary care, especially for families at social risk. This article is based on 6 brief talks, each identified by theme and speaker, focusing on the original concept and rationale for early literacy promotion in pediatric primary care; ROR as an instrument for social justice in the context of brain development, toxic stress, and resilience; efforts to define critical elements of the intervention and strengthen them through training and engagement of both practicing clinicians and residents; a multistage collaborative research effort centering parent leaders across the ROR network in the design of the CONNECT Survey, a measure of the parent/caregiver-clinician relationship; and the crucial contribution of parent voice. Research on ROR has shown positive effects on parent reading and child vocabulary; more recent research, highlighting parent/caregiver voices, emphasizes the importance of modeling by clinicians and of the relationships between primary care clinicians and families.

items.title: Shared Clinical Decision-Making for Vaccines: Looking Backward and Ahead
Dupilumab in Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Dupilumab is an approved biologic therapy for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE); however, real-world pediatric data remain limited. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of dupilumab in children with EoE enrolled in the international European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN)-funded pEEr registry, with a focus on combined remission, treatment deescalation, and predictors of sustained response. METHODS DU-PED is a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including children with confirmed EoE treated with dupilumab in routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was combined remission at 6 and 12 months, defined as simultaneous clinical (≥75% Pediatric Eosinophilic Esophagitis Symptom Score [PEESS] v2.0 reduction or symptom resolution), endoscopic (EoE Endoscopic Reference Score [EREFS] ≤2), and histologic remission (<15 eos/high-power field [HPF]). Secondary outcomes included longitudinal changes in disease domains, treatment deescalation, predictors of remission, and safety. Multivariable logistic regression and ROC analysis were performed. RESULTS A total of 109 patients from 22 centers were included (median age 16 years; 75% male). Combined remission was achieved in 53% at 6 months and 86% at 12 months. PEESS v2.0, EREFS, and peak eosinophil counts significantly improved over time (P < 0.001). At 12 months, 81% of patients were receiving dupilumab monotherapy, and 94% reduced concomitant EoE-directed therapy. Higher baseline proximal eosinophil density was independently associated with a lower likelihood of sustained combined remission at 12 months (odds ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.96–0.99). Dupilumab was well tolerated, with no treatment discontinuations. CONCLUSIONS In a large international registry-based pediatric cohort, dupilumab achieved high and durable rates of combined remission and enabled substantial treatment simplification, supporting its role as an effective long-term treatment strategy for pediatric EoE.

items.title: Racial and Ethnic Differences in Pediatric Perioperative Cardiac Arrest Survival
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE Perioperative cardiac arrest (POCA) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Disparities in perioperative outcomes have been reported, but whether similar differences exist following pediatric POCA remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in 30-day mortality after pediatric POCA. METHOD Within the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program for Pediatrics (NSQIP-P) registry, we identified 2646 children under 18 who underwent inpatient, noncardiac surgery (2012─2024) and experienced POCA. Race and ethnicity were categorized as Hispanic, non-Hispanic Asian, non-Hispanic Black or African American, non-Hispanic white, or other. Crude and adjusted risk ratios for 30-day mortality following POCA were estimated. RESULTS Among 2646 children with POCA, 47.9% (n = 1268) were non-Hispanic white, 28.2% (n = 745) non-Hispanic Black, 4.0% (n = 106) non-Hispanic Asian, 16.2% (n = 430) Hispanic and 3.7% (n = 97) Other race. Overall, 30-day mortality was 32.9% (871/2646). Mortality was similar across racial or ethnic groups (P = .72). In adjusted analyses, mortality risk did not differ significantly for non-Hispanic Black (adjusted relative risks [aRR] 1.02, P = .80), Hispanic children (aRR 1.06, P = .43), or children of other race (aRR 1.02, P = .88) compared with non-Hispanic white children. Emergent surgery (aRR 1.62, P < .001) and preoperative inotrope use (aRR 1.41, P < .001) were independently associated with increased mortality. CONCLUSION We found no significant racial or ethnic differences in mortality risk following POCA among children undergoing inpatient surgery. Mortality was associated with clinical and perioperative factors, including emergent surgery and preoperative inotrope use. This suggests that efforts to identify drivers of disparities in pediatric postsurgical mortality must look beyond POCA outcomes alone.

items.title: Complications in Pediatric Cancer Patients With Staphylococcus aureus Bloodstream Infection
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (BSIs) can cause significant morbidity in children with cancer. Current guidelines recommend central venous catheter (CVC) removal, though the necessity remains uncertain. We assessed risk factors for complications among affected patients, focusing on impact of CVC removal vs salvage. METHODS This multicenter retrospective study includes pediatric oncology patients with S aureus BSIs from 2005 to 2022. The complication outcome period (72 hours to 6 months after initial positive culture) was divided into short-term (72 hours to 8 days) and late periods (8 days to 6 months). The composite primary outcome included occurrence of at least 1 major complication: recurrent BSIs, deep abscess/myositis, S aureus–related death, exit site infection, meningitis, endocarditis, or osteomyelitis. Multivariable logistic regression with propensity score weighting for CVC removal was performed. RESULTS Among 322 BSI episodes, 90.7% (n = 292/322) had a CVC at presentation; salvage was attempted in 55.5% (n = 162/292). The primary outcome was met in 21.2% (n = 62/292) of episodes with a CVC, more frequently in the CVC salvage (25.3%, n = 41/161) vs removal (16.2%, n = 21/130) group. CVC salvage was independently associated with the primary outcome (OR, 3.37; 95% CI, 2.08–5.61; P < .01) in short-term (OR, 21.8; 95% CI, 7.09–95.4) and late (OR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.06–3.18) periods. Methicillin resistance, male sex, invasive infection at presentation, implanted ports, sepsis, and persistent blood culture positivity were also independently associated with the primary outcome. CONCLUSIONS CVC removal was associated with fewer short-term and late complications in pediatric cancer patients with S aureus BSIs, supporting recommendations for catheter removal in this population.

items.title: Middle Lobe Displacement Post Lobectomy in a Child With Congenital Pulmonary Airway Malformation
items.abstract: Congenital pulmonary airway malformations (CPAMs) are an important cause of structural lung disease in children and may remain undetected until later childhood. Although surgical resection is well established for symptomatic lesions, the long-term anatomical effects of lobectomy in pediatric patients remain incompletely understood. Postoperative changes in lung mechanics and lobar positioning can result in uncommon airway complications that are often under-recognized and diagnostically challenging. Obstruction of the right middle lobe (RML) bronchus due to postoperative lobar displacement is particularly rare, with reported cases originating from the adult surgical literature. We report a 9-year-old girl with mild persistent asthma who presented with an infected cystic lesion in the right upper lobe consistent with CPAM. She completed antimicrobial therapy and underwent right upper lobectomy, with pathology confirming type 1 CPAM. One month later, she developed a persistent cough refractory to optimized asthma treatment. Chest computed tomography (CT) demonstrated hyperinflation and poor visualization of the right upper and middle lobe bronchial orifices. Bronchoscopy identified RML bronchial obstruction, and fluoroscopy-guided bronchoscopy confirmed superior displacement of the RML with resultant bronchial kinking, likely related to postoperative lobar migration. Endobronchial stenting was unsuccessful, and further surgical intervention was not advised because of the anticipated risks of a second operation. Conservative management was pursued, resulting in modest symptomatic improvement, with the patient remaining clinically stable for 2 years. This case highlights a rare postoperative complication of CPAM resection in a child and emphasizes the need for heightened awareness, multidisciplinary evaluation, and pediatric-focused studies to guide management.

items.title: Penicillin Allergy Delabeling in Children
items.abstract: Nearly 10% of the global population has been labeled as having a penicillin allergy. Of those labeled, about 95% are not truly allergic, yet most do not receive any allergy evaluations. Patients with penicillin allergy labels are more likely to have worse clinical outcomes and incur higher health care costs, largely because they do not receive penicillin and other first-line β-lactam antibiotics for the treatment of infectious diseases. Consequently, the process of evaluating and removing inaccurate penicillin allergy labels—a process known as “delabeling”—has become increasingly supported by a growing body of evidence. Recently, penicillin allergy has garnered substantial public interest with the proposal of federal legislation to include evaluation of penicillin allergy during routine medical visits for Medicare patients. Although this moves delabeling into the generalist purview, most of the emphasis on penicillin allergies and delabeling has been on adult patients. Yet, penicillin allergy is a pressing issue for pediatrics, as most penicillin allergy labels are placed in childhood. Pediatric literature similarly demonstrates negative clinical and public health consequences of inaccurate penicillin allergy labels. Recent guidelines have strongly recommended a proactive effort to identify and delabel inaccurate penicillin allergies in children. To facilitate this process, simple delabeling procedures, such as direct oral challenge with amoxicillin, have been recommended for patients with low-risk allergy status, based on historical reaction verification, because of their safety and accuracy. These advancements are relevant to practicing pediatricians across specialties and practice locations.

items.title: Islamic Fatwa Guiding the Use of Pasteurized Donor Human Milk
items.abstract: Neonatologists noted hesitancy in Minnesota’s Muslim community to use pasteurized donor human milk, even when medically advised for premature and ill babies, due in part to religious concerns about milk kinship. To address these concerns and promote equitable health outcomes, we forged a coalition of partners including the Minnesota Islamic Council, Children’s Minnesota, M Health Fairview/University of Minnesota, Minnesota Milk Bank for Babies, Brighter Health Minnesota, and the Minnesota Breastfeeding Coalition. On Nov 16th, 2023, the Minnesota Islamic Council issued a fatwa, or a religious clarification, encouraging the use of pasteurized donor human milk for babies when a mother’s own milk is not available. The fatwa provides information on the health benefits of human milk for newborns, clarifies Islamic teachings, and encourages the use of donor human milk when indicated. This is believed to be the first fatwa regarding donor milk use in the United States, although there are precedents in other countries. We believe that this landmark decision, along with collaboratively developed patient and family education materials, will help clinicians across the country navigate conversations with Muslim families about pasteurized donor human milk in an empathetic and culturally sensitive manner, while simultaneously improving outcomes for babies and decreasing disparities. This effort also serves as an example to pediatricians interested in addressing specific religious or cultural concerns about an aspect of pediatric care in a community-centered manner.

items.title: Low-Level Pyuria and Antibiotic Prescribing for Suspected Urinary Tract Infection in Children
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE Our objective was to understand the impact of urinalysis results on clinician antibiotic prescribing for pediatric patients evaluated at ambulatory visits. We hypothesized that responses to low pyuria levels contribute disproportionately to overtreatment. METHODS This cross-sectional study combined electronic health record and abstracted symptom data from emergency department and urgent care visits to 4 Northern California settings. We sampled ambulatory visits by patients aged between 2 months and 17 years who underwent urinalysis between January 1, 2022, and December 31, 2023. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess relationships between urinalysis results, clinical covariates including age, and empiric antibiotic initiation. We estimated attributable impact of these relationships on overtreatment for patients in whom urinary tract infection (UTI) was excluded by culture criteria. We similarly estimated impact on treatment for those with culture-confirmed UTI. RESULTS Among 1150 patients with median age 6.3 years, 191 (16.6%) received antibiotics. Low pyuria levels (trace leukocyte esterase, 10-69 white blood cells [WBC]/mm,3 5-10 WBC/high-power field) were associated with antibiotic initiation with adjusted odds ratio 6.62 (95% CI 3.72–11.79) compared with no pyuria. The adjusted attributable fraction (aAF) for overtreatment at this level was 17.0% (95% CI 10.3%-23.2%), with aAF 1.8% (95% CI 1.1%-2.4%) for UTI treatment. Differential impacts on overtreatment and UTI treatment were consistent in age-stratified analyses. CONCLUSIONS To promote selective UTI treatment, clinicians should consider degree of pyuria in context with age, risk factors, symptoms, and other urinalysis results. Health system interventions should be designed to mitigate excess influence of low pyuria levels and promote integrated diagnostic assessments.

items.title: Facial Dysmorphism in Infants Following Combined Prenatal Exposure to Alcohol and Tobacco
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES Alcohol and smoking have well-established teratogenic effects; however, despite their frequent co-use during pregnancy, the combined impact on fetal development remains less understood. Facial dysmorphism is a sensitive marker of embryonic disruption. This study investigated whether concomitant prenatal exposure to alcohol and tobacco exerts synergistic effects on infant facial dysmorphism, facial size, and growth trajectories. METHODS This longitudinal study included 634 infants from a high-risk population in South Africa. Prenatal alcohol and smoking behaviors were assessed using a modified timeline follow-back interview at each visit, capturing frequency and quantity. Three-dimensional facial images were obtained at 1 month and 1 year postnatally. Infants were categorized into 5 exposure groups: control, continuous alcohol only, continuous smoking only, continuous coexposure, and continuous smoking with any alcohol. Group differences were evaluated using anthropometric measurements and dense surface modeling to assess facial dysmorphism, size, and growth trajectories. RESULTS Continuous prenatal coexposure to smoking and alcohol was associated with the greatest facial dysmorphism and reduced facial size compared to controls and single-exposure groups. Effects were largely sex specific, with stronger alterations in girls. Coexposure was also associated with ocular changes, including reduced palpebral fissure length and increased canthal index. Single exposures showed more limited effects, and facial growth trajectories were not significantly influenced by exposure. CONCLUSIONS Combined prenatal exposure to alcohol and tobacco is associated with greater facial dysmorphism than single exposures. These findings highlight the importance of interventions targeting alcohol and smoking cessation during pregnancy to reduce teratogenic risk.

items.title: Increasing Chlamydia/Gonorrhea Screening in Adolescents Across a Multisite Primary Care Network
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE To increase chlamydia and gonorrhea (CT/GC) screening among sexually active female adolescents in a large pediatric primary care network using a multifaceted quality improvement (QI) intervention, with secondary aims to increase male screening and case detection. METHODS From 2021 to 2025, we implemented a sequential QI intervention including Adolescent Health Questionnaire implementation, financial incentives, electronic health record (EHR) best practice advisories, and universal screening protocols across 33 practices. The primary outcome was CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients aged at least 15 years at well visits. Secondary outcomes included male screening rates and case detection rates. We evaluated outcomes using statistical process control and run charts. RESULTS During the study period, 136 241 adolescents aged 15–19 years received care across the network, with monthly well care visits increasing over time (average 1472-1681 visits/month). CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients increased from approximately 25% to 75%, with the most substantial improvements following universal opt-out protocols. Male testing rates similarly increased from approximately 20% to 75%. Monthly chlamydia case counts for female patients increased from approximately 8 cases/month to a peak of approximately 25 cases/month during the highest-volume testing period. For male patients, cases increased from approximately 4 to 16 monthly. Improvements occurred across demographic groups regardless of insurance type, race, or ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS A systematic, EHR-enabled QI intervention significantly improved adolescent CT/GC screening rates while increasing case detection. Universal opt-out screening protocols proved most effective in achieving comprehensive screening and identifying previously undiagnosed infections, demonstrating the clinical value of systematic CT/GC screening in pediatric primary care.

items.title: Parent Perceptions of Australia’s Social Media Minimum Age Law
Human in the Loop Might Not Be Enough: Large Language Model Oversight in Pediatrics
Father-Inclusive Perinatal Obesity Prevention: A Randomized Clinical Trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Although fathers influence early child feeding, growth, and health behaviors, they are rarely included in early life obesity prevention interventions. We hypothesized that the father-inclusive First Heroes program would reduce rapid infant weight gain and improve parental weight-related and health behavior outcomes. METHODS We conducted a randomized controlled trial (2020-2023) in a Massachusetts health care system, enrolling 227 English- or Spanish-speaking mother-father dyads during the second trimester. Dyads were randomized to the First Heroes intervention—three virtual health coaching sessions plus multimedia content from pregnancy through 12 months postpartum—vs safety education control group. Primary outcomes were odds of rapid infant weight gain from birth to 6 and 12 months and infant overweight at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included maternal postpartum weight retention, paternal body mass index (BMI) change, and parent health care and infant-care behaviors. RESULTS Among 194 infants, intervention participants had lower odds of rapid infant weight gain vs control participants at 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.42; 95% CI, 0.19–0.93) and 12 months (aOR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25–0.99); however, there was no difference in odds of infant overweight between groups. Fathers in the intervention vs control group had greater BMI reduction at 6 months postpartum (adjusted difference, −1.08; 95% CI, −2.06 to −0.11). Maternal weight outcomes were not significantly different by randomization group. CONCLUSIONS The First Heroes trial was associated with improvements in rapid infant weight gain, although other primary infant growth outcomes were not significantly different between groups. Future studies should examine strategies to sustain family-based obesity prevention across infancy.

items.title: Engaging Fathers and Mothers to Promote Responsive Feeding and Healthy Infant Growth
Supporting the Health and Well-Being of Youth Aging Out of Foster Care: Policy Statement
items.abstract: This policy statement examines disparities and structural barriers affecting youth aging out of foster care and evaluates existing policy efforts, such as extended foster care and Medicaid expansion, that have expanded access to care but remain constrained by administrative complexity, workforce shortages, and fragmented systems of care. This statement provides policy recommendations to improve outcomes for this population, including centering lived experience in policy development, strengthening collaboration between pediatricians and child welfare systems, expanding access to extended foster care, and enhancing transition planning for health care. Pediatricians play a key role in advocacy and trauma-informed care to support successful transitions to adulthood.

items.title: Advancing Pediatric Workforce Diversity and Culturally Effective Health Care for a Changing US Child Population: Policy Recommendations for Change: Policy Statement
items.abstract: This policy statement provides recommendations on enhancing pediatrician workforce diversity and providing culturally effective health care (CEHC). It highlights the barriers that racism and other biases create in providing culturally effective pediatric care and achieving child health equity. There are 3 interconnected areas needing greater attention: 1) expanding the underrepresented in medicine (URiM) candidate pool through fostering health career aspirations among diverse youth; 2) enhancing recruitment, retention, and leadership development of URiM pediatricians through facilitating health care system change; and 3) advancing CEHC delivery through synergistic efforts addressing care during clinical encounters, ability to access care, and ongoing improvement processes.

items.title: A Community-Engaged Research Partnership to Address Behavioral Health Inequities in ADHD Care
Weight Estimation and Dose Calculation in Resuscitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: CONTEXT The accuracy of instruments to estimate weight and calculate drug doses in children requiring medications during resuscitation is a critical patient safety issue. OBJECTIVE To determine if length-based tapes were superior to other instruments for drug dose calculation or improved the accuracy of weight estimation, time to drug administration, drug dose accuracy, or clinical outcomes during resuscitation. METHODS We systematically reviewed Embase, PubMed, and the Cochrane Library from inception to December 19, 2025. Systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, nonrandomized studies were included. Country, sample size, study design, and results were extracted. RESULTS In the 250 included studies, 9 enrolled children requiring resuscitation. Compared with the Broselow tape, the PAWPER tape (a length-based tape with habitus correction) was superior for time to drug administration, drug dose accuracy, and weight estimation accuracy in all analyses.
