In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72–31.07). Other significant factors included age 3–17 years vs. 0–2 years (aOR, 2.46–2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39–6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05–2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42–2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] –1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24–2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52–1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47–2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use ( p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge. Conclusions: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS –1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

items.title: Utility of Renal Replacement Therapy for Infants With Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support
items.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the association between renal replacement therapy (RRT) use and survival outcomes in infants with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) receiving extracorporeal life support (ECLS). Design: Multicenter retrospective cohort study using the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization database (2011–2020). Propensity score (PS) matching was used to account for pre-ECLS disease severity. Setting: International multicenter ECLS centers. Patients: Infants with CDH requiring ECLS. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Of 2815 infants, 749 infants (26.6%) received RRT. Before matching, +RRT patients had significantly lower survival to discharge (35.5% vs. 60.2%; p < 0.0001). PS matching generated 413 pairs with balanced pre-ECLS characteristics. After matching, +RRT remained associated with significantly lower survival to discharge (36.3% vs. 57.4%; survival odds ratio, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32–0.56; p < 0.0001). +RRT patients also experienced longer median ECLS durations (15 vs. 9.4 d; p < 0.0001) and higher rates of severe on-ECLS AKI (10.9% vs. 3.6%; p < 0.0001). Stratified analysis showed that RRT was associated with significantly worse survival only in patients undergoing on-ECLS CDH repair. Conclusions: In infants with CDH on ECLS, RRT use is strongly associated with increased ECLS duration and decreased survival to discharge. Although PS matching suggests this association persists regardless of baseline severity, RRT likely serves as a marker for significant clinical deterioration during the ECLS course.

items.title: The Current State of Ventilator Liberation Practices and Outcomes in the United States—A Report From the Ventilator Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative
items.abstract: Objectives: Describe and explore interunit baseline ventilator liberation practices and outcomes related to the 2023 Pediatric Ventilator Liberation Guidelines within the original cohort of Ventilation Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative units. Design: Observational cohort study. Setting: Nineteen VentLib4Kids ICUs in the United States (13 general medical/surgical, five cardiovascular, and one mixed). Patients: First planned extubation attempt where code status allowed reintubation in patients younger than 19 years old, endotracheally intubated for any indication between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2024. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: A total of 2315 ventilator courses were included. Most were 28 days to younger than 6 years old (65.5%) and had a lower respiratory infection diagnosis (23.8%). Prematurity (13.2%) was the most common comorbidity. Spontaneous breathing trial exposure demonstrated the highest guideline concordance at 74.6% (median; interunit range [IUR], 49.6–100%), whereas maximal inspiratory pressure testing was lowest (3.7%; IUR, 0–62.4%). Most courses (55.5%; IUR, 19.8–99%) included an air leak test. Among those without an air leak noted or greater than 25 cmH 2 O, 70.1% were exposed to dexamethasone in concordance with the guidelines. Initiation of dexamethasone greater than or equal to 6 hours before extubation predominated (81.1%) at a median dose of 0.5 mg/kg/dose in exposed groups. Planned postextubation high-flow nasal cannula (44.3%) and bilevel positive airway pressure (18.6%) were most common. Unit-level use of any planned postextubation noninvasive respiratory support ranged from 20.6% to 100%. Among infants, planned continuous positive airway pressure was used in 6.7% of subjects. Among all courses, 10.4% (IUR, 4.5–19.2%) ended with extubation failure (reintubation within 48 hr). Conclusions: Baseline VentLib4Kids practices demonstrate varying degrees of concordance with guideline recommendations along with significant interunit variation. These results align with prior international survey data and support the need for structured, multicenter quality improvement and guideline implementation strategies.

items.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury
items.abstract: Objectives: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes. Design: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock. Setting: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025. Patients: Patients 0–18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1–3 on days 1–2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement. Interventions: None. Measurements and Main Results: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0–6] vs. 5 [1–7] T2 vs. 5 [2–7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = –0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients. Conclusions: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

Association between obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes and severity in the Chinese population: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Background: A novel phenotype, uniform obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), has been proposed, but its association with disease severity remains unclear in the Chinese population. This study aims to evaluate the distribution of OSA phenotypes and their association with severity in Chinese individuals. Methods: This single-center cross-sectional study included consecutive patients with OSA [apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5] aged 14–80 years who underwent polysomnography (PSG) between 2019 and 2021. OSA phenotype was treated as a nominal three-category variable, including rapid eye movement (REM)-dependent OSA (REM-OSA), non-REM-dependent OSA (NREM-OSA), and uniform OSA, based on AHI ratios. Severity was classified as mild, moderate, or severe. The distribution of OSA severity across phenotypes was compared using the Pearson chi-square test with Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Multinomial logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with phenotypes. Results: Among the 238 OSA patients [82.4% male; median age 49 years; median body mass index (BMI) 27.1 kg/m²], uniform OSA was the most prevalent (55.9%), followed by REM-OSA (31.9%) and NREM-OSA (12.2%). The distribution of OSA severity differed significantly among phenotypes (χ²=99.040, df =4, P<0.001; Cramér’s V =0.456). REM-OSA predominantly comprised mild-to-moderate disease, whereas uniform OSA predominantly comprised severe disease (73.7%). Multivariable analysis indicated that, compared with severe OSA, mild-to-moderate OSA was associated with higher odds of REM-OSA than uniform OSA. Compared with uniform OSA, higher minimum peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ) was associated with REM-OSA and NREM-OSA, while older age was associated with NREM-OSA. Conclusions: Uniform OSA is highly prevalent and associated with severe disease in this Chinese cohort. These findings highlight the necessity of phenotype-specific screening and individualized management strategies to optimize OSA care.

items.title: Single-center experience with surgical site infection following adult pectus repair
items.abstract: Background: Infections after pectus repair are uncommon but significant due to implanted hardware. Data on surgical site infections (SSIs) after adult pectus repair are limited. This study aimed to quantify the infection rate and identify associated risk factors. Methods: A retrospective review was conducted of consecutive patients undergoing pectus repair (ages 16 and over) by a single surgeon between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025. Patients were stratified into primary minimally invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE) and complex procedures, which included hybrid and revision procedures. SSIs were classified as superficial or deep/organ-space according to the Infectious Diseases Society of America criteria. Both univariable and multivariable Firth regression analyses were performed to evaluate factors associated with infection. Results: In total, 1,364 patients were included (mean age 31.1±10.7 years). There were 1,060 primary MIRPE repairs (77.7%) and 304 complex procedures (22.3%). Infection was significantly less frequent following primary MIRPE than complex procedures (superficial SSI: 3.4% vs. 5.2%; deep/organ-space SSI: 0.75% vs. 2.9%; P<0.001). In the overall cohort, higher odds of postoperative infection were observed among patients undergoing complex procedures [odds ratio (OR) 2.71, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62–4.43; P<0.001], those with a history of smoking (OR 2.21, 95% CI: 1.19–3.89; P=0.01), prolonged operative duration (OR 1.01 per minute, 95% CI: 1.00–1.01; P<0.001), and pleural effusions requiring intervention (OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.99–4.24; P=0.053). Extensive adhesiolysis exceeding 45 minutes demonstrated a strong trend toward increased infection risk (OR 2.13, 95% CI: 0.98–4.17; P=0.057). In the primary MIRPE subgroup, smoking history (OR 2.25, 95% CI: 1.06–4.41; P=0.04) and postoperative intervention for pleural effusion (OR 2.92, 95% CI: 1.31–5.91; P=0.01) were significantly associated with infection, while concurrent breast surgery demonstrated a near-significant association (OR 2.75, 95% CI: 0.97–6.52; P=0.057). Conclusions: The rate of SSIs following adult pectus excavatum (PE) repair was low; however, subgroups experienced higher risks.

items.title: Surgical outcomes and long-term survival of chronic pulmonary aspergillosis: a 13-year single-center experience
items.abstract: Background: In tuberculosis-endemic regions, chronic pulmonary aspergillosis (CPA) remains a challenging surgical entity. The clinical characteristics and surgical outcomes of different CPA phenotypes, the evolving role of video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), and risk factors for major postoperative complications remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to characterize phenotype-specific clinical and surgical outcomes, examine temporal trends in VATS use, and identify factors associated with major postoperative complications and overall survival. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 314 patients who underwent pulmonary resection for CPA between 2013 and 2025. Patients were classified by imaging as simple aspergilloma (SA), Aspergillus nodule (AN), chronic cavitary pulmonary aspergillosis (CCPA), or chronic fibrosing pulmonary aspergillosis (CFPA). Perioperative metrics, major complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III), and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Temporal trends were compared between the early era [2013–2019] and recent era [2020–2025]. Results: Completed VATS utilization increased from 45% in the early era to 73% in the recent era. CCPA and CFPA were associated with longer operative times with greater blood loss (both P<0.001). Major complications occurred in 17% of patients, most frequently in CFPA (21%) and CCPA (20%). Longer operative time, diabetes mellitus, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) were independently associated with major complications. The estimated 10-year OS was 88.7%, with no significant difference among CPA phenotypes. In an original exploratory multivariable model with only 17 deaths, completed VATS was associated with lower observed mortality than primary thoracotomy or VATS-to-thoracotomy conversion [hazard ratio (HR) 0.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.08–0.77; P=0.02]. Conclusions: CPA phenotypes were associated with substantially different surgical complexity and perioperative risk. Completed VATS was associated with better long-term OS, but this observational association should be interpreted cautiously because surgical approach was not randomized and may be confounded by case selection, resection extent, and surgical era. These findings support phenotype-informed perioperative risk assessment and careful selection of minimally invasive surgery rather than a prescriptive surgical algorithm.

items.title: A nomogram based on peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen for predicting disease progression in lung cancer patients
items.abstract: Background: Current polygenic prediction models for lung cancer are complex, costly, and difficult to implement in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited hospitals. There is a lack of low-cost, easily scalable tools for individualized risk stratification of disease progression. We aimed to develop a simple nomogram using only two routinely available clinical variables—the baseline peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen—to predict disease progression in lung cancer patients. Methods: A total of 119 patients with lung cancer who received radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy between January 2025 and January 2026 were retrospectively enrolled. Peripheral blood lymphocyte subsets, including CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, NK cells, and B cells, were measured by flow cytometry before treatment. The CD4/CD8 ratio was calculated. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of disease progression. A simple nomogram based on routinely available variables was constructed and evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: The baseline CD4/CD8 ratio was significantly higher in the disease control (DC) group compared to the progression group (P=0.02). Multivariate analysis revealed that the CD4/CD8 ratio and targeted therapy were independent predictors of disease progression. The nomogram incorporating these two factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.755, with good calibration. DCA demonstrated that the nomogram provided a superior net benefit over individual predictors. Conclusions: The baseline peripheral blood CD4/CD8 ratio was an independent predictor of disease progression in this single-center retrospective cohort. The nomogram integrating the CD4/CD8 ratio and treatment regimen showed good predictive performance; however, external validation is required before it can be recommended for individualized risk stratification in broader clinical settings.

Parsimonious and interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of acute kidney injury in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a multicenter development and validation study
items.abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) frequently complicates acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and increases mortality, yet current risk assessment relies on late functional markers like serum creatinine and urine output. These markers reflect established injury, limiting opportunities for preemptive intervention. Machine learning (ML) approaches may improve early risk stratification, but existing models lack rigorous external validation and clinical interpretability. We therefore aimed to develop and externally validate a parsimonious and interpretable machine learning model for the early prediction of AKI in patients with ARDS using routinely collected clinical variables. Methods: This multicenter retrospective study included 2,477 ARDS patients from five randomized controlled trials (RCTs) for model development and an independent external cohort of 3,357 patients from three additional RCTs and two intensive care unit (ICU) databases [Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU)]. Six ML algorithms used predictors collected during hours 0–24 relative to cohort-specific time zero to predict new-onset AKI during hours 24–72 among patients without AKI at the 24-hour landmark. AKI was defined using only the serum-creatinine components of the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria in both cohorts. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) informed model interpretation and development of a parsimonious 10-feature model. Results: AKI occurred in 686 of 2,477 patients (27.7%) in the development cohort. A parsimonious 10-feature CatBoost model demonstrated good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.823 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.779–0.863] in the internal test set. The difference from the 53-feature counterpart (AUC 0.811) was not statistically significant (paired ΔAUC 0.013, 95% CI: −0.007 to 0.033; DeLong P=0.21). The 10-feature model exceeded the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score (AUC 0.688) and baseline serum creatinine (AUC 0.735; both paired DeLong P<0.001). In the independent external validation cohort, the model's discrimination remained strong with an AUC of 0.767 (95% CI: 0.732–0.802). SHAP analysis identified blood urea nitrogen (BUN), total bilirubin, and urine output as key predictors, revealing clinically relevant non-linear relationships. Conclusions: We developed and externally validated a parsimonious and interpretable 10-feature ML model that predicts AKI in ARDS patients using routinely collected clinical data. By providing early risk stratification through a web-based tool, this model holds the potential to facilitate timely intervention of AKI.

items.title: Machine learning-based prediction of recurrence-free survival after microwave ablation in patients with lung cancer: a retrospective study
items.abstract: Background: Microwave ablation (MWA) is an effective treatment for selected patients with lung cancer; however, reliable tools for predicting recurrence-free survival (RFS) after MWA are lacking. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning models for predicting RFS after MWA. Methods: We retrospectively included patients with lung cancer who underwent MWA at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between January 2013 and January 2023. Structured and unstructured data extracted from electronic medical records were used for model development. Candidate predictors of RFS were identified by univariable Cox regression in the training set. Five models were developed using Cox regression, eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), random survival forest (RSF), gradient boosting machine (GBM), and support vector machine (SVM). Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, the area under the curve (AUC), the concordance index (C-index), and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: A total of 100 patients were included, of whom 46 (46.0%) experienced recurrence. Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the highest C-index in the test set (0.856), with AUCs of 0.933, 0.855, and 0.891 for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year RFS, respectively. Conclusions: The XGBoost model showed good performance in predicting RFS after MWA in patients with lung cancer. Further external validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

items.title: Phenotype-guided individualized interventional bronchoscopy for benign central airway stenosis: a narrative review and proposed treatment algorithm
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Benign central airway stenosis (BCAS) arises from diverse etiologies and complex pathological mechanisms. Despite the availability of numerous interventional bronchoscopic modalities, standardized strategies based on the biophysical characteristics of the stenosis are lacking, and clinical decisions remain heavily experience-dependent. This review aimed to critically appraise the evidence on mainstream interventional techniques and to propose a phenotype-guided treatment framework. Methods: A targeted literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) was performed from database inception to October 2025, limited to English-language publications. Search terms combined disease-specific and intervention-specific keywords. After screening, 51 references were selected. Key Content and Findings: Balloon dilation remains the cornerstone for simple annular cicatricial stenosis, whereas carbon dioxide (CO₂) laser is preferable for dense fibrous rings and argon plasma coagulation (APC) for superficial granulomatous lesions. Silicone stents are preferred when malacia or complex mixed stenosis requires temporary support. Low-temperature plasma and local drug injection are useful adjuncts. We identified that the most critical deficiency of existing studies is the failure to stratify patients by pathological phenotype—cicatricial, granulomatous, cartilaginous malacic, or mixed—rendering their conclusions difficult to generalize. Conclusions: Therapeutic success now depends on matching technique combinations to pathobiological phenotypes rather than on selecting a single "best" modality. We propose an individualized treatment decision framework grounded in precise pre-procedural phenotyping and outline future research directions, including a core outcome set (COS) and phenotype-stratified prospective trials.

items.title: Imaging-guided Biopsy Techniques for Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions: A Bibliometric Study from 1977 to 2026
items.abstract: Background: Imaging-guided biopsy plays a central role in the tissue diagnosis of peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs). This study aims to map the global research landscape, identify dominant contributors, and characterize recently active research themes. Methods: Relevant publications from 1977 to April 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package "bibliometrix" were used for network visualization, cluster analysis, and trend mapping. Results: A total of 1,181 original articles from 48 countries published in 282 journals were analyzed. The annual output accelerated after 2014, peaking at 110 articles in 2025. China, the United States, and Japan led in productivity, while the United States accumulated the highest total citations. Journal of Thoracic Disease was the most prolific journal and Chest accumulated the most citations. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four thematic clusters covering bronchoscopic navigation, percutaneous biopsy and complications, oncologic management, and preoperative localization. Burst analysis revealed that radial endobronchial ultrasound, diagnostic yield, safety, and transthoracic needle biopsy are the most bibliometrically active recent topics. Conclusions: Imaging-guided biopsy research for PPLs has expanded from foundational technique description to additionally encompass navigation-based precision, harmonized outcome reporting, and integrated diagnostic-therapeutic workflows, with bronchoscopic, percutaneous, oncologic, and localization themes persisting concurrently rather than replacing one another. As bibliometric findings describe research activity rather than comparative clinical performance, they offer a hypothesis-generating reference framework for future research rather than evidence of clinical superiority.

items.title: How to manage residual aortic regurgitation at aortic valve-sparing operation: consideration for aortic reclamping
Week-1 blood counts for early risk stratification of grade 3–4 neutropenia during concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage III non-small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: Background: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) frequently causes myelosuppression, and grade 3–4 neutropenia often forces treatment interruption or dose reduction. Risk prediction in this setting has largely relied on pre-treatment information. We examined whether risk could be screened from end-of-week-1 data. Methods: We retrospectively studied 237 patients with stage III NSCLC given platinum-based CCRT at a single institution. The endpoint was grade 3–4 neutropenia [Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v5.0], an absolute neutrophil count nadir below 1,000/µL during weeks 2–6. Risk was estimated by L2-penalized logistic regression on eight variables—five week-1 blood counts, age, sex and the prescribed radiotherapy dose—with performance assessed by internal cross-validation. Neutrophil and monocyte trajectories were compared by paired nadir timing and by the fall from each patient's own baseline. Results: Grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 48 patients (20.3%). The area under the curve was 0.673 (95% confidence interval: 0.593–0.753) with good calibration (slope 0.978, Brier 0.153), exceeding the same model refitted with pre-treatment instead of week-1 blood counts (0.590; DeLong P=0.03). Week-1 neutrophil, platelet and monocyte counts were the strongest predictors, though the neutrophil count read alone discriminated as well (0.688; DeLong P=0.64). The monocyte nadir preceded the neutrophil nadir by a median of 6 days (P<0.001), the monocyte count having already fallen further by week 1 (69% versus 88% of baseline, P<0.001). The upper tertile of predicted risk carried a 31.6% event rate against 14.6% in the lower two tertiles (negative predictive value 0.854), but on decision-curve analysis the confidence bands did not separate the model from both reference strategies at any single threshold. Conclusions: Blood counts at the end of week 1 carry information about the eventual nadir that pre-treatment counts do not, and the monocyte lineage supplies its timing. The landmark model turns this into a calibrated absolute risk rather than better discrimination; its high negative predictive value defines a low-risk group in which reduced monitoring—and with it the burden of repeated blood sampling—could be tested prospectively. External validation is warranted.

Population-based Prevalence of Bronchiectasis in the United States
items.abstract: Background Bronchiectasis is a chronic, heterogeneous lung disease of rising prevalence; however, contemporary epidemiological data are lacking. Furthermore, paediatric prevalence and cystic fibrosis (CF)-related bronchiectasis prevalence are frequently absent from existing literature. Research question What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States? Study design and methods This retrospective, observational study utilised data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart claims database to estimate the age- and sex-standardised prevalence of bronchiectasis in the US in people of all ages and paediatrics (aged Results In the overall population, 94,392 cases of bronchiectasis were identified (median age, 76 years). Five-year prevalence was 221.6 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 220.1-223.1) per 100,000 persons and increased with age. Prevalence was higher among females (274.6 per 100,000 persons), Asians (302.3 per 100,000 persons) and Medicare Advantage enrolees (528.6 per 100,000 persons). In total, 1.4% of the overall population had a diagnosis of cystic fibrosis. Five-year prevalence in the paediatric population (including 465 cases; median age, 12 years) was 11.9 (95% CI: 10.8-13.1) per 100,000 persons. Paediatric prevalence was similar between sexes, higher in Caucasians and higher in those with non-CF-related bronchiectasis than CF-related bronchiectasis. Interpretation This current study reports that bronchiectasis prevalence continues to increase in the US compared with previous studies, with a consistently higher prevalence in females and Asians, and that a lower proportion of individuals have CF-related bronchiectasis compared with non-CF-related bronchiectasis.

items.title: Giving or Taking? Ethical Guidance for Hospital Administrators Involved in Organ Procurement
items.abstract: Organ procurement from unrepresented decedents is legal in the United States, and some states even designate "the hospital administrator" as having the right to authorize donation. However, there is little guidance for an administrator to consult in their effort to make a socially responsible decision. In this case study, we review the arguments in favor of deferring, deciding against, or deciding in favor of authorization. We contend that that there are three reasons involving uncertainty, inequity, and the risk of mistrust that should give an administrator pause in endorsing organ procurement. We ultimately recommend that organ recovery should not be authorized unless there is (1) strong evidence that a diligent search for surrogates has been undertaken, establishing a reasonable amount of certainty that none are forthcoming, and (2) some evidence suggesting that the decedent would favor organ donation.

items.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF. RESEARCH QUESTION: Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence. RESULTS: PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD. INTERPRETATION: These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

items.title: “Bold and necessary experiments:” The redelegation of authority and responsibility to nurses at the origins of cardiac intensive care
items.abstract: Coronary Care Units (CCUs) were at the forefront of the development of intensive care in the 1960s and 1970s. The development of CCUs, and intensive care more broadly, was enabled by the interplay of expanding medical technology and the evolving role of nurses vis-à-vis physicians. This paper examines the history the CCU at New York Hospital, the teaching hospital of Cornell University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, with a particular focus on role of nurses in the unit's success. Drawing from historical archives of New York Hospital and the Cornell University School of Nursing, this paper argues that that nurses were co-creators, alongside physicians, of the NYH CCU, and demonstrates how nurses drew from the NYH CCU experience to expand critical care services at the local and national level, including by advocating for the creation of the NYH medical intensive care unit (MICU), leading a CCU nurse training program to expand regional CCU capability, and contributing expertise to a federally-sponsored national conference on CCUs. A close reading of this history offers lessons and insights as intensive care medicine moves into an uncertain future, chief among them that work of caring for critically ill patients requires the thoughtful integration of new technologies with hands on care.

items.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end. RESULTS: The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change. INTERPRETATION: Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.

items.title: Patient Self-selection of In-Person vs Virtual Pulmonary Rehabilitation
The Impact of Undernutrition on Post-Tuberculosis Lung-Function: A Prospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background Undernutrition is the leading driver of tuberculosis worldwide, yet its effect on the lungs of people who complete treatment is not well defined. Research question Among adults treated for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis, is undernutrition associated with worse post-treatment lung function, radiographic severity, exercise capacity and respiratory quality of life, and does systemic inflammation mediate that association? Study design and methods Adults (≥18 years) with drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis were enrolled at treatment initiation in India. We measured associations of baseline body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and premorbid BMI with spirometry, chest radiograph score, six-minute walk distance and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Plasma IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-6 were measured at baseline and month 2; counterfactual mediation analysis partitioned the effect of undernutrition on lung function into direct and inflammation-mediated components. Results Of 156 participants analyzed, 76 (48.7%) had a ventilatory defect; 52 (33.3%) had airflow obstruction and 31 (19.9%) had restrictive spirometry. Each 1 kg/m 2 higher baseline BMI was associated with lower odds of any ventilatory defect (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90), and BMI below 16 kg/m 2 carried five-fold higher odds than BMI ≥18.5 kg/m 2 (aOR, 5.08; 95% CI, 1.76-16.02). MUAC and premorbid BMI showed similar associations. Lower BMI was associated with restrictive spirometry (aOR, 0.74 per kg/m 2 ; 95% CI, 0.59-0.89) but not airflow obstruction (aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.80-1.03). Undernourished participants had higher baseline IL-6, which mediated 32% (FEV1) and 49% (FVC) of the association with impaired lung function. Interpretation Undernutrition before and at treatment initiation is a potentially modifiable determinant of post-treatment lung impairment, with systemic inflammation mediating part of the effect. Nutritional assessment belongs in routine tuberculosis care, and nutritional support should be tested to prevent lung-function impairment in tuberculosis survivors.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial
items.abstract: Background Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking. Research question In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality? Study design and methods In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay. Results Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009). Interpretation In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings. Clinical trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; https://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02647554.

items.title: From Response to Remission in Adult Severe Asthma
A Young Man With Hypereosinophilia and Pseudochylothorax
items.abstract: Case presentation A 31-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of dry cough, progressive dyspnea, intermittent fever, and unintentional weight loss of 8 kg. He had no wheezing, hemoptysis, chest pain, palpitations, or skin rashes. He did not smoke and reported occasional alcohol intake. One year earlier, he had been diagnosed elsewhere with pleuro-pericardial TB based on an ultrasound showing right-sided pleural effusion, and 2-dimensional echocardiography showed pericardial effusion. Pleural fluid analysis showed a lymphocytic exudative pleural effusion with elevated adenosine deaminase levels (46 IU/mL). The patient received anti-tubercular therapy along with tapering corticosteroids, showing initial clinical improvement. He was employed as a soldier in the army, and his last posting was in northeast India, where he frequently consumed raw crabs pickled in alcohol. There was no other significant environmental history.

items.title: A 63-Year-Old Man With Dyspnea and Loculated Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: Case presentation A 63-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension and end-stage renal disease receiving scheduled hemodialysis via a left upper extremity fistula sought treatment for shortness of breath of 1 to 2 years' duration that worsened acutely for 1 day after missing a hemodialysis session. In addition, the patient reported mild central chest pain without radiation. He otherwise was in his usual state of health and did not report fevers, chills, cough, sputum production, wheezing, abdominal pain, or hemoptysis. He reported history of tobacco use, having smoked one-half a pack of cigarettes for 15 years and quit about 15 years ago.

items.title: Mediastinal Mass With Recurrent Hemorrhagic Pleural Effusion
items.abstract: CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old man was admitted with a 2-year history of recurrent dyspnea and exertional breathlessness, accompanied by intermittent blood-tinged sputum. During this period, he had been hospitalized 7 times at external institutions, where he underwent extensive investigations including fiberoptic bronchoscopy, endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration, mediastinoscopy, thoracoscopy, and CT imaging-guided biopsy of a mediastinal mass. Empirical antituberculosis therapy also was administered, but no definitive diagnosis was established.

items.title: Persistent Severe OSA Despite Ongoing CPAP Therapy
items.abstract: Case Presentation A 51-year-old man was referred to our sleep medicine clinic for reevaluation of previously diagnosed OSA. The diagnosis had been established approximately 4 years earlier, at a body weight of 105 kg (BMI, 31.7 kg/m 2 ). At that time, cardiorespiratory polygraphy documented severe OSA, with an apnea-hypopnea index of 97 events/h. Mean nocturnal oxygen saturation (Spo 2 ) was 91%, and the cumulative time spent with Spo 2 < 90% accounted for 38% of the total recording time, indicating a substantial nocturnal hypoxemic burden. Nocturnal CPAP therapy had been prescribed, delivered through an oronasal mask at a fixed pressure of 11 cm H 2 O.

items.abstract: Case presentation A 64-year-old man who underwent bilateral orthotopic lung transplant for emphysema related to α1-antitrypsin deficiency 8 months ago presented to the clinic for assessment of bilateral pulmonary nodules identified on routine postlung transplant surveillance without any symptomatic concerns. The donor was positive for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus, and the recipient was negative for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus. He denied any fever, chills, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, weight loss, or night sweats. The patient lived in South Florida with no recent travel history outside the United States or infectious contacts. His posttransplant course was complicated with antibody-mediated rejection at 1.5 months after lung transplant. Antibody-mediated rejection was successfully treated with our institutional multimodal regimen, including a combination of plasmapheresis, carfilzomib, and anti-thymocyte globulin followed by monthly IV immunoglobulin and tocilizumab injections. Also, because of calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-related renal dysfunction, the patient's immunosuppression was converted to a belatacept-based CNI-sparing regimen in addition to prednisone, with a tacrolimus goal trough of 4 to 6 ng/mL. He was also placed on mycophenolic acid, which was soon held because of neutropenia.

Associations between temperatures, extreme temperature events, and onset of acute exacerbations of COPD: a time-stratified case-crossover study in China
items.abstract: Background Non-optimal temperatures and extreme temperature events may trigger acute exacerbations of COPD (AECOPD), but most evidence is admission based, potentially misclassifying exposure timing and obscuring susceptible groups. Research question Are non-optimal temperature and extreme temperature events associated with AECOPD onset, and which patients are most susceptible? Study design and methods We used the Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Registry (ACURE) data and assigned residential temperature exposure using ERA5-Land, a reanalysis dataset of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Cold spells (CS) were defined as consecutive days below location-specific low-temperature thresholds, and compound cold spells (CCS) as concurrent daytime and nighttime cold spells. Associations with reported symptom onset were estimated using a time-stratified case-crossover design, conditional logistic regression with distributed lag nonlinear models. Subgroup and cytokine analyses assessed susceptibility and inflammation. Results Among 5,634 patients with AECOPD (mean age, 69.4 ± 9.5 years; 78.8% male), lower temperature was associated with higher odds of AECOPD onset, whereas higher temperature was not. The strongest associations occurred for CS lasting ≥3 days and CCS lasting ≥2 days over lag 0-3 days, with ORs of 1.84 (95% CI, 1.22-2.78) and 4.31 (95% CI, 2.07-8.97), respectively. Nearly half had delayed admission within 14 days. Using admission rather than onset dates attenuated estimates by 88.8% for CS and 84.8% for CCS. Associations were stronger among older adults, men, smokers, patients with severe AECOPD in the past year or previously diagnosed COPD, and those using combination inhaler in the preceding year. CS were also associated with higher TNF-α, IL-6, and CXCL-11 concentrations. Interpretation Lower temperature and extreme cold events, particularly CCS, were associated with AECOPD onset. Symptom-onset timing may better capture temperature-related associations than admission timing. These findings highlight the need for targeted cold-weather prevention strategies to reduce AECOPD burden. Trial registry ClinicalTrials.gov; NO.: NCT02657525.

items.title: Pragmatic Clinical Indicators of TB Transmission Risk
items.abstract: Background Interrupting TB transmission is a priority in high-burden settings. Identifying highly infectious people with TB may guide targeted interventions. Research question Can readily available clinical characteristics (eg, lung cavitation, cough duration, modified Bandim TB score) indicate the transmission risk in participants with TB? Study design and methods We conducted an observational cohort study in Lima, Peru, enrolling 4,500 index participants. Of the 4,044 people with microbiologically confirmed TB, 3,109 had at least 1 household contact (HHC), yielding 12,767 HHCs. Index participants underwent chest radiograph and TB symptom assessment, from which we derived a modified Bandim TB score. We assessed HHCs for TB infection at baseline and 6 months, and for incident TB disease over 12 months. We analyzed associations between index participant indicators and TB outcomes in HHCs using modified Poisson regression with generalized estimating equations, adjusting for relevant covariates. Results Among child HHCs, baseline TB infection risk increased with greater cavitary extent (adjusted trend P = .005) and longer cough duration (adjusted trend P = .002), with similar trends at 6 months. Among cavitation categories, multiple-quadrant involvement was associated with the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.10-2.39), but not with incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.56-2.60). Among cough duration categories, ≥ 56 days showed the highest baseline infection risk (adjusted prevalence risk ratio, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.18-2.13), but not incident disease (adjusted cumulative risk ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.85-1.99). The modified Bandim TB score was not associated with transmission risk. Interpretation Our results show that in this large household cohort, cavitary extent on chest radiograph and cough duration in people with TB were associated with increased TB transmission risk and showed dose-response relationships with TB infection. These simple, readily available indicators may help target preventive interventions in high-burden settings; however, associations with incident TB remain uncertain.

items.title: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being
items.abstract: Background Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited. Research question What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD? Study design and methods An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience. Results A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief. Interpretation Findings from this US survey of patients with IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough indicate that, among respondents, chronic cough burden manifests physically, psychologically, and psychosocially. Reports of limited relief from available therapies suggest an unmet need in managing chronic cough in this patient population. Clinical trial registration Not applicable.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus DPP-4 and SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients with Bronchiectasis and Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: Background Bronchiectasis is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited disease-modifying therapies. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, but their impact on bronchiectasis outcomes remains unknown. Research question Is GLP-1RA use, compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i) use, associated with better clinical outcomes in patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes (T2D)? Study design and methods Using the TriNetX global federated research network, we conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1RA therapy between June 1, 2022, and May 30, 2025. We compared clinical outcomes, including all-cause mortality, bronchiectasis exacerbation, acute respiratory failure, and lower respiratory tract infections, with patients receiving DPP-4i) or SGLT2i using propensity score matching to balance baseline characteristics. Results After propensity score matching, 1,029 patients per group were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i cohort, and 2,255 patients per group in the GLP-1RA versus SGLT2i cohort. Compared with DPP-4i, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.43; 95% CI, 0.33-0.56) and reduced risks of acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.46-0.65). Similar benefits were observed compared with SGLT2i for all-cause mortality (HR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.40-0.60), acute respiratory failure (HR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.39-0.55), and lower respiratory tract infection (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.68-0.86). Stratified analyses demonstrated consistent mortality benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups, with particularly pronounced effects in obese patients but there was no statistically significant reduction in bronchiectasis exacerbations. Interpretation Among patients with bronchiectasis and type 2 diabetes, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with significantly lower mortality and reduced respiratory complications compared with DPP-4i or SGLT2i. These findings suggest potential disease-modifying benefits of GLP-1RAs in bronchiectasis beyond glycemic control.

items.title: How I Do It: An Intensivist's guide to RV Failure and Right Ventricular Assist Devices
items.abstract: Right ventricular failure (RVF) is a high-mortality form of cardiogenic shock frequently encountered in critical illness and is often underrecognized due to its heterogeneous presentation. This article presents a physiology-driven, stepwise approach to the diagnosis and management of acute RVF using a longitudinal case in the intensive care unit. We highlight practical bedside tools for recognition, including point-of-care ultrasound and invasive hemodynamics, and review targeted strategies for preload optimization, afterload reduction, and contractility support. Special emphasis is placed on airway management, vasoactive medications, and timely escalation to mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in appropriately selected patients. This bedside "How I Do It" guide is written for intensivists and pulmonary/critical care clinicians and translates advanced hemodynamic and device concepts into practical decision points for acute care management.

items.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in individuals with and without impaired spirometry
items.abstract: Background Cardiovascular disease risk scores likely underestimate risk in individuals with impaired spirometry (airflow obstruction and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)). Research question How do risk scores perform between individuals with impaired and normal spirometry, and can they be improved by adding spirometry and dyspnea? Study design and methods Ten-year incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) ie., myocardial infarction, stroke or death from coronary heart disease, from 7 US population-based cohorts was used for this analysis. The pooled cohorts' equations' (PCE) ability to predict MACE was compared between normal and impaired spirometry. Cox-models adding spirometry, dyspnea to PCE variables were evaluated for improvement in MACE prediction. Results Among 26523 participants, those with impaired (N=7547) compared with normal (N=18932) spirometry had a higher incidence of MACE (14% vs 7%), hazard ratio 95%CI 1.25[1.17,1.34] adjusted for PCE variables. Discrimination using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)95%CI of the PCE for MACE was 0.792[0.780,0.803] vs 0.740[0.724,0.755] in normal vs impaired spirometry. Discrimination of MACE improved slightly by adding to the PCE: dyspnea plus 1)impaired spirometry 0.792[0.783,0.800], 2)PRISm, mild, moderate+ airflow obstruction 0.792[0.783,0.801], 3)FEV 1 %predicted, FEV 1 /FVC splines 0.793[0.784,0.802], compared with PCE variables 0.790[0.781,0.798]. The differences in AUC[95%CI] were: 1)0.002[0.001,0.003]p=0.002, 2)0.002[0.001,0.004]p=0.002, 3)0.003[0.002,0.005]p=0.0005 respectively. Among participants with impaired spirometry, only the model that added FEV 1 %predicted, FEV 1 /FVC continuous and dyspnea to the PCE showed improvement in AUC[95%CI], 0.750[0.735,0.765] vs 0.746[0.730,0.761] for PCE variables, difference of 0.004[0.001,0.008]p=0.008. There were no differences among models in calibration, sensitivity, specificity, overall performance, and after bootstrapping 1000 samples. Interpretation Performance of the PCE was better among individuals with normal vs impaired spirometry, despite the latter having an excess burden of MACE. Adding spirometry and dyspnea to PCE variables showed a small statistically significant improvement in MACE prediction, which may not be meaningful clinically, so other risk factors should be considered.

Can robotic living donor hepatectomy be safely offered to all donors? evidence, experience, and program development
items.abstract: Robotic living donor hepatectomy (R-LDH) aims to improve the safety and experience of healthy donors by combining three-dimensional visualization, wristed instrumentation, precision, and stable ergonomics with the benefits of minimal access. This review article summarizes current evidence and offers a pragmatic approach for centers to transition from open to routine robotic donation. Available evidence from retrospective feasibility series, matched cohorts, multicenter analyses, and registry data suggests that R-LDH may reduce donor morbidity compared to open and some evidence of fewer recipient biliary complications, although current evidence remains heterogeneous and largely non-randomized. Available comparative data, including single-center and international registry analyses, suggest lower morbidity with the robotic approach than with laparoscopy, although these comparisons remain limited and would benefit from confirmation in prospective multicenter studies. Learning-curve studies and prospective series suggest that with standardized technique, simulation, and early proctorship, proficiency appears achievable within a limited number of cases, with reduced complications over time. A center-readiness structure focused on “People” (trained team), “Process” (protocolized pathways with explicit conversion criteria), “Platform” (reliable robot access, ICG, ERAS), and “Proof” (prospective audit and external validation) supports phased adoption from standard to complex anatomy. Persistent barriers include limited robotic platform access, scheduling constraints, heterogeneity in reporting, and incomplete cost data, though shorter hospital stay, less pain, and faster return to normal daily activities may partially or potentially offset procedural costs in high-volume programs. In appropriately prepared centers, routine consideration of R-LDH for eligible donors may represent a reasonable donor-centered strategy. Concrete steps are outlined that surgeons and hospital leaders can undertake to implement R-LDH safely, monitor outcomes, and improve equitable access.

Hospital at home for the acute care of patients with liver disease: a clinical review
items.abstract: Patients with liver disease experience frequent hospitalizations for complications such as hepatic encephalopathy, ascites, infections, and gastrointestinal bleeding, resulting in substantial healthcare utilization and reduced time spent at home. Hospital at Home (HaH) is an increasingly utilized care model that delivers hospital-level acute care in the patient’s home through multidisciplinary care teams, remote monitoring, and home-based diagnostic and therapeutic services. This review summarizes the rationale for considering HaH in liver disease and outlines key program components. We review the existing evidence supporting HaH, including the limited hepatology-specific literature as well as broader data from randomized trials and systematic reviews in related populations. We show early studies in patients with cirrhosis suggest that HaH is feasible and safe in appropriately selected individuals. Furthermore, the broader studies comparing HaH to traditional care have consistently demonstrated comparable or improved clinical and patient-centered outcomes such as mortality, readmission rates, cost of care, patient experience, and caregiver burden. HaH represents a promising patient-centered addition to the continuum of acute care for individuals with advanced liver disease. Broader implementation in hepatology will depend on establishing evidence-based patient selection frameworks, defining disease-specific models of care, and carefully designed studies to better understand the impact of HaH on clinical outcomes, healthcare utilization, equity in access to care as well as patient-reported and caregiver outcomes.

items.title: Living donor–domino liver transplantation for maple syrup urine disease: surgical and metabolic outcomes
items.abstract: This study evaluates the feasibility and safety of combining living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) with domino liver transplantation (DLT) for maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). MSUD causes neurological impairment due to branched-chain amino acid accumulation (BCAA). Liver transplantation restores metabolic homeostasis via branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase (BCKDH) present in the donor graft. MSUD livers can be reused as domino liver grafts (DLG) since enzyme deficiency in DLG is supplied by production in other recipient’s tissues. From October 2012 to September 2025 live donors (LD), MSUD patients and DLG recipients were enrolled for DLT and followed for at least 1 year after transplantation. Plasma BCAA levels in MSUD patients at 3 time points (pretransplantation, early [1–90 d], and late [>90–365 d] posttransplantation) were compared with age-matched pediatric controls without metabolic disorders. Surgical and metabolic outcomes were monitored up to 1-year post-transplantation. Among 32 LDLT for MSUD, 27 (84.4%) grafts were reused. Patient/graft survival was 93.8% for MSUD recipients and 96.3%/85.2% for DLG recipients, respectively. Late hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 3.1% of MSUD patients and 7.4% of DLG recipients. Primary factors for DLG disposal were double arteries and younger MSUD patients, related to small arterial caliber. No increased risk related to DLG donation was demonstrated. Combining LDLT and DLT expands the donor pool for pediatric patients while ensuring safety in MSUD treatment, with microsurgical arterial reconstruction supporting DLG reuse. Higher graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR) was associated with better early metabolic control, but this association was not significant after adjustment for age, suggesting that the apparent contribution of graft size to early metabolic adaptation may be age-related.

Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions
items.firstAuthor: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)
items.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

items.title: MRI-based biomarkers for risk stratification and assessment of treatment response in Metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatotic liver disease
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects up to 38% of the population globally. Liver biopsy, the historical reference standard, is invasive, subject to sampling error and not scalable. MRI-based biomarkers provide non-invasive, quantitative whole liver assessment. MRI proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) is the most accurate noninvasive measure of steatosis (thresholds of 6.4%, 17.4% and 22.1% for grades ≥1, ≥2 and 3), and a ≥30% relative reduction is associated with histologic response. Liver stiffness by magnetic resonance elastography (MRE-LS) is the most accurate imaging biomarker for fibrosis: MRE-LS of 3.1-4.4 kPa corresponds to F2-F3 and ≥5 kPa to cirrhosis, and each 1-kPa increase is associated with a 43% higher risk of hepatic decompensation. Iron-corrected T1 is a sensitive but nonspecific marker of disease activity whose prognostic value requires further study. Composite scores, MAST, MEFIB, and MASH Resolution Index, combine imaging and blood tests for advanced fibrosis diagnosis and response assessment. MRE is cost-effective compared with vibration-controlled transient elastography for detecting advanced fibrosis. Artificial intelligence may broaden access by automating analysis and enabling PDFF from routine MRI. We review the evidence supporting these biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis and regulatory use, and their role in clinical trials and in treatment decisions for approved MASH therapies.

Treatment with elafibranor to normalize alkaline phosphatase in patients with primary biliary cholangitis and incomplete response to ursodeoxycholic acid: Results from the phase III randomized controlled ELSPIRE trial
items.abstract: Background & Aims: Definitions of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) treatment response commonly include alkaline phosphatase (ALP) <1.67× upper limit of normal (ULN). However, ALP >ULN is associated with active disease and reduced transplant-free survival, whereas ALP normalization is associated with better complication-free survival. Elafibranor, a peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-α/δ agonist, has been shown to be effective and well-tolerated as a second-line treatment in patients with PBC and ALP ≥1.67x ULN. We report phase III ELSPIRE trial results, evaluating the effect of one year of elafibranor treatment on ALP normalization (ALP ≤ULN; ≤120 U/L) in patients with PBC and ALP >1–<1.67× ULN after incomplete response/intolerance to ursodeoxycholic acid. Approach & Results: In ELSPIRE, 92 patients were randomized, double-blind, 2:1 to elafibranor 80 mg (n=62) or placebo (n=30) for 52 weeks, stratified by ALP at randomization (>1–≤1.33× ULN vs. >1.33–<1.67× ULN). At Week 52, 85.3% of patients receiving elafibranor achieved the primary endpoint of ALP normalization, versus 23.3% receiving placebo (treatment difference: 62.0%; 95% CI: 44.3, 79.7; p <0.0001). Least squares mean percentage change from baseline in ALP at Week 52 was –36.5% with elafibranor versus –4.2% with placebo ( p <0.0001). A greater proportion of patients receiving elafibranor versus placebo achieved ALP normalization with ≥15% reduction from baseline and complete biochemical response (normal ALP, total bilirubin, transaminases, albumin, and INR). Elafibranor was well tolerated; no new safety signals were observed. Conclusions: These results support elafibranor as second-line treatment with UDCA for patients with PBC and ALP >1–<1.67× ULN, with ALP normalization as an achievable treatment goal.

items.title: AASLD EXPO: Diagnosis and management of hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection
items.abstract: Background: HDV infection represents a rare co-infection or super-infection among persons with HBV infection and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to an increased risk of liver events such as hepatic decompensation and HCC. Methods: The Expert Practice Opinion (EXPO) document was developed by subject matter experts and commissioned by the AASLD Practice Guidelines Committee to provide timely guidance on the screening, diagnosis, and management of HDV infection. Writing group members performed a targeted literature review and generated EXPO statements which were agreed upon by group consensus. Results: All individuals who are HBsAg positive should be tested at least once for HDV infection with HDV antibody. HDV antibody positive individuals should undergo HDV RNA testing to confirm active infection. All individuals with chronic HDV should undergo further evaluation including non-invasive fibrosis testing, preferably with elastography. Lab monitoring and HCC surveillance imaging is suggested every 6 months. All adults with chronic HDV viremia and compensated liver disease should be considered candidates for HDV therapy with bulevirtide for chronic virologic suppression, or alternatively bulevirtide plus peg-IFN alfa-2a for individuals without contraindications to peg-IFN and who desire a finite duration regimen. Considerations for patient selection, treatment regimen, monitoring, assessment of response, and care of patients in special populations are summarized in the document. Conclusions: All HBsAg positive individuals should be screened for HDV. All adults with chronic HDV and compensated liver disease are candidates for HDV therapy. Recent advances in HDV treatment offer hope for meaningful improvement in clinical outcomes.

items.title: ATTEST 2027: A Framework for AI Transparency Tiered by Evidentiary Stakes
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now being used across scientific research workflows, from data extraction and code generation to literature synthesis and manuscript drafting. Scientific journals and professional organizations agree that authors should disclose AI assistance. But disclosure that treats all AI use equally with a single generic declaration reveals little about the nature of AI’s influence on evidence generation. Polishing grammar carries a different risk than extracting outcomes from clinical notes, classifying pathology, or making causal inference. We propose ATTEST ( A I T ransparency T iered by E videntiary St akes), a framework that evaluates AI assistance by its consequences. ATTEST classifies AI use into eight broad categories of functions, each scored at one of four risk tiers (Low, Medium, High, Very High). The framework is operationalized by a declaration checklist that authors complete at submission. Within this tiered system, we propose minimum reporting standards by function, cross-cutting requirements, and obligations for reviewers and editors. The goal is to make AI’s role in evidence generation transparent to readers, reviewers, and editors so they can evaluate the integrity of scientific findings.

items.title: Remote patient management reduces liver-related hospitalizations in patients with acutely decompensated cirrhosis
items.abstract: Background: Patients with decompensated cirrhosis experience frequent hospitalizations, yet evidence supporting remote post-discharge care remains limited. This study assessed the impact of cirrhosis-specific Remote Patient Management (CiRPM) program following hospitalization for acutely decompensated (AD) cirrhosis. Methods: Adults hospitalized for AD cirrhosis were included in a three-cohort observational study comparing CiRPM (2021-2024) with contemporary (C-control) and historical controls (H-control, 2018-2019). CiRPM enabled vital-sign and symptom transmission with 24/7 virtual nursing support. Subgroup analyses were conducted by disease etiology, CLIF-C AD score, and decompensation type. IPTW was used to adjust for confounding, and time-to-event outcomes were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Results: Among 430 patients (156 CiRPM, 152 H-control, 122 C-control), mean age was 59 years, 65% had alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), CLIF-C AD score of 56. CiRPM was associated with lower 90-day liver-related readmissions versus C-control (39% vs. 58%; HR 0.57, p =0.01) and a similar trend versus H-control (39% vs. 52%; HR 0.67, p =0.07). Associations were stronger among patients with CLIF-C AD ≥60 (HR 0.43 vs. H-control, p =0.005; HR 0.51 vs. C-control, p =0.02). Among ALD patients, fewer fluid-related readmissions (OR 0.40 and 0.37; both p <0.001) and recurrent hospitalizations (OR 0.51; p =0.001 and p =0.002) were observed in the CiRPM group. In non-ALD patients, hepatic encephalopathy readmissions were lower (OR 0.29, p =0.004; OR 0.36, p =0.02). Mortality did not differ across groups. Conclusion: CiRPM enrollment was associated with fewer liver-related hospitalizations, particularly among patients with ALD and CLIF-C AD ≥60, supporting targeted remote management as a scalable post-discharge strategy for this high-risk population.
