Positive pressure ventilation in newborns at birth: a systematic review of recipient characteristics and temporal trends
items.abstract: AIM: To synthesise evidence on temporal trends, recipient characteristics and variation in the use of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) at birth. METHODS: This systematic review was registered (CRD42024487025) and followed a condition-context-population framework. Five electronic databases and grey literature were searched to 25 June 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI checklist, and reporting followed PRISMA 2020. RESULTS: Forty-two studies from 34 countries (27 from high-income countries), reporting 269 to 10,696,831 livebirths per study (1984-2024), were included. Heterogeneity in whether continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was distinguished from PPV, interface definitions and eligibility criteria precluded meta-analysis. Fifteen studies included only preterm infants and 19 excluded congenital anomalies. Nine population-based and large multicentre studies that excluded CPAP and included all age groups reported PPV incidence ranging from 3.0% to 8.0%. Rates were much higher among very and extremely preterm infants. Temporal trends suggested increasing PPV incidence overall and via facemask, whereas tracheal-tube PPV was stable or declining. Lower PPV incidence was reported in low-resource and lower-level birthing centres. Few studies reported indications for or timing of PPV initiation, and reported data items were inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: PPV remains common in neonatal resuscitation, with higher use at lower gestational ages and higher-level birthing services. Limited and heterogeneous reporting of indications and PPV timelines constrains interpretation and comparison. Standardised, neonatal Utstein-aligned reporting, including PPV indications and time intervals and separate reporting of airway interfaces and CPAP, is needed. Further population-based studies, particularly in low-and middle-income countries, are warranted.

items.title: Coronary Perfusion Pressure During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation is Associated with Outcomes from Pediatric In-hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.abstract: Background Multiple animal studies and one adult study establish that coronary perfusion pressure (CoPP) during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is associated with survival outcomes, such as return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Yet, CoPP during pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (pIHCA) has not been investigated. We hypothesized that an average CoPP ≥20mmHg during the first 10 minutes of CPR for pIHCA would be associated with higher rates of ROSC. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of the ICU-RESUScitation trial, a cluster randomized, step-wedged trial of a physiology-focused quality improvement bundle in pIHCA. Index CPR events among patients ≥37 weeks corrected gestational age and Results Among 111 included patients, median age was 0.2 years [0.0, 0.6]. Seventy-one (64%) achieved ROSC. Thirty (27%) had CoPP ≥20mmHg. Patients with CoPP ≥20mmHg were more frequently ≥1 year of age and less frequently had congenital heart disease. In adjusted models, average CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with higher rates of ROSC (aRR 1.48 [95%CI 1.12, 1.95]; p=0.005). CoPP Conclusions In this first investigation of CoPP during CPR for pIHCA, CoPP ≥20mmHg was associated with ROSC.

items.title: Cycle-to-Cycle Prediction of Return of Spontaneous Circulation Using End-Tidal Carbon Dioxide Dynamics in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.abstract: Background Prognostication in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) commonly relies on static pre-resuscitation variables, although resuscitation is a rapidly evolving physiologic process. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO 2 ) is continuously available during cardiopulmonary resuscitation, but its sequential information has not been fully used for real-time prediction. We aim to develop and internally validate a cycle-to-cycle time-updated prediction model using sequential EtCO 2 values to estimate the probability of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) in the subsequent 2-minute resuscitation cycle. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult OHCA patients from the NTUH-HYCARD database between 2016 and 2023. Event-level EtCO 2 sequences were extracted from resuscitation records and standardized into 2-minute intervals for up to 30 minutes, consistent with Advanced Cardiac Life Support reassessment cycles. At each prediction time point, the model used EtCO 2 values available from event onset to the current time point, without using future values. A two-layer long short-term memory model estimated the probability of ROSC in the subsequent cycle. Performance was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation at two levels: the event level (one prediction per event) and the cycle level (one prediction per 2-minute cycle). Results The final analysis included 1,651 event-level EtCO 2 sequences from 1,480 patients; 583 events ended with ROSC. At the event level, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.876 (95% CI, 0.863-0.890) and a Brier score of 0.140 (95% CI, 0.131-0.149). When applied to every 2-minute cycle (17,029 prediction points; ROSC prevalence, 3.4%), the AUROC was 0.685 (95% CI, 0.664-0.706), and the model systematically overestimated ROSC probability (Brier score, 0.285; 95% CI, 0.268-0.303). Conclusion Sequential EtCO 2 dynamics showed good event-level discrimination for predicting ROSC in the subsequent cycle. When applied at each cycle, the model retained modest discrimination but overestimated ROSC probability, indicating that recalibration is required before cycle-to-cycle use.

Trends in United States Pediatric In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence and Mortality in a Nationally Representative Sample, 2009–2022
items.abstract: AIM: National estimates of pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) incidence in the United States rely on a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative datasets offer a nationally representative alternative. We estimated nationally representative pediatric IHCA incidence and mortality trends from 2009 through 2022. METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of five triennial editions of the Kids' Inpatient Database (2009-2022), identifying IHCA in children <18 years by ICD-9 (99.60, 99.63) and ICD-10 (5A12012) cardiopulmonary resuscitation procedure codes. Two hospitals with implausible CPR rates were excluded. Survey-weighted incidence per 1,000 hospitalizations and in-hospital mortality among resuscitated children were estimated overall and by neonatal status, complex chronic condition (CCC) status, ZIP-code income quartile, and US Census region. Trends were tested with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression across the full period and, as exploratory analyses, within the ICD-10 era (2016-2022). RESULTS: Observed IHCA incidence was 1.11/1,000 in 2009 and 1.22/1,000 in 2012, decreased to 1.11/1,000 at the ICD-10 transition and increased to 1.35/1,000 by 2022. IHCA incidence in children hospitalized with a CCC rose from 3.26 to 6.60/1,000 (6.2%/year, p<0.001), while incidence without CCC remained low. Incidence varied by socioeconomic status (lowest vs highest income quartile 1.78 vs 1.04/1,000 in 2022). In-hospital mortality ranged from 34.1% (2012) to 40.4% (2019), whereas IHCA deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased 1.7%/year (p<0.001), concentrated among children with a CCC. CONCLUSION: The incidence of pediatric IHCA increased among hospitalizations involving children with CCC and was higher among children who live in lower income areas. In-hospital mortality after CPR was largely stable, whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased among children with CCC. A single hospital's coding practices can materially distort national administrative estimates. What is already known Pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest affects approximately 15,200 children annually in the United States, with this national estimate derived primarily from a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative databases offer nationally representative coverage but rely on procedure codes that are susceptible to misclassification. What this study adds In this nationally representative administrative database sample spanning 2009-2022, this study demonstrated that: 1) the incidence of IHCA among children with complex chronic conditions (CCC) rose steadily and accounted for the substantial majority of events, 2) the overall IHCA incidence was higher among children who live in lower income areas with the gradient worsening over the period evaluated, and 3) in-hospital mortality after CPR increased only slightly (34-40%), whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased more, driven mainly by rising incidence among children with CCC, and 4) CPR coding at a single hospital can substantially distort national administrative estimates.

Out-of-hospital cardiac arrests due to foreign body airway obstruction: A CanROC registry, retrospective cohort study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Foreign body airway obstruction (FBAO) is a treatable cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but North American data are limited. METHODS: Exploratory retrospective cohort study of EMS-treated OHCAs using the Canadian Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium (CanROC) registry (2005-2023), classified as obviously FBAO-related or of no obvious cause (presumed cardiac). Logistic regression compared Utstein characteristics between etiologies and identified factors associated with prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and survival to acute care discharge. RESULTS: Among 105,178 EMS-treated OHCAs, 1,106(1.1%) were obviously FBAO-related. Compared with cases of no obvious cause, obviously FBAO-related cases were older (median 73 vs 68 years, p<0.001), more often witnessed (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.98[5.36-9.25]), more often attended by trained bystanders (aOR 3.30[2.41-4.41]), and less often had a shockable rhythm (aOR 0.11[0.07-0.15]). Obviously FBAO-related cases more often achieved prehospital ROSC (62.7% vs 37.8%; OR 2.77[2.44-3.13]), but survival did not differ (10.6% vs 9.0%,p=0.094). Within the obviously FBAO-related cohort, ROSC was associated with witnessed arrest (aOR 1.66[1.13-2.43]) and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.95 per minute[0.92-0.99]). Survival was associated with younger age (aOR 0.76 per decade[0.61-0.93]), initial shockable rhythm (aOR 4.76[1.55-13.30]), and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.81 per minute[0.66-0.98]). Survival was 18.1% and 0.8% among obviously FBAO-related OHCAs with and without prehospital ROSC, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Obviously FBAO-related OHCAs are uncommon but clinically distinct. ROSC is frequent, yet survival remains low and is associated with early prehospital factors, supporting choking prevention initiatives, bystander training, and rapid EMS response.

items.title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest
items.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images. METHODS: Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy. RESULTS: Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

items.title: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia
items.abstract: AIM: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations. RESULTS: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants. CONCLUSION: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

items.title: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score
items.abstract: Introduction Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA. Methods MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC). Results Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99. Conclusion MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

items.title: RescQTM: One-year implementation and feasibility results of a digitally enabled support pathway for bystanders of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
items.abstract: Background Bystanders to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) are at significant risk of psychological distress, yet no standardised support pathway exists for them in the UK. RescQ™ is a digital-first bystander support pathway embedded within regional prehospital and cardiac arrest care services. Aim To evaluate the feasibility of embedding RescQ™ into routine emergency medical services (EMS) practice leading to appropriate contact with bystanders involved in OHCA. Secondary aims were to describe digital access, demand for liaison officer (LO) support, identification of younger bystanders, and EMS clinician acceptability. Methods Prospective one-year regional service evaluation of RescQ™ across Essex, UK. Bystanders involved in eligible OHCA events were registered by EMS clinicians and provided with immediate access to secure digital resources. Bystanders could self-refer for additional support through LO. Results During the one-year evaluation, 220 of 432 eligible OHCA incidents had at least one bystander identified and the incident entered into the RescQ™ pathway, representing an incident-level capture rate of 50.9%. Across these incidents, 298 bystanders were identified, of whom 260 eligible adults were registered with RescQ™. Of registered adult bystanders, 96.2% accessed the digital resources at least once. Among all identified bystanders, 30/298 (10.1%) were aged under 18 years. Approximately 10% of registered bystanders self-referred for additional personalised LO support. Among 25 EMS clinician survey respondents who had used RescQ TM in clinical practice, ratings indicated acceptability. Conclusion RescQ™ demonstrated the feasibility of identifying and supporting bystanders following OHCA through a digitally enabled pathway, achieving incident-level capture above the pre-specified feasibility threshold and high website access among registered adults. These findings support further multi-region evaluation of implementation, sustainability and scalability across different EMS systems.

items.title: Survival after out of hospital cardiac arrest in relation to AED usage in a multi response system including AED equipped drones
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early defibrillation is a key determinant of survival in out‑of‑hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). In multi-response systems, it remains unclear which responders contribute most to early AED use and survival. This study compared first AED-attaching responders and their association with 30-day survival in a regional multi-response system. METHODS: This registry‑based cohort study included OHCA cases in Västra Götaland Region, Sweden, between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Data were obtained from EMS, dispatch, and registry databases. The primary outcome was 30‑day survival. RESULTS: Among 9,413 OHCAs, EMS attached the first AED in 72% of cases, followed by on-duty first responders (ODFR) (18%), bystanders (6.0%), and community first responders (CFR) (4.5%). EMS attachment decreased from 77% to 67%, whereas CFR involvement increased from 1% to 13%. 30‑day survival was highest when AEDs were attached by bystanders (28%), compared with 9.0% for EMS, 8.7% for ODFR and 8.6% for CFR. Among witnessed OHCAs with an initial shockable rhythm, 30-day survival was highest in bystander-attached cases (62%), compared with 36% for CFR, 32% for ODFR, and 24% for EMS. In the multivariable analysis, bystander AED attachment was associated with higher odds of 30‑day survival compared with EMS (OR 2.25; 95% CI 1.77-2.85). CONCLUSION: In this multi-response system, survival was highest when AEDs were first attached by bystanders and remained higher after adjustment for known prognostic factors. This association likely reflects earlier access to defibrillation. These findings suggest that improving immediate access to defibrillation may have the greatest impact on OHCA outcomes.

items.title: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.abstract: Introduction Early defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet bystander defibrillation remains uncommon despite the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). We investigated whether HeartRunner community first responder activation increased the likelihood of bystander defibrillation and 30-day survival in relation to the distance to the nearest accessible AED. Methods Linking data from the Danish Cardiac Arrest Registry, Danish AED Network, and HeartRunner application, we identified patients with OHCA eligible for HeartRunner activation during 2017-2021. Using street-network distances to the nearest accessible AED, we examined associations between HeartRunner activation, bystander defibrillation, and 30-day survival using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). Results Among 5,753 OHCAs (median age, 74 years; 64% male; 78% in private locations), HeartRunner activation (41%) was associated with higher bystander defibrillation across AED distances (p-interaction = 0.004), with no interaction for 30-day survival (p-interaction = 0.054). Predicted bystander defibrillation with versus without HeartRunner activation was 9.6% vs 5.5% at Q1 (389 m), 10.0% vs 4.3% at median (717 m), and 13.0% vs 4.8% at Q3 (1,183 m). TMLE estimated a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of bystander defibrillation (95% CI, 4.5-7.8; p Conclusion HeartRunner activation attenuated the decline in bystander defibrillation with increasing AED distance following OHCA, without a corresponding distance interaction for 30-day survival. Overall, TMLE supported higher bystander defibrillation and suggested a modest increase in 30-day survival with HeartRunner activation.

Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority. RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

items.title: Management of Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Older Adults — The P in PICOT
TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: , and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

items.abstract: BACKGROUND: messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke — New Directions
items.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

items.title: Lung Hernia with a Chest-Wall Hematoma
Equity in Maternal–Fetal Medicine — Technological Advances and a Potential Path Forward
Early Days, Late Nights
Mass Surveillance with Artificial Intelligence — A New Determinant of Health?
Hyperaldosteronism Remission after Extended Aldosterone Synthase Inhibition

items.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke. RESULTS: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

items.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a)
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo. CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

items.title: Bringing Rapid Reperfusion to More Patients with Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited. METHODS: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge. RESULTS: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

items.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks. RESULTS: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group. CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity. METHODS: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand. RESULTS: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. CONCLUSIONS: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

items.title: A Liver-Targeted CIDEB siRNA in Adults with MASLD
items.abstract: A single dose of an siRNA targeting liver expression of CIDEB was associated with a reduction in liver fat of 58 to 80% at week 36 after treatment in persons with metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease.

items.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

items.title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome). RESULTS: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80). CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

items.title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels. METHODS: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change). RESULTS: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

items.title: Cancer Vaccines — From Treatment to Prevention
Interferon-γ Underlying Thymoma-Associated Immune Dysregulation
items.abstract: In an observational study, thymoma-associated immune dysregulation was characterized by interferon-γ pathway activation. Four patients with severe disease treated with Janus kinase 1/2 inhibitors had clinical and biomarker responses.

items.title: Autoantibodies against Type I Interferons and Death from H7N7 Avian Influenza
Subretinal Gene Therapy in X-Linked Retinoschisis
items.abstract: To the Editor: Liang et al. (June 11 issue) 1 report the results of a study involving 12 pediatric patients with X-linked retinoschisis. Complete closure of the macular schisis cavity was observed in the treated eye of each patient after subretinal injection of a self-complementary AAV8 vector containing a human RS1 transgene (scAAV8-hRS1). Although these results are encouraging, pars plana vitrectomy, posterior vitreous detachment, stripping of the internal limiting membrane, and air tamponade were performed in all the treated eyes before administration of scAAV8-hRS1 (see the Supplementary Appendix of the article). The effects of these surgical manipulations on schisis closure warrant . . .

items.title: Iptacopan in IgA Nephropathy — Final 24-Month Data
items.abstract: To the Editor: IgA nephropathy is the most common chronic glomerulonephritis in children, and its disease burden extends across decades. Barratt et al. (July 30 issue) 1 report final 24-month results from APPLAUSE-IgAN, a trial involving adults. The absence of dedicated data from children drives widespread off-label reliance on broad immunosuppression and its associated growth and metabolic toxic effects. 2 Enrollment of younger children across complement-targeted trials has been incomplete; although IgA nephropathy trials of iptacopan (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06994845 ) and ravulizumab ( NCT07024563 ) are enrolling children as young as 2 years of age, many trials exclude children. The proteinuria-based end points in the . . .

items.title: Perioperative Apalutamide in High-Risk Localized Prostate Cancer
items.abstract: To the Editor: In their report of the PROTEUS (Perioperative Treatment with Erleada United with Surgery) trial, Taplin et al. (Aug. 6 issue) 1 conclude that perioperative treatment with androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) plus apalutamide improved the outcomes of radical prostatectomy in high-risk prostate cancer as compared with ADT plus placebo. Two concerns should temper this conclusion. First, the benefit with respect to metastasis-free survival was fragile. The hazard ratio of 0.80 for distant metastasis or death (P=0.02) was driven by metastasis events detected on prostate-specific membrane antigen positron-emission tomography (PSMA PET); the between-group difference in metastasis-free survival as assessed with conventional . . .

items.title: Case 32-2026: A 50-Year-Old Man with Recurrent Cardiomyopathy
Aspirin Therapy — Enough after Arthroplasty?
Lung Hernia with a Chest-Wall Bulge
Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

items.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
items.abstract: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

items.title: High-Flow Oxygen Therapy with Nasal Cannula
Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma. METHODS: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety. RESULTS: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered. CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68. RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group. CONCLUSIONS: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
items.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

items.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion
items.abstract: Importance Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. Objective To determine if either reduced-dose non–vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. Design, Setting, and Participants This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. Interventions Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. Results The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, −1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, −3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, −0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria ( P &lt; .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. Conclusions and Relevance Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463

items.abstract: Importance Refusal of newborn prophylactic vitamin K has been increasing in the US, placing more infants at risk for vitamin K deficiency bleeding. Objective To describe US trends in nonreceipt of newborn vitamin K and infant bleeding, and to compare risks of bleeding and mortality with concurrent bleeding among infants who did and did not receive newborn intramuscular (IM) vitamin K. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study included infants born at 35 to 43 weeks’ gestation between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, at hospitals and health systems from 50 states contributing to the Epic Cosmos dataset. Exposure Nonreceipt of newborn IM vitamin K. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was bleeding within the first 6 months of life based on International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. Secondary outcomes were bleeding during the birth hospitalization and after discharge, intracranial bleeding, and mortality with concurrent bleeding during the birth hospitalization. Robust Poisson regression was used to estimate relative risks while adjusting for covariates. Results Among 5 240 780 infants, the rate of vitamin K nonreceipt increased from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Between 2017 and 2025, the incidence of bleeding by 6 months increased from 225.3 to 394.0 per 10 000 births in infants who did not receive newborn IM vitamin K, compared with 136.6 to 221.8 per 10 000 in infants who received vitamin K. Infants who did not receive vitamin K had significantly higher risk of bleeding by 6 months than infants who did receive vitamin K (288.0 vs 185.9 per 10 000; adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 1.47; 95% CI, 1.43-1.51). They also had higher risk of intracranial bleeding (33.0 vs 13.2 per 10 000; ARR, 2.43; 95% CI, 2.26-2.62) and mortality with concurrent bleeding during the birth hospitalization (2.9 vs 1.1 per 10 000; ARR, 2.69; 95% CI, 2.09-3.47). Conclusions and Relevance Nonreceipt of vitamin K and infant bleeding incidence have increased in the US, and newborns who did not receive vitamin K were at significantly higher risk of bleeding during their first 6 months.

Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND
items.abstract: Importance It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy. Objective To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease. Design, Setting, and Participants In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle. Intervention ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy. Main Outcomes and Measures All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time. Results Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, −1.0 percentage point [95% CI, −4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, −1.4 percentage points [95% CI, −4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, −0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, −41 to 70 days]). Conclusions and Relevance In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877
